terms.definition: Certification that the borrower does not have an identity-of-interest with the seller of the property and does not have a conflict of interest with any other party to the transaction, including the realtor, lender, contractor, consultant, and/or the appraiser. In addition, certifying that the borrower is not obtaining any source of funds or acting as a 'straw buyer' for another individual, partnership, company, or investment club.

Certification letter completed by all consultants and plan reviewers who are required to sign the following certification after preparing/reviewing the work write-up and cost estimate. The signer certifies that all items requiring correction and that the rehabilitation proposal now meets all HUD requirements for 203(k) Rehabilitation Mortgage Insurance.
Describes the work that needs to be done to bring the house to FHA standards. AKA: 203K Specification of Repairs.
Breakdown of the costs, by line item, associated with the work to be conducted in the rehabilitation of the property.
Provides information required to release funds based on work in place. Must be signed by contractor, borrower and inspector. AKA Form HUD-9746-A
Confirms the final bid amount for the project and the time frame for completion. A contract between the homeowner and the contractor. AKA: 203K Contractor Acknowledgement.
Provides information required to release funds based on work in place. Must be signed by contractor, borrower and inspector.
Determines Maximum amount for 203K Mortgage based on the loan amount; closing costs; sales price (if purchase) and work to be performed. Provided to the Lender. AKA: MMW.
Establishes the terms and conditions of the 203K loan program works and describes the guidelines that will be followed in administering funds.

Applies to all MISMO Products (standards and collateral) issued prior to January 1, 2018. This license is automatically granted when an organization downloads any MISMO Product (MISMO standards or collateral) with an issue date through December 31, 2017.123

Applies to all MISMO Products issued on or after January 1, 2018. The Distributor License is appropriate for organizations that develop technology that incorporates MISMO Products and makes that technology available to customers or external partners

Applies to all MISMO Products issued on or after January 1, 2018. The 2018 End-User License is appropriate for organizations that download MISMO Products or develop technology that incorporates MISMO Products released after December 31, 2017, where the MISMO Products are used for internal company use when the organization does not make the MISMO products available to customers or external partners.

Mortgages which meet the credit underwriting guidelines of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHA, VA or major jumbo purchasers. Those who have credit ratings or other qualification deficiencies would be rated as B, C or D credit.

Refers to security classes (tranches) rated as investment grade for institutional investors; can also include the class rated BBB, as that is considered an investment grade for most regulated institutions;aka senior pieces.
A prime tenant who has the highest credit rating.
American Bankers Association
The intentional relinquishment of claim or title to personal or real estate.
A reduction or elimination of rent payments for a specified period of time, usually granted by the landlord as an inducement to the tenant to enter into or to renew a lease.

A reduction in real property tax granted by a taxing authority as the result of an appeal. In some jurisdictions, tax abatements may also be granted as an inducement for development or to attract or retain job-providing industries.

Ability to Repay (ATR) requires that a lender make a reasonable, good-faith determination before or when consummating a mortgage loan that the consumer has a reasonable ability to repay the loan, considering such factors as the consumer’s income or assets and employment status

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Credit Extended Purpose Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the purpose of the extension of credit exempts the transaction from Regulation Z requirements.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Creditor Organization Type
terms.definition: Specifies the creditor organization type exempts the transaction from Regulation Z Ability-to-Repay requirements.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Creditor Organization Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Ability To Repay Exemption Creditor Organization Type.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Loan Program Type
terms.definition: Specifies the Loan Program that exempts the transaction from Regulation Z Ability-to-Repay requirements.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Loan Program Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Ability To Repay Exemption Loan Program Type.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Reason Type
terms.definition: Specifies the reason that transaction is exempt from Regulation Z Ability-To-Repay requirements.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Exemption Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Ability To Repay Exemption Reason Type.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Interest Rate Debt Expense Ratio Percent
terms.definition: The ratio of all debt payments of the borrowers, including proposed housing expenses, to the qualifying income of the borrowers (back-end ratio) based on the note interest rate.
Specifies the method by which the creditor satisfied Regulation Z Ability-to-Repay requirements.
A value from a MISMO defined list that identifies how a loan is designated under TILA/Regulation Z.

terms.term: Ability To Repay Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Ability to Repay Type.
A unique value that represents a user defined version identifier.
Indicates the room is above grade and can be included in GLA.
When a mortgage is sold for more than its face value because it has an above market interest rate. For example, a $100,000 mortgage may be sold for 101.00, or $101,000.

The part of a Web page that is visible once the page has loaded — normally the top part. This term is pertinent to the electronic mortgage world as E-sign requires the presentation of documents to be compliant with state statutes that govern font, pagination, format etc.
Ownership of property (usually income producing) by a non-occupant who employs others to manage and maintain the property.

The level of property units rented or sold after which price concessions must be made for market demand to continue at current levels. Used to determine the feasibility of new residential or commercial construction.

The rate at which vacant space is either leased or sold to users in the market place. Absorption rate is usually expressed in square feet per year or, in the case of multifamily housing, number of units per year.

A unique number (or alpha-numeric designator) assigned to a land Title Abstract document (i.e.: a sequential collection of documents relating to a specific parcel of land). The boundaries of a parcel of real property is determined from the information contained in the Title Abstract document.
Establishes that the lender will not be responsible for replacing the abstract.
Derived from a Judgment; contains only the details of a court action that relate to fulfilling the court order.
A written history of ownership of a parcel of land, summarizing the material parts of any occurrence affecting title of said land.
Method for computing depreciation by comparing the replacement cost of the improvements to the sales price less land value.
Part of the Economic Recovery Act of 1981, an accounting method which allows for a shorter depreciation period for real property over traditional depreciation methods.
A method of calculating depreciation in which a larger portion of depreciation is charged in early years than in later years.
Indicates that mortgagor participates in some sort of accelerated principal re-payment program which may be administered by a third party.

An option available to Freddie Mac sellers and servicers which allows the lender to decrease the guarantee fee due Freddie Mac in return for shortening the monthly remittance delay by paying principal and interest payments early.
A common provision of a mortgage which allows the holder to demand the entire outstanding mortgage balance due and payable in the event of a breach of the mortgage contract.
When true, indicates that at the time of conveyance, the property meets all acceptable conveyance conditions defined by the agency or investor.
An instruction as to the signing methods that are acceptable for this document. It does not reflect a document instance state.
An offerees consent to enter into a contract and be bound by the terms of the offer.
A document signed by a construction loan borrower stating that all work is complete and of acceptable quality.
A right to ingress and egress from one's property; may be implied or expressed.
Title to property is gained through its addition to the owner's existing real estate and can apply to both land and improvements.
Describes the number of accessory units associated with the structure.
An unplanned, unexpected and undesigned event which occurs suddenly at a definite place. Also see OCCURRENCE.
A portion of the amount paid by a borrower for mortgage insurance that ensures the continuance of mortgage payments in the event of a mortgagor's disability or illness.
A promissory note or other negotiable instrument signed by a third party (accommodation party) guaranteeing the repayment of a loan.

A person who lends his name to guarantee a loan for another by signing a promissory note, bill or other negotiable instrument; the endorser becomes the guarantor of the loan and is therefore responsible for its repayment.
When true, indicates that the fee must be paid back to the lender because the account was terminated before the end of the contracted term.
When true, indicates the user requested an account transcript which contains information about the financial status, penalties, and adjustments. Used on the IRS Form 4506T and 4506-C.
Money owed by a business to suppliers of goods or services. Accounts payable are considered current liabilities on the balance sheet.
Money owed to a business for goods or services provided to customers. Accounts receivable are classified as current assets on the balance sheet, with a contra account for bad debts on receivables.
An accredited credential service provider within the domain of the SISAC.
A build up of land by natural forces, such as wind, waves or the flow of water.

An accounting method under which income and expenses are charged to the periods for which they are applicable, rather than when payment is made or received. In contrast, cash accounting is the method calling for income and expenses to be based on payment being made or received.

A bond on which the interest accrues, but is not paid to the investor during the period of accrual. Instead, the amount accrued is added to the principal balance and is paid at maturity. Also called accretion bonds or Z-bonds.
Interest earned for the period of time elapsed since interest was last paid.

terms.term: ACH ABA Routing and Transit Identifier
terms.definition: The 9 digit routing and transit number for the bank from which the payment is drafted.
The account type from which the payment is drafted.
Dollar amount beyond the normal PITI that is be drafted and applied to the escrow account.
Dollar amount beyond the normal PITI that is be drafted and applied to reduce the principal of the loan.
The number identifying the account from which the payment is drafted.
Identifies the purpose of the account where the payment or refund is drafted.

terms.term: ACH Bank Account Purpose Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for ACH Bank Account Purpose Type.
Establishes a direct debit from a borrowers account for loan or escrow payment. AKA: ACH.
An unstructured name that identifies the name of the account holder from which the ACH payment will be withdrawn.

terms.term: ACH Draft After Due Date Day Count
terms.definition: The number of days past the payment due date that payment drafting is scheduled to occur. Payment due date plus ACH Draft Days after Due Date equals draft date.
A value from a MISMO defined list that indicates how frequently the servicer drafts the scheduled mortgage payment from the account of the borrower.

terms.term: ACH Draft Frequency Type Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the ACH Draft Frequency Type.

terms.term: ACH Draft Frequency Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for ACH Draft Frequency Type.
Identifies who is drafting the payment on the loan.
The date a borrower opted into ACH payments.
When true, indicates that a loan is enrolled in Automatic Clearing House (ACH) payment drafting.
The abbreviated name of the depository institution assigned by the Federal Reserve.
Identifies the date on which automated drafting is scheduled to begin.
The subaccount name for the receiver of the wire.
Indicates if the ACH information is current or pending.
The dollar amount of funds being transferred by the wire.

A formal declaration attached to or part of an instrument, made before a duly authorized officer (usually a notary public) by the person who has executed that instrument, the execution being a free act and deed.

terms.term: Acknowledgment Of Notice Of Right To Cancel
terms.definition: Confirms that a borrower has received and understands the Notice Of Right To Cancel document. Sometimes contained with the Notice Of Right To Cancel document.
A form utilized by the insurance industry for use between an Agency and a Company for Organization, Research and Development.

terms.term: Acquisition And Development Loan (A and D Loan)
terms.definition: A loan for the purchase and preparation of raw land for development. Usually a construction loan or land sale is the source of repayment.

In a HUD/FHA transaction, the price the borrower paid for the property plus any of the following costs: closing, repairs or financing (except discounts in other than a refinance transaction). Does not include prepaid discounts in a purchase transaction, mortgage insurance premiums or similar add-ons.
A document evidencing payment in full of a debt obligation. One example would be a satisfaction of mortgage.
A unit of measure for land, 43,560 square feet.
An event which causes damage by nature such as a flood, earthquake or winds; an occurrence which was not caused by man.
A court action to remove any interest or claim in or title to real property; to remove a cloud on title.
Process in which the Lender notifies the MI Company that the loan has closed and that the MI is requested to be activated.
When true, indicates that the loan is actively in the foreclosure process.
When true, indicates that a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) or Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) was associated with the agency.
When true, indicates that the loan is subject to active litigation.
When true indicates that a loan is currently part of a transfer of servicing rights.
Specifies the date of the document status for an active workout.
Specifies the status of the documentation for an active workout.

terms.term: Active Workout Document Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Active Workout Document Status Type.
Valuation of damaged property which allows for depreciation.
The actual dollar amount of the contribution.

terms.term: Actual HUD Funded Counseling And Education Activities Count
terms.definition: The number of actual HUD funded housing counseling and education activities per category.
The actual dollar amount of the insurance claim.
The actual dollar amount of the insurance proceeds.

terms.term: Actual Rent Per Unit Finished Area Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the rent per finished area unit of measure (e.g. square feet, square meters) determined by dividing the amount of actual rent by the total finished area of the living unit.
The ActualSignatureType contains the actual type of the signature applied to the signature field.
Contains a description of the signature type when the value of Other is used for the ActualSignatureType attribute.
Remittance to investors which requires the servicer to give the investor actual interest (net of servicing fees) and actual principal collected from borrowers.
Based on the value of the property.
Real estate taxes on the assessed value of property.
Compliance with the provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act which establishes minimum requirements for facilities with public access to accommodate physically handicapped persons.
The rehabilitation of old property for a new purpose.

terms.term: Add Mortgage Loss Payee Clause for Each Policy
terms.definition: Process of reviewing that the Lender information is accurately listed as the Mortgage Loss Payee on each of the subject property's insurance policies. The addition of the loss payee clause helps protect the Lender from loss, after closing, in the event the subject property is damaged by a covered event.

The full amount of interest calculated on the original principal for the term of the loan. This interest is added to the original principal, thereby becoming a part of the face amount of the promissory note.

An agreement or list that is added to a contract, agreement or other document such as a letter of intent. FHA and VA require that an addendum be added to or incorporated in a sales contract, if it is written prior to the appraisal.
The income or assets of a person other than the borrower (including the spouse of the borrower) will be used as a basis for loan qualification.

terms.term: Additional Borrower Assets Not Considered Indicator
terms.definition: The income or assets of the borrower's spouse will not be used as a basis for loan qualification, but his or her liabilities must be considered because the borrower resides in a community property state, the security property is located in a community property state, or the borrower is relying on other property located in a community property state as a basis for repayment of the loan.
The monetary amount of a charge, an adjustment, a loss, a recovery, or an advance associated with a loan.
The date of the additional charge being reported to the Investor.
A description of a charge, an adjustment, a loss, a recovery, or an advance associated with a loan.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Additional Charge Type.

terms.term: Additional Client Requested Conditions Comment Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field describing the client requested conditions of the assignment.
When true, indicates that one or more additional client requested value conditions are present in the appraisal report.
A free-form text field describing the additional comparison item.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying an additional comparison item.
The name for the additional data item.
The value for the additional data item.
An individual, business or organization covered by a policy in addition to the named insured.
An additional opinion of value for the subject property for a specific client requested condition.

terms.term: Additional Opinion Of Value Requested Indicator
terms.definition: When true, appraiser is asked for an additional opinion of value commensurate with the Property Valuation Conditional Conclusion requested.
Describes the specific ownership or use of the project.

terms.term: Additional Project Considerations Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Additional Project Considerations Type.

terms.term: Additional Property Analyzed Not Used Text
terms.definition: A free-form text field commenting on the reason the appraiser did not include the property in the Sales Comparison Approach.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents supplemental rental income for a rental property.

terms.term: Additional Rental Income Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Additional Rental Income Type.
The dollar amount a borrower has to pay when a property is underinsured or not insured sufficiently to bring the property back into a livable state.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying the valuation report as assigned by a party other than the appraiser (e.g. Client Reference ID, Agency Case Number).
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the individual or organization which assigned the valuation identifier.

terms.term: Additional Valuation Identifier Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Additional Valuation Identifier Type.
A free-form text field describing the additions made to the structure.
Address information that cannot be contained in the Address Line Text.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains a second additional line of Address information.
A free-form alphanumeric string that describes the apartment or condominium component of a specific address.
When true, indicates that the borrower is a participant in a state sponsored address confidentiality program (ACP).
A collection of values that specify an address format as defined by the USPS Publication 28 Appendix A2 Address Types.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Address Format Type.

terms.term: Address Housing Emerging Risks and Opportunities
terms.definition: The process of addressing housing emerging risks and opportunities.

terms.term: Address Is Not USPS Codable Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the given Address is not formatted according to USPS standards or on the USPS master file.
The address with the address number, pre-directional, street name, post-directional, address unit designators and address unit value.

A free-form alphanumeric string that describes the urbanization component of a specific address. Urbanization denotes an area, sector, or development within a geographic area. Often preceded by "URB" in the address, it is commonly used in urban areas of Puerto Rico, and is an important part of the addressing format, as it describes the location of a given street.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of address.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Address Type.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies a further level of detail for a street address, for example, Suite or Unit. This list is based on the USPS Publication 28 on Postal Addressing Standards.

terms.term: Address Unit Designator Type Other Description
terms.definition: The description of the Address Unit Designator Type when Other is selected as the option from the enumerated list.
The identifier value associated with the Secondary Address Unit Designator. Example: 123, C, B1C, etc.
Indicates that this feature is adequate for normal needs.

A mortgage loan or deed of trust which allows the lender to adjust the interest rate in accordance with a specified index periodically and as agreed to at the inception of the loan. Also called "variable rate mortgages" (VRM).
The original cost of a property, plus the value of any capital expenditures for improvements to the property, minus any depreciation taken.
The fair market value of the property minus reasonable costs associated with the transaction or a cost factor defined by investor guidelines.
A person's total income, as reported on the IRS 1040 tax return form, after allowable contributions, deductions and expenses (alimony).
IRS term for the sales price of a home minus the costs of the sale. Used to calculate capital gains.
The sales price of a comparable property after it has been adjusted to reflect the differences between the comparable property and the subject property.

terms.term: Adjusted Sales Price Per Bedroom Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of a bedroom determined by dividing the adjusted sales price by the total bedrooms in all living units (including any accessory dwelling units).

terms.term: Adjusted Sales Price Per Room Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of a room determined by dividing the adjusted sales price by the number of rooms in a property.

terms.term: Adjusted Sales Price Per Unit Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of a living unit determined by dividing the adjusted sales price by the number of living units (including any accessory dwelling units).
The effective payment due date of the Interest Rate, principal and interest Payment or Service Fee Change.
The index value used to calculate the interest rate percent for this adjustment.
The calculated or pre-determined interest rate percent that will be effective on the Adjustment Change Effective Due Date.

terms.term: Adjustment Change Occurrence Extended Term Months Count
terms.definition: The total number of months after which the loan will mature following an extension. When the term of a loan can be extended rather than increasing the principal and interest payment, this is the new term of the loan including any extension.

terms.term: Adjustment Change Occurrence Pass Through Rate Percent
terms.definition: The new rate, expressed as a percent, at which the Servicer passes through interest on the loan to the investor. It can be computed using either a top-down formula: Loan Interest Rate - Servicing Fee Rate - Excess Yield Rate -Lender Guaranty Fee Rate, or a bottom-up formula: Index Rate + Net (a.k.a. Required) Margin Rate + Investor Guaranty Fee Rate + Yield Excess/Deficit Rate, and then applying any caps that are in effect.
Indicates the reason for the Interest Rate, principal and interest Payment or Service Fee change on an existing mortgage loan.

terms.term: Adjustment Change Occurrence Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture the Adjustment Change Occurrence type if Other is selected.

terms.term: Adjustment Change Principal And Interest Payment Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the principal and interest payment associated with the Adjustment Change Effective Due Date.

terms.term: Adjustment Change Projected Principal Balance Amount
terms.definition: The projected principal balance amortized to the date for which interest rate, principal and interest payment, or convertible calculations were performed.
The recalculated fixed dollar amount that is paid to the servicer by the investor for servicing the mortgage if a service fee percent is not expressed.

terms.term: Adjustment Change Service Fee Rate Percent
terms.definition: The recalculated percentage of interest collected that is paid to the servicer by the investor for servicing the mortgage (gross).
On an adjustable rate mortgage (ARM), the interval of time between changes in the interest rate or monthly payment, typically one, three or five years, depending on the index.
The length of time which dictates interest rate adjustments on an adjustable rate mortgage. A six-month ARM would have an adjustment every six months.

The amount that the interest rate is allowed to increase or decrease at the time of adjustment of an adjustable rate mortgage. A one year adjustable would have an annual cap, since the adjustment period is every year.
Specifies whether the occurrence of the adjustment is the first change or a subsequent change.
The process of setting up and managing fee names, fee amounts and other rules for use in systems.

The cyclical process of receiving principal, interest, taxes and insurance (PITI) payments from borrowers, applying the funds to a loan's financial record and ensuring that these payments are properly reported and disbursed to Investors, Insurers, Tax Agencies and others as appropriate.
The process of calculating and applying loan payoff proceeds and clearing the loan from the servicer's portfolio.
The process of determining rules and assessing fees for early payoff of a loan based on the terms of the mortgage note.
The process of managing and marketing properties obtained through default on behalf of the investor or guarantor. Often an insurer will market a foreclosed property on their own behalf.
An insurance company licensed to do business in a certain jurisdiction (i.e., state).
Accessory Dwelling Unit
In real estate, a partial disbursement of funds under a note. Most often used in connection with construction lending.
A written promise to make an investment at some time in the future if specified conditions are met.
The date the advance was disbursed.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying a check number, wire number or other tracking identifier for the disbursement activity.
When true indicates that the advance amount is not recoverable from another party.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the expected entity that should repay the advance.

terms.term: Advance Recovery Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Advance Recovery Source Type.
The portion of advances that is to be forgiven.
Specifies the type of advance made on the loan by the servicer.
A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Advance Type.
A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Advance Type.
Steps taken by a lender to collect past due mortgage payments. Sometimes these steps lead to foreclosure.

terms.term: Adverse Action Credit Repository Decision Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates credit decision was based in whole or in part on information obtained in a report from a consumer-reporting agency.
The date the determination for adverse action was made.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the source of information that prompted the adverse action determination.

terms.term: Adverse Action Decision Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Adverse Action Decision Source Type.

terms.term: Adverse Action Non Credit Repository Decision Indicator
terms.definition: When true, credit decision was based in whole or part on information obtained from an affiliate or from an outside source other than a consumer-reporting agency.
The date that the adverse action determination notice was sent.
A free-form text field used to describe the account, transaction, or credit for which the borrower applied.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of adverse action that was taken.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Adverse Action Type.
Indicates at least one adverse influence has been noted about the neighborhood.

The right by which someone occupying a piece of land acquires title against the real owner, if the occupant's possession has been actual, continuous, hostile, visible and distinct for a statutory period.
A sworn statement in writing, usually requiring notarization.
Establishes the fact of death but does not contain personally identifiable information.
Establishes the fact that the Note is lost. The Lost Note Affidavit together with a copy of the lost note may be accepted as a note equivalent.

Informs the borrower of any Lender-related businesses (i.e., subsidiaries or affiliates) and borrower options related to using these providers. This document is a part of HUD Regulation X (RESPA/Reg X).

terms.term: Affordable Loan Total Subordinate Financing Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of subordinate financing associated with an affordable loan program.

The number of individual dwelling units related to the property securing the loan or, in the case of an application, proposed to secure the loan that are income-restricted pursuant to Federal, State, or local affordable housing programs.

The property a debtor acquires after the execution of a mortgage or other form of indebtedness that additionally secures the indebtedness. If the mortgage note contains a statement on after-acquired property, it is said to have an "after-acquired" clause.
The cash flow remaining after deduction of an allowance for taxes attributable to that income.
The chronological age measured in years. (i.e. the age of a structure)
Federal or quasi-federal organization involved in mortgage lending, such as Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae.
A unique identifier for the individual appraiser as assigned by the identified government agency.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list which represents the governmental agency for which the appraiser has been approved to conduct the appraisal.

terms.term: Agency Appraiser Identifier Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Agency Appraiser Identifier Type.
Describes the federal, state, or local agency program under which the loan is originated.
Securities issued by government or quasi-government agencies such as Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
One who legally represents another, called a principal, from whom express or implied authority has been derived.
The dollar amount of the gross premium that is retained by the agent issuing policy.

terms.term: Agent Validation Affiliated With Title Company Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the Settlement Agency employing this Settlement Agent has an affiliated relationship with the Title Company.
When true, indicates the Settlement Agent was found in the Title Company database.

terms.term: Agent Validation Authorized For Transaction Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the Settlement Agent is authorized to close the transaction described in the Agent Validation Request message.
An accounting method a servicer uses in conducting an escrow account analysis by computing the sufficiency of escrow account funds by analyzing the account as a whole.
A provision whereby the policyholder agrees to self-assume the payment of claims incurred up to a specific amount or limit, with the insurer paying all claims after such limit is attached.

A provision which limits the maximum liability of an insurer for losses in a given time period (usually 12 months). Policy limits are usually expressed in maximums per accident (or occurrence), with an aggregate for all losses in any one year.
The total amount of principal that has been paid from origination to date over and above the scheduled principal amount.
The accounting method wherein a servicer computes the sufficiency of the escrow funds by analyzing the account as a whole.
An entity that purchases mortgages from financial institutions and then securitizes them into mortgage-backed securities (MBS).

An agreement whereby the coinsurance clause is waived if the insured agrees to carry a specific amount of insurance which represents at least 90% to 100% of total values at risk. Also known as "stated amount coinsurance."

An insurance endorsement used with a policy containing a coinsurance clause. It binds the insurance company to an agreement that the amount of insurance carried under the policy is sufficient to meet the requirements of the coinsurance clause in the policy. Addition of the agreed amount endorsement eliminates the risk of the coinsurance penalty.
A contract for the sale of property in which transfer of title to the buyer is contingent on the fulfillment of certain conditions.

A written document in which the purchaser agrees to buy certain real estate or personal property and the seller agrees to sell under stated conditions. Also called a sales contract, binder or earnest money contract.
The ownership of the right to use, control or occupy the air space over a designated property, without the right to use the land surface.
The space above the surface of land that is owned by the landowner and that may be divided and sold or leased to others.
Confirms that a borrower is aware of presence of airport and possible noise situations. Provided by Borrower.
Also known as

A step-by-step procedure used to solve a problem or accomplish a specific end. It is a sequence of instructions that are followed to perform a computation or solve a class of problems, often involving the repetition of operations.
A value that identifies the algorithm used to calculate digest. For example: http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#sha1
A unique alphanumeric string identifying the account under which credit has been granted to the party using the identified alias (alternate name).
An unstructured name that identifies the grantor of credit to the party using the identified alias (alternate name).
When true indicates that this alias name was used on a tax return.
A description of the type of ALIAS.
A description of an ALIAS type not included in the enumerated list.
The transfer of title to real property from one owner to another.
A type of acceleration clause that demands payment of the entire balance upon sale or other transfer of title; also called a "due-on-sale" clause.
When true, indicates that a borrower has obligations for alimony, child support, etc.
An unstructured name that identifies the person to whom alimony payments are owed by the borrower.
When true, indicates all ownership rights of the property are being included as part of the valuation.
A proposal to purchase property without any contingency to obtain a loan to finance any portion of the purchase price.
The term applied to the total costs of a securitization; usually quoted in basis points to reflect what the costs would have added to yield if they had not been spent on the creation of the security.
A refinancing technique involving the creation of a new deed of trust that includes the balance due on the existing note plus new funds advanced; also known as a wraparound mortgage.
When true, indicates at least one client or household member reported they believe they were a victim of housing discrimination.
When true, indicates at least one client or household member reported they believe they were a victim of predatory mortgage lending.

The portion of the principal amount of a blanket mortgage associated with each individual property. This term is applicable when a number of properties are financed under one blanket mortgage with each property allocated its share of the total mortgage balance.
A method of site valuation in which the appraiser deducts the estimated value of the building from the total sales price of an improved property to arrive at the estimated land value.
A CMBS provision that defines how realized losses will be allocated to certificate holders.
The date the Allonge was executed.

terms.term: Allonge To Note Pay To The Order Of Description
terms.definition: The name of new note holder identified on the Allonge.

terms.term: Allonge To Note Without Recourse Description
terms.definition: Description for Allonge section pertaining to recourse and without recourse typically note holders name and address.

When true, indicates that there is Live/Work space available within the residential unit. A measurement that specifies the allowable space within the residential unit to be used for non-residential purposes. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Area Unit Of Measure Type.

terms.term: Allowance For Vacancy And Income Loss
terms.definition: In accounting, an estimated amount reflecting probable vacancy, nonpayment of rent by tenants and any other income loss. These funds are set aside to cover either expected or unanticipated income losses.

terms.term: ALTA Registry Number Of Confirmations Count

The date that an ALTA Registry Role was recorded in the ALTA Registry.

The date on which an entity in the ALTA Registry was confirmed by an underwriter.
A unique alphanumeric string representing the ALTA Identifier of the confirming underwriter for an agent.

A change to the terms or conditions of a document and/or change in the variable information added to the Record or Electronic Record, after it is signed; or if it is not required to be signed, after it is delivered.
The cost of any alterations, improvements, repairs and rehabilitation that are to be made on the subject property.
Appointed by the Member, the employee who may act for the Voting Representative if that individual is unable to do so.
A program created by Fannie Mae to provide liquidity to the multifamily CMBS market.
Use of bank statements, W-2's and pay stubs to document an applicant's income and assets instead of verification forms mailed by the lender.
A mortgage that differs from the typical mortgage instrument either in the amount of principal, the interest rate, the periodic or monthly payments or terms for repayment.

A measurement that specifies the elevation above sea level where the image was captured. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Linear Unit Of Measure Type.

An evaluation published by the A.M. Best Company of all life, property and casualty insurers (U.S. domiciled and U.S. branches of foreign property insurer groups) which are active in the United States. These ratings are often used by agents, brokers and commercial insurers to determine the suitability, service record and financial stability of insurance companies.

Adds HUD required conditions to the Purchase Agreement. Escape clause allowing a borrower to exit transaction if it does not meet value. These do not have HUD number but are required in Purchase Agreement. AKA: Real Estate Certification.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list which represents the overall rating of the differences between the comparable and the subject for all types of amenities included in the rental agreement.
A feature that enhances property value. Examples are off-street reserved parking within a condominium community, tennis courts, a swimming pool or the proximity of public transportation.
A measurement that specifies the area of the amenity. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Area Unit Of Measure Type.

terms.definition: When true, indicates that the amenity is permanently affixed to the manufactured home.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a high-level category in which the identified amenity is grouped.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Amenity Category Type.
The number of the amenities specified by Amenity Type that are present in the property. For example two fireplaces.
A free-form text field used to describe, in detail, the amenity specified by Amenity Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of material used in construction.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Amenity Material Type.

A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Amenity Ownership Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a particular service, feature or facility available to residents and/or guests of a project or property.
A free-form text field used to describe the amenity if Other is selected as the Amenity Type.

The organization which authorizes industry standards for information management and electronic interchange communication between companies (computer-to-computer). Headquartered in New York City.
Repayment of a mortgage debt with periodic payments of both principal and interest, calculated to retire the obligation at the end of a fixed period of time.
A table showing the amounts of principal and interest due at regular intervals and the unpaid mortgage balance after each payment is made.

The dollar amount of the portion of the total payment amount which is applied to the interest due on the loan as reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.
The interest rate percent of the loan used to calculate the principal and interest or dollar amount of the payment reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.

The dollar amount of a single payment reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.
The due date of a single payment reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.
The number used to identify a single payment within a sequence of payments reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.
The dollar amount of the portion of the payment amount which is applied to the principal due on the loan as reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.

terms.term: Amortization Schedule USDA Annual Fee Payment Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the USDA Annual Fee payment due in addition to the payment amount reflected on the Amortization Schedule for the loan.
A classification or description of a loan or a group of loans generally based on the changeability of the rate or payment over time.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information or a description of the amortization type when Other is selected.
The amount of money, or fair market value of other property, received in a sale or exchange.

terms.term: Amount To Make The Project Operational (AMPO)
terms.definition: An allowance, ordinarily a percentage of the replacement cost, that can be included in the mortgage insured by HUD/FHA to provide a nonprofit sponsor with working capital during the initial period of operation of a project.
The actual amount of the cost of a structural component that is being analyzed as specified by the Analysis Component Type.

terms.term: Analysis Component Actual Total Cost Amount
terms.definition: The actual amount of the total cost of structural components that are being analyzed.
The estimated amount of the cost of a structural component that is being analyzed as specified by the Analysis Component Type.

terms.term: Analysis Component Estimated Total Cost Amount
terms.definition: The estimated amount of the total cost of structural components that are being analyzed.
A collection of values that specify the component, room or structural element being analyzed.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Analysis Component Type.
Process in which the Lender analyzes and reports on delivery performance, including the reason for fallout.
A prime tenant in a shopping center, such as an established department store, which attracts the bulk of customers to the center.

A contract under which HUD makes payments to public housing agencies to cover debt service payments on public housing projects or to provide rent subsidies and administrative costs under the Section 8 Housing Assistance Payments Program.
A yearly HUD/Census Bureau study of housing units and trends in the movement of owners and renters.
A report prepared by the lender or servicing agent for the mortgagor, stating the amount of taxes, insurance and interest that was paid during the year, and the outstanding principal balance.

A term defined in section 106 of the federal Truth in Lending Act (15 USC 1606), which expresses on an annualized basis the charges imposed on the borrower to obtain a loan (defined in the Act as "finance charges"), including interest, discount and other costs.
Periodic fixed payments to be received for a specified period of time or for life, in consideration for prior lump sum or installment payments made to the other party in the annuity contract.
The first day of the first period for which an amount is due as payment under an annuity contract.
Specifies how the loan conditions have been changed for this comparison instance for the purposes of anti steering (safe harbor) regulatory requirements.

terms.term: Anti Steering Comparison Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field which contains the description of the Anti-Steering comparison type when Other is selected as the Anti-Steering Comparison Type.
The date that the lender expects the recordation of the lien documents to be completed given geographical custom.

Sets forth the MISMO policy on complying with Antitrust laws and avoiding the appearance or execution of collective action by Members or Non-Members. The MISMO Antitrust Policy may be found on the footer of mismo.org.
A complete and separate living unit in a building containing at least one other like unit.

terms.definition: A notice from the loan originator to the borrower that the borrower must notify the loan originator of any additional loan debt that the borrower takes on after loan application and before the loan closing.

Fee charged by a lender at the time of loan application. This fee may include the cost of an appraisal, credit report, lock-in fee or other closing costs which are incurred during the process or the fee may be in addition to other charges.
A set of rules or protocols that enables software applications to communicate with each other. APIs act as intermediaries, allowing different programs to exchange data, features, and functionality.
The date the creditor or originator received the application from the borrower for the subject mortgage loan.

terms.definition: The date the Loan Originator signed the loan application.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the method used to take the application.
The process of applying the funds towards payoff of a loan.

terms.term: Applying For Restoration Of VA Entitlement Indicator
terms.definition: When true, allows a borrower who has previously utilized their VA loan entitlement to purchase another home with the VA's guaranty.

A pro-rated division and distribution of prepaid or accrued taxes, prepaid insurance premiums, prepaid rents and other income and expenses. When a property is sold, apportionment is used to distribute or collect funds due from the buyer and seller for income and expenses.
An opinion or estimate of value. Also refers to the process by which a value estimate is obtained.
A coded value defined by the appraisal analysis provider identifying a type of feedback message about the appraisal analysis.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains the feedback message text about the appraisal analysis from the appraisal analysis provider.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the assessed risk score of a property appraisal.

The specific value of the score representing the risk associated with the property appraisal and/or valuation.
Indicates whether the appraisal report is a Certification of Completion of improvements upon which a previous appraisal report is dependent.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the Appraisal Completion Report.
A free-form text field describing how the appraiser determined that the conditions or requirements stated in the original appraisal report have been satisfied.

A unique identifier assigned by a party for all appraisal data delivered to the party for this loan. The party assigning the identifier can be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI associated with a MISMO identifier.
Professional society in Chicago that provides training in valuation of residential and income properties, market analysis and standards of professional practice. Confers the MA and SRA designations.

A Recertification of Value is performed to confirm whether or not the conditions of a prior appraisal have been met. It does not change the effective date of the value opinion. It is often used for the final inspection or completion certificate for a newly constructed home when the original appraisal was done using plans or specs or when the house was partially complete. It is also used when the original appraisal was subject to repairs or alterations to be made to the house. Confirms that the appraised value of a home has not decreased. The use of the document type includes the Fannie Mae 1004D and Freddie Mac 442.
A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent appraiser in accordance with USPAP and in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion.
The effective date of the appraisal report on the subject property.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent appraiser in accordance with USPAP and in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion without a physical inspection and may rely on expert systems and data.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent appraiser in accordance with USPAP and in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion and an exterior-only inspection of the subject property.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent appraiser in accordance with USPAP and in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion and an interior and exterior inspection of the subject property.
Documents the results of a independent evaluation of an appraisal report and is usually conducted from a checklist and is usually focused on completeness and consistency.
Specifies the accuracy of a category of the appraisal review report (e.g. Accurate, NotAccurate, NotApplicable or NotDeveloped).

terms.definition: A free-form text field used to comment and describe the changes in the market value of the property between the original appraisal and the review of the appraisal.

terms.term: Appraisal Review Original Appraised Value Accurate Indicator

Requests an internal review and evaluation of an appraisal.

terms.term: Appraisal Review Value Conclusion Comment Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe or summarize the reasons why the new data supports a different market value than was reported in the original appraisal report.

terms.term: Appraisal Review: Exterior Only Inspection With Value Opinion
terms.definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion and an exterior-only inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

terms.term: Appraisal Review: Exterior Only Without Value Opinion
terms.definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work DOES NOT include the development of a value conclusion and an exterior-only inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

terms.term: Appraisal Review: Interior Exterior Inspection With Value Opinion
terms.definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion and an interior and exterior inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

terms.term: Appraisal Review: Interior Exterior Without Value Opinion
terms.definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work DOES NOT include the development of a value conclusion and an interior and exterior inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

terms.term: Appraisal Review: No Inspection With Value Opinion
terms.definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion however no inspection of the subject property was performed.
A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work DOES NOT include the development of a value conclusion and no inspection of the subject property was performed.
A unique identifier for the individual appraiser as assigned by the federal authority, the Appraisal SubCommittee. Only one identifier per individual.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the approximate ceiling height.

A feature that is included as part of a parcel of property (usually in a condominium) but may not be located in physical proximity to the parcel and is not constructed as an improvement on the parcel.

The simultaneous buying and selling of any securities including mortgages, mortgage-backed securities, or futures contracts in different markets for the purpose of realizing a profit from differences in price.

A document, usually issued by an independent architect, verifying that a certain portion of construction on a project has been completed in accordance with approved plans and specifications. A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of architectural design for detached dwellings, as defined by local markets.

The component delinquent payment amounts that make up the total arrearage amount.

A property or right owned, tangible or intangible, that has monetary value and is capable of providing future benefits to its owner.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the period for which the association charges are assessed.

terms.term: Association Charge Period Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Association Charge Period Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents an amount charged when the property is part of an association (e.g. Homeowners Association, Condominium Association).
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Association Charge Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the existence of, proposal of, or absence of special assessments for the project.
The date the loan becomes assumable.
Indicates whether the loan is assumable by another borrower.
The length of time the loan is assumable in months.
Specifies when the loan assumption is permitted.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Assumability Type.
When true, indicates that the loan has been assumed.
The dollar amount of an existing loan assumed by the borrower.

The act of taking over the previous borrower's obligation of a mortgage note. Assumptions may be advantageous if the terms of the mortgage are advantageous and they are not changed by the lender when the mortgage is assumed.
A written agreement that a property buyer will assume responsibility for the obligations of a mortgage from the builder or original owner.
The date the loan was assumed.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the reason an assumption request was denied.

terms.term: Assumption Denial Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is used for AssumptionDenialReasonType.
The amount paid a lender for the paperwork and processing of records necessary to approve and document a new debtor.
A buyer's acceptance of primary liability for payment of an existing note secured by a mortgage or deed of trust. The seller remains secondarily liable, unless specifically released by the lender.
The date associated with the specified AssumptionStatusType.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the current status of the assumption.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is used for AssumptionStatusType.
Describes escrowed repairs and certifies that escrowed repairs will be completed. Provided by Lender. AKA: Mortgagee's Assurance of Completion.

Public Key Infrastructure term. A process that uses two different but mathematically related keys; one for creating a digital signature or decrypting data, and another key for verifying a Digital Signature or encrypting data. For either key of the Key Pair, it should be computationally infeasible to calculate the complementary key of that pair.

Internal Revenue Service rules restricting leverage opportunities by limiting a taxpayer's deductible losses to the amount one has "at-risk." One is "at-risk" to the extent of cash contributed and amounts borrowed for which one is responsible for payment from personal assets.
In options trading, the point at which the strike price is equal to the market price of the underlying security.
Ability To Repay
The act of taking property by judicial order into the custody of the court as security for payment of a judgment in an impending suit.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of physical attachment, if any, between the dwelling and adjacent dwellings.
The process in which prospective borrower(s) may attend homeownership education and/or counseling.
A label that identifies the person or department to whose attention the mailing is sent.

A borrower's attestation of the damage to the permanent residence in a FEMA major declared disaster area as demonstrated by an insurance report, an inspection report by an independent fee inspector or government agency, or conclusive photographic evidence showing the destruction or damage.
Indicates that the structure has an attic.
A free-form text field used to describe in detail the attic feature.
Specifies the aspect or feature that is present in the attic of the structure.
A free-form text field used to describe the attic feature if Other is selected as the Attic Feature Type.
The name of the firm of the attorney providing the representation.
The type of function the attorney is performing in this instance.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Attorney Function Type.

Confirms that a person is under a Power of Attorney and warrants specifics facts about the person such as: POA has not been revoked, principle has not died, no divorce action has been commenced if spouse of the principle, a guardian or conservator has not been appointed for the Principle.
Indicates that the contact party is approved to act as an attorney in fact.

terms.term: Attorney In Fact Signing Capacity Text
terms.definition: The specific text which describes the signing capacity of the individual acting as attorney-in-fact.
The agent who is granted authorization to perform specific acts on behalf of another.

Addresses trust or other property matters and confirms the legality of the information that is being provided to the lender. This could consist of beneficiary information, assets used as collateral, trustee and revocable nature of trusts. In Some States, Title insurance is provided via an Attorney's Opinion Letter. AKA: Title Opinion, Opinion of Abstract.
A letter acknowledging a new owner as a landlord or a new organization as a loan servicer. Also called Attornment.
A quality or feature regarded as a characteristic or inherent part of a data element.
An implementation of the ability to extend an instance document by using any attribute. To change from Lax to make an redefinition restriction of AttributeExtension attribute group.
A process of linking an Electronic Signature to the individual or legal entity previously authenticated.

The official examination and verification of bookkeeping accounts to prove the accuracy of figures and the adequacy of accounting controls. An audit may be done by public accountants hired for this purpose or by a company's own employees. The latter is called an internal audit.
Chronological and detailed list of critical events and actions.

A process of confirming an identity of an individual or legal entity, either in connection with the creation of a relationship or in connection with the individual's or the legal entity's participation in a transaction.

The unique, identifiable, and unalterable copy of the Transferrable Record (eNote) maintained within the Control environment established by the Controller. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Ability to assign responsibility, ownership or role in order to perform some activity.
Electronic drafting system that debits an authorized bank account and electronically transfers funds scheduled for remittance.
A field of research and a suite of technologies that aim to automate the end-to-end process of applying machine learning to real-world problems.
A unique identifier assigned by the underwriting system to the underwriting case for a specific loan application.
The date and time of the underwriting decision.
The status of the Automated Underwriting Certificate Request.

Confirms results from Desk Top Underwriter, Loan Prospector or other underwriting system, including the loan decision and conditions or stipulations of the approval. AKA: DU Findings, LP Feedback, Feedback Certificate, Findings, Feedback, Findings Report and Underwriting Analysis, AUS Findings.
Specifies the version of the automated underwriting system used to underwrite the loan.
A free-form text description of the automated underwriting process or procedure used on the loan.
The loan approval recommendation determined by the Automated Underwriting system.
A system that retrieves relevant data such as loan application information and borrower credit history to arrive at a computer-generated recommendation for the loan underwriting recommendation.

terms.term: Automated Underwriting System Document Waiver Indicator
terms.definition: When a returned AU system recommendation indicates that some or all of the loan information is not required to be formally documented in the loan submission package, e.g., no requirement to provide a wage statement, tax returns, etc. A loan of this type would not be considered an Alt A product because the borrower is not applying for a limited/reduced documentation loan.
A free-form text field used to describe the message and review rules returned by the AUS scoring the loan submission.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying an AUS feedback message as defined by the AUS owner.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains a feedback message returned by the AUS scoring of the loan submission.
The message and the review rules derived during the loan validation process by the AUS.
The result of the private automated underwriting evaluation system.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the automated underwriting system used to evaluate a loan.

terms.term: Automated Underwriting System Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Automated Underwriting System Type.

terms.term: Automated Underwriting System Used For Final Decision Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the associated Automated Underwriting System Type was used to make the final underwriting decision.

A valuation report from an automated valuation model or system that is not signed by a certified or licensed appraiser and contains both property data and an estimate of value usually quantified by some type of confidence score and value definition.

A valuation report from an automated valuation model or system that is not signed by a certified or licensed appraiser and contains both property data and an estimate of value usually quantified by some type of confidence score, a value definition and some level of condition of property report from a physical inspection.
A payment method in which funds are automatically debited from a borrower's checking or savings account.
A VA program that enables eligible single-family lenders to conduct the processing and closing of VA single-family loan applications without VA's prior review.
An action that enjoins collection efforts from proceeding.
A free-form text field describing the make and model of borrower's vehicle disclosed as asset.
The model year of the borrower's vehicle disclosed as an asset.
The total number of automobiles owned by a borrower.
All funds available or collected including prepayments and servicer advances.
Limited amount of interest payable to certificate holders to the extent of interest accrued on a group/pool of mortgage loans.

A statistic used to estimate the yield on mortgages. Most mortgages written for long terms pay off earlier, either voluntarily or by foreclosure after default. For example, 30-year mortgages have traditionally been considered to have approximately a 12-year average life. Investors base impact of discounts or premiums on the yield of a mortgage on the average life, as opposed to the written term.

An annual percentage rate that is derived from average interest rates, points, and other loan pricing terms currently offered to consumers by a representative sample of creditors for mortgage transactions that have low-risk pricing characteristics. The Federal Reserve Board publishes average prime offer rates for a broad range of types of transactions in a table updated at least weekly. This rate is used in determining Higher Priced Mortgage Loans (HPML).
The return on an investment as calculated by averaging the total cash flows over the years during which the cash flows are received by the investor.
Automated Valuation Model
The name of the AVM preference table applied in this transaction.
A decimal value representing a fraction of one, which represents the estimated probability of an AVM value being within +/- 10% of the market value as of the AVM’s effective date.
The level of the confidence score as expressed as a rating for a given AVM provider.
Indicator that the particular automated valuation model has the ability to generate a confidence level estimate of its results.
The confidence score used by various automated valuation models to indicate the confidence level of the value estimate.
The date the automated valuation was calculated for the subject Property.
Confirms results from an automated property valuation system. AKA: AVM, Automated Value Model.
The upper end of the value range for the subject property resulting from the application of an automated valuation model.
A value from a MISMO list that represents the name of the publisher of the repeat sales index data used in an automated valuation process.

terms.term: AVM Index Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the AVM Index Source Type.
The name of the published index used in the AVM.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for AVM Index Type.
The low end of the value range for the subject property resulting from the application of an automated valuation model.
Specifies the method used by the Automated Valuation system.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Automated Valuation Method Type.
The last update date for the AVM used in this transaction.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the name of the AVM model used to calculate the valuation of the subject property.

terms.term: AVM Model Name Type Other Description
terms.definition: The name of the AVM model used to calculate the valuation of the subject property when Other is selected from the enumerated list.
The type of value computed by the AVM for presentation.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for AVM Outcome Type.
The vendor who provided an AVM evaluation for the subject property.
The AVM computed value of the subject property resulting from the application of an automated valuation model.
An abrupt and extensive erosion of land by a force of water and its subsequent deposit onto the property of another owner.

Architecture Work Group. The AWG manages MISMO engineering disciplines providing overall technical direction and support for all MISMO Products. AWG is responsible to ensure that MISMO Products follow all published MEGs and other established product development guidelines.
A term applied to the classes (tranches) of CMBSs rated "BB" and lower. Also called below investment grade (BIG) by regulated institutional investors.
An escrow set up to facilitate the simultaneous purchase of one property and the sale of another property by the same party.
Transactions involving selling one home and purchasing another on the same day, usually within hours of one another.
The process of taking all data stored on the computer and copying it onto tapes, or another storage medium, so it can be shipped to another location for safekeeping.
A secondary offer to buy property although the first offer has been accepted, useful in case the first offer fails.
Confirms that a company will return to the funding lender the collateral package, the funded value, or mortgage-backed security value of a property.
A report of the financial position of a business at a specific point in time, showing its assets, liabilities and owner's equity.
Informs borrower of what will happen when lender is instructed to pay off debt on behalf of a borrower directly from a Home Equity account
When true, indicates refinancing of the balloon mortgage loan is guaranteed by the lender.
When true, indicates that a final balloon payment is required to fully pay off the loan.

A mortgage with periodic installments of principal and interest that do not fully amortize the loan. The balance of the mortgage is due in a lump sum at a specified date, usually at the end of the term.

A mortgage with periodic installments of principal and interest that do not fully amortize the loan. The balance of the mortgage is due in a lump sum at a specified date, usually at the end of the term.
A scheduled payment on a mortgage that is larger than other, periodic payments, usually the unamortized final payment.
The dollar amount of the final, or lump sum, balloon payment.
The largest scheduled lump sum payment over the life of loan. This applies when there are scheduled lump sum payments that are more than twice as large as the average of earlier scheduled payments.
The smallest scheduled lump sum payment over the life of loan. This applies when there are scheduled lump sum payments that are more than twice as large as the average of earlier scheduled payments.

Informs the borrower that rate and payment amount may change when the refinance option is chosen for balloon loans and describes how the interest rate and payments are determined. AKA: Convertible Balloon Disclosure.
The date the balloon loan was reset to the current market rate for the remainder of the amortization period.
When true, indicates that the balloon loan has been reset to the current market rate.
When true, indicates the balloon loan has an option to reset.
The risk that a borrower is unable to make a balloon payment at maturity.
An approach to developing a capitalization rate by creating a weighted average rate reflecting the percentage of value represented by each debt and ownership position.

This is generally used to describe a network connection's information-carrying capacity. It can refer to phone or computer networks, radio frequency signals and even monitors. The more bandwidth, the more users it can support and the more data those users can transmit and receive. Bandwidth is often measured in cycles per second, or hertz (Hz), which is the difference between the lowest and highest frequencies transmitted. But it's also common to use bits or bytes per second. A full page of pure text is about 16,000 bits, and a fast modem can move about 56,000 bits per second.
Provides written evidence of a deposit to a financial institution.
A corporation that owns a controlling interest in one or more banks.
Members are primarily commercial banks.
Describes transactions recorded and account balances of the accounts of a customer during a specified period. AKA: Account Statement.

terms.term: Bankruptcies In Last Three Years Count
terms.definition: The number of times the borrower or guarantor filed for bankruptcy within the last three years.

Court proceedings to relieve the debts of an individual or business unable to pay its creditors. An individual, firm or corporation who, through a court proceeding, is relieved from the payment of all debts. Bankruptcy may be declared under one of several chapters of the federal bankruptcy code: Chapter 7, which covers liquidation of individual or business assets; Chapter 11, which covers reorganization of bankrupt businesses; Chapter 12, which covers certain farm bankruptcies; and Chapter 13, which covers workouts of debts by individuals.
The date associated with the specified Bankruptcy Action Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies an action or step taken in the bankruptcy process.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Bankruptcy Action Type.
The percentage of the debt paid by the consumer. This amount is negotiated and assigned by the courts.
The amount of the defendants declared assets at the time of bankruptcy.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that indicates the type of instructions from the servicer to the bankruptcy attorney on the portion of the bankruptcy proceedings the attorney is to complete on the servicer's behalf.

terms.term: Bankruptcy Attorney Service Referral Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Bankruptcy Attorney Service Referral Type.
The date by which proofs of claim must be filed in a bankruptcy proceeding.
The court-issued case number associated with the bankruptcy filing being reported.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the chapter of the US Bankruptcy Code under which bankruptcy has been filed.
A free-form text field used to capture the Bankruptcy Chapter Type if Other is selected as the Bankruptcy Chapter Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a general grouping for activities that may create a delay in the actual bankruptcy process.

terms.term: Bankruptcy Delay Category Type Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark to an individual bankruptcy delay category type.

terms.term: Bankruptcy Delay Category Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Bankruptcy Delay Category Type.
The date the bankruptcy delay event ended.
When true, indicates that there is an outstanding delay in the bankruptcy process.
The date the bankruptcy delay event started.
Confirms that a person or company is legally free and clear to repay certain debts. Provided by the court.
The date when the Bankruptcy Disposition Type occurred.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the administrative standing of the bankruptcy case based upon a court ruling at a procedural milestone.
A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Bankruptcy Disposition Type.
The name of the district in which the bankruptcy petition will be processed.
The name of the court in which the bankruptcy petition will be processed.
The value of exempt assets that the bankruptcy court allows the debtor to retain.

The dollar amount of fees and other costs associated with bankruptcy based on the borrower's or guarantor's time in bankruptcy and the average amount per the state (United States) where the property is located as published by the investor.
The name of the state in which the bankruptcy petition was filed.
When true, indicates that the borrower declared bankruptcy within the past seven years.
