The amount of the defendants declared liabilities at the time of bankruptcy.

terms.term: Bankruptcy Payment Change Notice Reason Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the reason that a Payment Change Notice reflecting a change in the amount due to the servicer was filed.

terms.term: Bankruptcy Payment Change Notice Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Bankruptcy Payment Change Notice Reason Type.
Indicates the type of amendment being made to a bankruptcy plan.
The percentage of the total bankruptcy amount that will be paid to the creditors.
A unique code that identifies the priority and position of the lien holder involved based on the approval of the bankruptcy plan.
The date associated with the specified Bankruptcy Status Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the documented status of the bankruptcy.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Bankruptcy Status Type.
Unapplied funds related to a loan that is in bankruptcy.

terms.term: Bankruptcy Suspense Balance Amount Total Amount
terms.definition: Provides an arithmetic total of the Bankruptcy Suspense Balance Amount data items within the Loan container in this data set.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that indicates whether the bankruptcy filed is related to personal assets or a business.
When true, indicates the bankruptcy was filed voluntarily.

A measurement that specifies the elevation of flood water in relation to sea level at its highest point for a property. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Linear Unit Of Measure Type.

The guaranty fee rate prior to applying any adjustments, such as buyup/buydown. This can be specified in a price sheet, commitment, or other agreement. The guaranty fee is a portion of the interest on the loan that is paid to a party to ensure the timely payment of principal and interest to the holders of securities backed by the loan.

The Government Survey Base coordinate of the property that is the east-west line from which to measure Township lines (six [6] miles apart) north or south of the base line. For example: Township 2 North, Range 2 West measured from a Base and Meridian point.
The base loan amount to be loaned to the borrower not including PMI, MIP, or Funding Fee.
The result of dividing the unpaid principal balance (UPB) of the mortgage (not including any financed mortgage insurance premium) by the value of the subject property.
The mortgage amount before financed mortgage insurance or VA funding fee is added.
The minimum fixed guaranteed rent in a commercial property lease.

The maximum amount of building operating expenses which will be borne by the landlord prior to passing additional amounts through to the tenant. The base stop is expressed as an absolute dollar amount or dollar per square foot amount.

Similar to "base stop," except that rather than being specified as an absolute amount, the landlord's expenses are limited to the amount incurred in a specified calendar or fiscal year, usually (but not always) the calendar year in which the lease commences.
Describes the materials used to finish the basement ceiling.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the feature specified in the Basement Feature Type.
Specifies the basement feature that is present in the basement.
A free-form text field used to describe the Basement Feature if Other is selected as the Basement Feature Type.
A free-form text field describing the finish of the basement.
A measurement that specifies the total finished area of the basement. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Area Unit Of Measure Type.
Indicates that the basement is finished.
The percentage of the basement that is considered finished.
Specifies the percent of the first floor which the basement overlaps.
Describes the materials used to finish the basement floor.
Describes the materials used to finish the basement walls.
The rent charged in a subsidized housing project and computed on the basis of a maximum subsidy.

The cost of a property, including improvements, refinancing costs, closing costs and similar costs, less depreciation. Basis is used for tax purposes to calculate any profit or loss realized on the sale of a property.

The amount that is the basis for discounting the policy, if prior policy, loan payoff amount, or a simultaneous policy exists. Should a loan policy exceed the owner's insurance amount to determine if an additional premium is needed.
One one-hundredth of one percent. Used primarily to describe changes in yield or price on debt instruments, including mortgages and mortgage-backed securities.

Refers to the risk of the underlying mortgage loans and offered certificates tied to different indices. It is the possibility of the certificate accruing interest at higher interest rates than the underlying mortgage loans. When the aggregate amount of interest on the certificates is greater than the collateral, the amount is known as the basis-risk shortfall.

A stipulation within the regulatory acts governing the investments of insurance companies, savings and loan associations and mutual savings banks, allowing for a small percentage of total assets to be placed in investments not otherwise permitted by the acts.
Holds the number of bath equipment or fixtures specified by Bath Equipment Type.
A free-form text field used to describe in detail the identified bath equipment.
A collection of values that specify the bath equipment normally found in a living unit or residence.
A free-form text field used to provide additional information when Other is selected as the Bath Equipment Type.
A market characterized by falling prices. A bear market in the mortgage industry may be triggered by rising interest rates.
A suburban residential area where most residents commute to neighboring metropolitan areas to work.
The number of bedrooms per unit.
Gross income minus all expenses, except income taxes.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the primary type of exterior access for any below grade area.

terms.term: Below Grade Exterior Access Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Below Grade Exterior Access Type.
Indicates whether the seller provided below-market subordinate financing.

Describes mortgage insurance programs where the interest rates on the mortgages are below that ordinarily charged for similar conventional financing; used to assist low- and moderate-income families to rent or buy dwelling units.
A person who benefits from a life insurance policy, will, contract or deed of trust. In the latter case, the lender is the beneficiary.

The lender's statement under a deed of trust, detailing the remaining principal balance, monthly payment and interest rate on the loan. Also called a "bene statement," "offset statement" or "estoppel certificate."
Outlines the details for distribution of funds from a benefit plan.
Method of appraising corner lots which takes into consideration the value of the lot portions facing each street. Also called the "Baltimore Rule."

The Business Executive Team (BET) is responsible for reviewing proposed change / project requests received from Work Sponsors and to prioritize the work efforts of the organization to maintain and update the MISMO Products.
An improvement, replacement or maintenance which results in a higher asset valuation.
The Budget and Finance Committee (BFC) primary responsibility is to manage, review and recommend to the Board the annual budget.

1) The price at which a seller will sell particular securities. In the securities and commodities trade, the highest price offered for a security or commodity at a given time. Also called a quotation or quote. 2) Describes required home repairs or improvements and provides an estimation of cost to complete. AKA: Estimate to Complete Work, Repair Estimate, Alteration Improvement and Repairs.
The final amount bid for the property at a foreclosure sale. The sales price for a foreclosed property.
The minimum bid for a foreclosure sale that would be accepted by an investor.
The initial opening bid amount presented at the foreclosure sale for a property.
The difference between the highest price offered for securities and the lowest price that will prompt a seller to sell.
Large and complex data sets that traditional data-processing software typically cannot manage and analyze.
A document signed by a seller that certifies a transfer of ownership of personal property.
If appointed by the Member, the employee or office to which MISMO will send invoices.

A preliminary agreement between a buyer and seller which includes the price and terms of the contract. In commercial real estate, a legal agreement issued by the insurer or its agent to provide evidence of coverage until such time as a full policy(ies) is/are issued.
Confirms details about the birth of an individual. An official record provided by a government entity such as a state, county, city or borough.

The date of birth for the current INDIVIDUAL or CONTACT as a means of verifying identity. Note: For Party Role Type = Borrower, this would duplicate an existing field Borrower Birth Date. Actual usage would be dictated by implementation.
For a loan with scheduled biweekly payments this is the alternative maturity date if the loan had scheduled monthly payments.
A mortgage with payments due every two weeks, totaling 26 payments a year.

terms.term: Biweekly To Monthly On Default Indicator
terms.definition: Indicates if the lender allows conversion from Bi-weekly payments to monthly upon a default by the borrower.
The coverage of more than one piece of property under one instrument, such as a blanket insurance policy, blanket deed of trust, blanket assignment or blanket survey.
A mortgage that covers more than one parcel of real estate owned by the mortgagor.
A securities offering of interests in a property or group of properties that have yet to be acquired.
A square or rectangular portion of a city or town enclosed by streets. Often used as part of a subdivision legal description.
State laws covering the registration and sale of new securities.
The process of establishing a loan on a servicing system, either through new loan origination and set-up or via a servicing transfer.

terms.term: Board Of Governors Of The Federal Reserve System
terms.definition: Governing body of the Federal Reserve System that regulates all national and state-chartered banks in the Federal Reserve System and sets and regulates monetary policy. Commonly known as "the Fed."
Protection against loss arising out of the liability imposed upon the insured by law for damages due to bodily injury, sickness or disease sustained by third parties. Also see PERSONAL INJURY.
A free-form text field describing the body of water and/or its impact on the value and marketability of the property.
An unstructured name that identifies the name of the body of water.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents proximity of the body of water to the property.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of water body located on or near the property.

terms.term: Body Of Water Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Body Of Water Type.
Coverage for the loss to boilers and machinery caused by explosion or mechanical breakdown. The policy may cover damage to the boilers, machinery, other property and business interruption.
A Latin term meaning "in good faith," without fraud.
When true, specifies whether the split of the Loan Discount Fee meets the definition of ?bona fide? that applies for the jurisdiction.

An obligation written under seal. For example, the obligation may be to make good if a third party defaults (performance bond), or betrays a trust (fidelity bond), or an obligation to pay interest and principal as specified. The latter type of bond is a debt instrument which may be secured by a mortgage or a pool of mortgages.
Confirms the ownership of a bond.
A state or local sponsored method of assisting low income borrowers and first time homeowners in the purchase of a home at a reduced interest rate.
A long-term absolute net lease with a tenant who has a very high credit ceiling. The lease must be noncancelable and must call for a net rental equal to or above the amount of debt service.
The actual cost of assets purchased or acquired.

The capitalized cost of an asset, less depreciation taken for accounting purposes, based on the method used for the computing of depreciation over the useful life of the asset. The actual value of an asset after deducting depreciation and all liabilities is the "net book value."
Securities that are kept in computerized record form rather than paper certificate form.
Electronic registration of ownership and interests in securities.

A mortgagor who receives funds in the form of a loan with the obligation of repaying the loan with interest (if applicable), and in addition, any person purchasing (aka purchaser) the real property securing the loan, executing the promissory note, executing a guaranty of the debt evidenced by the promissory note, or signing a security instrument in connection with a loan.
Confirms that the borrowers understand the condition of the property.

terms.term: Borrower Age At Application Years Count
terms.definition: The age of the borrower at the time of application in years.
The date that the borrower signed the loan application.

terms.term: Borrower Authorized Additional Per Diem Days Count
terms.definition: The number of additional days of per diem interest between loan funding and the disbursement of loan proceeds that the borrower has formally authorized the lender to charge, according to state regulations.
When true, indicates that the borrower has filed a bankruptcy petition.
Borrower's date of birth.
Specifies the classification applied to a borrower for the purposes of processing or reporting.
The description of the Borrower Characteristic Type when Other is selected as the option from the enumerated list.
When true, indicates the provider of the service for which the particular fee or payment is charged was selected by the borrower independent of lender-provided list.
Indicates whether the borrower is the primary or a secondary borrower.
When true, indicates that there was a response from the borrower to the specified collection effort.

terms.term: Borrower Continues To Own Property Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the property associated with the loan is still owned by the borrower(s).
When true, indicates the borrower contribution to the workout was received.
When true, indicates a borrower contribution was a required condition of a workout.

Describes items related to the application including borrower credit, income, employment or assets. Typically provided by borrower. Includes items provided by third parties in support of the application of the borrower. Documents provided by the lender to be signed by the borrower are not considered Borrower Correspondence.

Under Section 6 of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act, a written request to the loan servicer which identifies the borrower by name and account, includes a statement of reasons why the borrower believes the mortgage account is in error, and which should include the words qualified written request. The servicer has legal deadlines to respond to a qualified written request.
The number of borrowers obligated on the note.
The date of the borrower's death.

terms.term: Borrower Financed FHA Discount Points Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of discount points allowable by the applicable FHA guidelines to be financed on a FHA no cash out refinance. Used for FHA loans. Note: Discount points financed and not financed by borrower are equal to the Discount Points Total Amount Paid by Borrower - FHA.
When true, indicates that at least one of the borrowers on the loan application qualifies as a first generation homebuyer as determined by lender or investor guidelines.
Indicates that the borrower qualifies as a first time homebuyer as determined by the lender and/or the investor. (Note: The 3 year rule used in the Declarations alone is not sufficient.)
Indicates if a Borrower Acknowledgement Letter needs to be processed with the order.
The funding fee percentage due from the borrower. The fee is entered as a percentage.
When true indicates that borrower(s) have chosen to have a home inspection performed.
When true, indicates the borrower has agreed to allow servicer to release borrower contact information to a housing counselor.

terms.term: Borrower Is An Individual Person Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the applicant or co-applicant is a natural person and not a legal entity.
Verifies that there are no outstanding liens or mortgages that would not allow for the appropriate lien position of a new loan. AKA: Borrowers Affidavit.

terms.term: Borrower Mail To Address Same As Property Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the mailing address for the borrower is the same as the property address.
The date that the borrower may request cancellation of MI insurance as identified by HOEPA regulations.
The dollar amount of the borrower's portion of closing costs associated with the process of modifying the terms of a mortgage.

terms.term: Borrower Nearest Living Relative Relationship Description
terms.definition: Describes the type of relationship of the nearest living relative to the Borrower.

terms.term: Borrower Paid Discount Points Total Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount of discount points that are paid by the borrower.

terms.term: Borrower Paid FHA VA Closing Costs Amount
terms.definition: The estimated dollar amount of closing costs that will be paid by the borrower on the subject property excluding discount points and prepaid items. Used for FHA and VA loans.

terms.term: Borrower Paid FHA VA Closing Costs Percent
terms.definition: The percentage of the estimated closing costs that will be paid by the borrower on the subject property excluding discount points and prepaids.
The total monthly borrower income per lender or investor guidelines.
The description of the relationship of a borrower to (an) other borrower(s), if any, for Title purposes.

terms.term: Borrower Relationship Title Type Other Description
terms.definition: When Other is specified in Borrower Relationship Title Type, this element contains the description.
A portion of 100 that represents the interest rate on the loan being initially requested by the borrower.
The amount of the loan initially requested by the borrower. This amount may include financed PMI, MIP and Funding Fees.
The number of loan payments that are available to the borrower from verified financial reserves after closing.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the basis on which the borrower lives/lived at the indicated address.
The total number of months the borrower (has) resided at the indicated address.
The number of years the borrower resided at the indicated address. Could be either current or prior address.
The date the borrower actually moved out of the indicated address.
The date it was reported that the borrower moved to the indicated address.
The date the borrower actually moved to the indicated address.
This attribute, accompanying borrower residence data, qualifies it as either the current or prior borrower's residence.
When true, indicates that the Borrower is also the Builder on the loan transaction.

terms.term: Borrower Selected Anti Steering Comparison Type
terms.definition: Specifies the loan characteristic(s) used as the basis for the comparison loan chosen by the Borrower.

terms.term: Borrower Selected Anti Steering Comparison Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field which contains the description of the Anti-Steering comparison type when Other is selected as the Borrower Selected Anti-Steering Comparison Type.
A numeric value that identifies a specific borrower among multiple borrowers.
The expiration date of the last solicitation offered to the borrower.
The number of 1-4 unit properties that are financed and owned and/or obligated on by an individual borrower.
Specifies the reason that the borrower does not occupy the delinquent property.

terms.term: Borrower Vacancy Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Borrower Vacancy Reason Type.
Process in which the Borrower(s) inform the Lender that they do not wish to proceed with the loan origination process.

An agreement wherein the borrower/guarantor has personally agreed to fully repay all amounts owed under a mortgage loan, irrespective of whether the collateral is adequate to retire the debt. This agreement gives the holder of the note, or other negotiable instrument, the right to recover against the borrower/guarantor personally, including any and all assets of the borrower/ guarantor.

An agreement wherein the borrower/guarantor has personally agreed to repay a set dollar amount, all amounts exceeding a stated dollar amount or a percentage of the outstanding balance of the mortgage loan. This agreement gives the holder of the note, or other negotiable instrument, the right to recover against the borrower/guarantor personally, including any and all assets of the borrower/guarantor, but only to the extent specified. For example, a borrower/guarantor may agree to pay the first $1 million of a $5 million loan or the top 25% of the loan.
Authorizes lender to request personal information on the borrower's behalf. AKA: Borrowers Authorization, General Certification and Authorization.

terms.term: Borrowers Contract With Respect To Hotel And Transient Use Of Property
terms.definition: Certification that the borrower will not use a multiple dwelling property for hotel or transient housing. AKA: Hotel Transient, HUD 92561.
See DEBT-TO-INCOME RATIO.
The boundary direction type indicated for a specific boundary along with a boundary type.
A free-form text field used to describe the boundary direction if Other is selected as the Boundary Direction Type.
Polygon of X-Y coordinates that represent a shape of an area and is recognizable to geospatial standards such as KML as used by commercial earth mapping services such as BING or Google Earth.
The boundary type indicated for a specific boundary along with a boundary direction.
A free-form text field used to describe the type of boundary if Other is selected as the Boundary Type.

A variable rate loan that attempts to smooth the impact of rate increases on borrowers by deferring a portion of high interest rates until maturity. Usually, all interest above a certain rate is deferred to maturity.
Failure to perform under a contract or the violation of a legal obligation.
The date the Servicer intends on commencing the foreclosure process as stated in the written notification to the borrower that they have failed to make payments, or arrangements to make repayment.
The first written notification to a borrower that an account has moved from a current to delinquent status. Includes the necessary terms to cure the breach. AKA: Breach Letter
The figure at which occupancy income is equal to all required expenses and debt service. Used to determine the amount of cash flow necessary to operate a residential or commercial property.

In a retail lease, the point specified in absolute sales dollars or sales dollars per square foot, above which the tenant has agreed to pay percentage rent in addition to base rent. For example, in addition to base rent, a tenant may agree to pay 2% of annual gross sales above $2 million. In this case, $2 million is the breakpoint.
A loan which enables a homebuyer to get financing to make a down payment and pay closing costs on a new home before selling the present house. Also called "gap financing."
A term used to describe coverage which extends beyond "standard" peril insurance policies, i.e., fire and extended coverage, named perils, etc.

An endorsement to a general liability policy which grants expanded coverage to property in the care, custody or control of the insured, property which is not normally insured if damaged by the insured's negligence.

When true, indicates that high-speed internet access is available exclusively through a digital subscriber line, fiber-optic or cable. When false, indicates that high-speed internet access is unavailable.

An individual employed on a fee or commission basis as an agent to bring buyers and sellers together and assist in negotiating contracts between them. Also see MORTGAGE BROKER and THIRD-PARTY ORIGINATOR (TPO).
Describes sources and amounts of compensation a brokered mortgage transaction. Provided by Broker to Borrower.

A report produced by a real estate sales person or broker which provides an estimation of the subject property's most probable selling price and a listing of comparable sales. The report typically combines information from a drive-by exterior inspection and various external data sources, such as MLS, but not an interior inspection. AKA: BPO.

A report produced by a real estate sales person or broker which provides an estimation of the subject property's most probable selling price and a listing of comparable sales but with no physical inspection of the subject property.

A report produced by a real estate sales person or broker which provides an estimation of the subject property's most probable selling price and a listing of comparable sales and includes details from a physical inspection of the subject property.

Mortgage for which a third party takes an application, and may process or underwrite the mortgage documents, then assigns the documents to another mortgage lender. After receiving the assigned mortgage documents, the mortgage lender underwrites, funds and closes the mortgage in its own name.

A project sponsor specifically organized to build or rehabilitate and sell a project immediately upon completion to a private, nonprofit organization, at the certified cost of the project. The nonprofit sponsor buys a total package.

terms.term: Builder's And Sponsor's Profit And Risk Allowance (BSPRA)
terms.definition: A credit against the required equity contribution in HUD/FHA insurance programs granted the developer for its services in sponsoring and building the project.
Fire and extended coverage insurance for a building under construction. Coverage increases automatically as the building progresses and terminates at completion.
Confirms that the property construction is completed to requirements. Provided by builder. AKA: Termite Treatment Builders Certificate (99A).
Regulations based on safety and health standards that govern design, construction and materials used in construction.
The total number of detached buildings on the site.
A ratio of net rentable area to gross building area.
The trade association of owners and managers of commercial real estate, who benefit from exchange of information and management techniques.
Written authorization from a local municipal authority for the construction of a new building, or for extensive repairs or improvements on an existing structure.
Indicates the level or classification of the instance of the Building Permit Work Type.

terms.term: Building Permit Level Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the permit classification if Other is selected as the Building Permit Level Type.
Commentary about the building permit proposed usage provided by the permitting authority and is not categorical in nature.

The identifier used by the permitting authority to designate this instance of a permit. Often prefixed by the 2- or 4-digit year and an abbreviation of the type and/or work class of permit or certificate.
The date corresponding to the status of the permit as indicated in the Permit Status Type as assigned by the authority for this permit.
Commentary about the building permit status provided by the permitting authority and is not categorical in nature.
The current status for this permit.

terms.term: Building Permit Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the permit status if Other is selected as the Building Permit Status Type.
Commentary about the building permit trade provided by the permitting authority and is not categorical in nature.
Commentary about the building usage permit provided by the permitting authority and is not categorical in nature.
The usage standard designation assigned by the permitting authority for this permit.

terms.term: Building Permit Usage Standard Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the permit usage standard type if Other is selected as the Building Permit Usage Standard Type.
Commentary about the building work purpose provided by the permitting authority and is not categorical in nature.
The class of work related to the current structure(s) (if any) on the property for this permit.

terms.term: Building Permit Work Purpose Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the permit work class if Other is selected as the Building Permit Work Purpose Type.

The primary type of trade work permissions on this permit and is directly related to the type of inspection for the component of the structure that would be required by the respective jurisdictional building code and conducted by the local permitting authority.

terms.term: Building Permit Work Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the permitted work type if Other is selected as the Building Permit Work Type.
A method of real estate appraisal used to determine the value of a building when the land value is known.
Permanent, immovable appliances or similar features.
Transfer of servicing in a one-time transaction where all loan files and portfolio information are transferred on a specific date or within a short, specified time frame.
A market characterized by rising prices. In the mortgage industry, a bull market may be prompted by falling interest rates.
Interim financing for leased-up properties often used to repay the construction loan; typically an interest-only loan for 2 to 10 years that cannot be prepaid.

1)Days on which a bank or market is open for business or trading; usually excludes Saturdays, Sundays and legal public holidays. 2)The type of day used by business partners to specify time-bound requirements for processing an eMortgage.
Compensation to a business owner or operator for income lost when the business is closed due to fire or any other insured hazard.
Authorizes the legal operation of a business in an area issued by the state or municipality.

A set of high level, generic business process flows depicting common activities that may occur over the 'Life of a Loan'. Links are provided within the process flows and related process narratives to MISMO Products. Enables business professionals to access MISMO Products within the context of the business process or processes they support.
Proof that federal assistance is required to keep a development project from failing.
A mortgage with a below- market interest rate made by a lender in return for an interest rate subsidy in the form of additional discount points paid by the builder, seller or buyer.

An agreement between an interim and permanent lender for the sale and assignment of a mortgage to the permanent lender upon the completion of a building. Often the mortgagor is a party to this agreement on the theory that the mortgagor should have a contractual right to insist that the permanent lender buy the mortgage.
Freddie Mac's up-front payment to a loan seller in exchange for a higher guarantee fee.
Establishes a rate variant, or temporary adjustment, of interest rate on the loan. Used to reduce, or step down, an interest rate.
The dollar amount associated with the Buydown Funding Type and/or Fund Source Type.
The date from which the duration of the buydown is counted.

terms.term: Buydown Base Date Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Buydown Base Date Type.
The value to be used to base buydown calculations. Original loan amount or declining loan amount.

The time interval in months between interest rate increases during the buydown period. For example if the interest rate increases annually during a two year buydown, the frequency of interest rate change is 12 months.
The total number of months during which any buydown is in effect. This represents the accumulation of all of the buydown periods.
The method used for providing the buydown funds.
Used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Buydown Funding Type.
The amount by which the interest rate can increase at each adjustment period within the buydown duration.
The percent by which the interest rate was bought down at origination. For example, for a 3-2-1 buydown this would be 3.

terms.term: Buydown Initial Effective Interest Rate Percent
terms.definition: The final bought down interest rate. The rate that the applicant will pay after the buydown is applied.
Indicates whether or not the lender is funding the interest rate buydown.
The effective date of the Buydown Occurrence that is being reported.
Describes how the remaining buydown funds are disbursed at time of payoff.
The percentage associated with the Buydown Funding Type and/or Buydown Source Type.
When true, indicates that the buydown rate is reflected in the note.
The effective reduction against the initial note rate while this buydown payment is in effective.
A unique sequence number for the entries in the buydown schedule. Used to establish correct sequence of the payment elements when an effective date has not yet been established.
The amount of buydown for each payment per the buydown schedule.

terms.term: Buydown Schedule Periodic Payment Effective Date
terms.definition: The first date the specific buydown payment becomes effective.
Number of payments in the period. Referred to at time of loan application as the period to next adjustment when establishing the terms of the buydown agreement.
The buydown subsidy amount that is a part of the total payment amount being reported.
The effective date of the buydown subsidy amount that is being reported.
When true, indicates that there is buydown funding on this loan that reduces the interest rate and/or the payments for a specified period.
The total dollar amount of funds held for the buydown subsidy portion of the monthly principal and interest payment, to be discharged according to the buydown schedule.
When true, indicates the buyer's and the seller's agents are the same party.
Economic conditions in which the supply of housing exceeds demand. Sellers may be forced to make substantial price concessions.

terms.term: Buying Your Home Settlement Costs And Helpful Information
terms.definition: Describes the settlement process, charges, rights and remedies available under RESPA, as well as explanation of settlement services and costs. AKA: Settlement Cost Booklet.
Bid Wanted In Competition
A "call-on-call" compound option.
A "call-on-put" compound option.
Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System

Confirms results from the HUD Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System, which indicates whether the individual is in default on direct or guaranteed federal loans or are otherwise ineligible for an FHA loan. Result is transcribed or captured as a screen-print from the HUD website. AKA: CAIVRS.
An identifier assigned by HUDs Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System, an interactive system used to check the applicants outstanding federal obligations.

Process of calculating the minimum required amount of any insurance required by the Lender based on loan amount, dwelling replacement costs, or environmental factors. The Lender confirms the Borrower has obtained sufficient coverage on each policy to meet the Lender's minimum coverage and deductible requirements.
A portion of 100 that represents the percentage of calculated median income representing the entire household.
The specific value of the result of the requested or performed calculation.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of calculation requested or performed.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Calculation Type.
A formal process to announce the intent to pursue development of a MISMO Product and solicit participation by interested parties.
A contract granting the right, but not the obligation, to purchase a security at a specified strike price on a particular date.

A provision of a note that allows the lender the right to demand or "call in" the balance of the mortgage obligation. The call can be exercised due to a breach of specified terms or conditions, or at the discretion of the lender (such as when the note rate is lower than the current market rate). In bonds, the issuer's right to redeem the bond before maturity.
The Canadian Social Insurance Number associated with the party.
In a lease or other contract, a provision detailing conditions under which each party may terminate the agreement.
Confirms that a property is no longer listed with a real estate agent.
The net worth of a business represented by the amount that its assets exceed liabilities. Money invested to create income.
An asset of a permanent or fixed nature to be used in a business or trade and not sold.
The cost of a capital asset or a property improvement made to add value to or extend the useful life of an existing capital asset.
The gain or loss incurred from the sale or disposition of a capital asset.
Any structure or component erected as a permanent improvement to real property that adds to its value and useful life.
Reserves that may be required by loan documents to fund the future payment of capital improvement for the property.
The financial market for buying and selling long-term investments (those with maturities of greater than one year), such as mortgages, Treasury bonds and certificates of deposit.
The conversion of a future net income stream into present value by using a specific desired rate of earnings as a discount rate.
The dollar amount of the Capitalization Charge Type.
The analysis based on the conversion of a future net income stream into present value by using a specific desired rate of earnings as a discount rate.
Specifies the type of fee or charge that is capitalized into the principal balance.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Capitalization Charge Type.
A free form comment or description associated with the capitalization charge.
The date on which the fee or charge was capitalized into the principal balance.

The rate of return on net operating income considered acceptable for an investor and used to determine the capitalized value. This rate should provide a return on, as well as a return of, capital. Also known as "cap rate."
Indicates that the mortgage balance includes capitalized origination fees.
Indicates that interest accrued, escrow disbursements made and/or fees charged are included in the unpaid principal balance.
The estimated market value of business assets in terms of the present value of anticipated earnings.
A rate commitment by a lender which locks in a maximum rate but allows the borrower to relock if market rates decrease. Also referred to as cap and float.
Consumer safeguards on an adjustable rate mortgage which limit the amount the interest rate may change per year and over the life of the loan.
Consumer safeguards on an adjustable rate mortgage which limit the amount monthly payments may change.
A measurement that specifies the area of the identified car storage. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Area Unit Of Measure Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies how the vehicle storage is connected to a dwelling.
A free-form text field used to describe in detail the identified car storage.
When true Indicates the presence of car storage.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of vehicle storage.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Car Storage Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list which represents the overall rating of the differences between the comparable and the subject for all types of vehicle storage included in the rental agreement.

A postal carrier route code is a part of the complete carrier route. The carrier route code is 4 characters consisting of 1 letter for the type of carrier route and 3 digits for the carrier route. The complete carrier route identifies a group of addresses to which the USPS assigns the same code to aid in mail delivery. The complete Carrier Route consists of 9 digits, 5 numbers for the ZIP Code and the 4 characters for the carrier route code.
An agreement in which the seller takes back a note for part of the purchase price secured by a junior mortgage, wrap-around mortgage or contract for deed.
The charges or costs incurred for holding property when it is idle, non-productive or in interim use, including the opportunity cost of non-productive use of the property.

Indicates if the difference between capped and uncapped interest rate is to be carried over and applied to a future interest rate change. If Carryover Rate Indicator is present, any accumulated rate is placed in Carryover Rate Percent.

The cumulative unapplied difference between the calculated interest rate and the capped Interest Rate that can be used to modify the calculated interest rate at future interest rate change dates. Carryover Rate Percent is only present if Carryover Rate Indicator is true.
A unique identifier assigned by the court of law with legal jurisdiction over a legal case.
When true, indicates the activity was spent on case administration work versus active counseling.
An accounting method under which income is reported when actually received and expenses are deducted when paid.

A method of calculating the appraised value of a property that considers sales and financing concessions when evaluating comparable properties. There is no standard in the appraisal industry for measuring cash equivalent value, but investors and mortgage insurers sometimes insist that cash equivalency be incorporated in appraised values.
Cash received less cash paid out, including income taxes paid.
Cash received less cash paid out, before any consideration for income taxes.

terms.term: Cash From Borrower At Closing Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount required from the borrower to consummate the closing of a real estate transaction.

terms.term: Cash From Seller At Closing Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount required from the seller to consummate the closing of a real estate transaction.
A market where mortgages and/or mortgage-backed securities are bought and sold for immediate delivery and cash payment. Also called spot market.
Reserves normally kept by the owner of the property to fund any operating shortfall or capital improvements that are required for the property.
When true, indicates the borrower cannot make mortgage payments due to insufficient cash reserves.
The process by which a dollar adjustment rather than a physical instrument is used to satisfy the delivery requirement of a given contract at expiration.

terms.term: Cash To Borrower At Closing Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount received by the borrower to consummate the closing of a real estate transaction.

terms.term: Cash To Seller At Closing Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount received by the seller to consummate the closing of a real estate transaction.
The rate of return on an investment as measured by cash returned to the investor, based on the investor's cash investment and without regard to income tax savings or the use of borrowed funds.

When the principal amount of a new mortgage involved in refinancing is greater than the principal amount outstanding of the existing mortgage being refinanced, and all or a portion of the equity is converted to cash.
Losses on property arising from fire, storm, theft or similar sudden and unexpected occurrences.

Development Process Document Only: 1. Failure to adhere to, or rejection of, the IPR or Antitrust Policies; 2. Repeated blatant disregard of MISMO-approved processes after receiving a written request from MISMO to cease and desist prohibited activities; and 3. Making endorsement claims prohibited of a MISMO Member (or that would be prohibited of a person or entity if they were a Member) under MISMOs Bylaws or MISMO-approved processes. Policies and Procedures Only: 1. Failure to adhere to or rejection of the IPR or Antitrust Policies. 2. Repeated blatant disregard of these Policies and Procedures after receiving a written request from MISMO to cease and desist prohibited activities; and 3. Making endorsement claims prohibited of a MISMO Member (or that would be prohibited of a person or entity if they were a Member) under MISMOs Bylaws or these Policies and Procedures.
Latin for "let the buyer beware." This term signifies that the seller offers goods "as is," with no warranty.
Coastal Barrier Reform Act
The stated maximum percentage to which the interest rate can increase over the life of the loan.

terms.term: Ceiling Rate Percent Earliest Effective Months Count
terms.definition: The minimum number of months at which the maximum interest rate could be reached.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the style of the ceiling.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Ceiling Style Type.
Consolidation, Extension and Modification Agreement

A single digit number which is the first digit of all the blocks which comprise the block group. A statistical subdivision of a census tract, a block group is the smallest geographic unit for which the Census Bureau tabulates sample data. Example: block group 3 consists of all blocks within a 2000 census tract numbering from 3000 to 3999. In 1990, block group 3 consisted of all blocks numbered from 301 to 399Z.

A four-digit number to identify a census block. A subdivision of a census tract, a block is the smallest geographic unit for which the Census Bureau tabulates 100-percent data. Many blocks correspond to individual city blocks bounded by streets, but blocks - especially in rural areas -- may include many square miles and may have some boundaries that are not streets.
Six digit number designated by HUD to identify a neighborhood. Census tract numbers are entered on compliance reports to monitor a lender's mortgage activity.

A four-digit number used to identify a census tract. A census tract is a small, relatively permanent statistical subdivision of a county delineated by a local committee of census data users for the purpose of presenting data. Census tract numbers are always unique within a county and usually unique within an MA. Almost all census tract numbers range from 0001 to 9499. Leading zeroes are not shown on the Census Bureau's maps or in its printed reports.
Identifies census tract as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau where subject property is located.

Census tract suffixes may range from 01 to 98. Many census tracts do not have a suffix; in such cases, the suffix field is either left blank or is zero-filled. The decimal point separating the four-digit basic tract number from the two-digit suffix is shown in printed reports, in microfiche, and on census maps; in machine-readable files, the decimal point is implied.
The area geographically located within the central business district of a municipality.
A unique standard for the global interoperability of smart cards, first developed by Visa before being handed over to the European Committee for Banking Standards.
The date of the certificate application as recorded by the local authority.

A trusted third-party organization or company that issues, manages, renews, and revokes Digital Certificates used to create Digital Signatures. The Certificate Authority registers the certificate holder's name and address and allows others to see if the certificate is valid, revoked, or expired. The third-party certificate authority also has the ability to confirm the identity of the certificate holder. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
The type of authority which issued the permission for the property.
A free-form text field used to describe the status of a given certificate issued by a local authority if Other is selected as the Certificate Authority Type.
The date of the certificate expiration as recorded by the local authority.
The date of the certificate issuance as recorded by the local authority.

A contingent promise to reimburse an insured mortgagee for certain costs incurred during foreclosure of an insured mortgage, provided the proceeds from the sale of the property are sufficient to cover the lender's claim.
A document issued by an architect or engineer stating that construction is completed in accordance with the terms, conditions, approved plans and specifications.
Certificates issued by financial institutions with a stated return or interest rate, and with a set maturity. The bank pays the holder in due course at maturity.
A document issued by the Veterans Administration which verifies a veteran's eligibility for a VA mortgage guarantee.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the purpose of obtaining a Certificate of Eligibility.

terms.term: Certificate Of Eligibility Use Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Certificate of Eligibility of Use Type.
A form which evidences policy coverage, limits, etc., which is generally used as proof of insurance. These forms have no legal status and cannot be used in lieu of actual insurance policies.
Written authorization given by a local municipality that allows a newly completed or substantially renovated structure to be inhabited.
A document issued by the Veterans Administration which establishes a maximum value and loan amount for a VA guaranteed mortgage.
An affidavit issued the buyer of real property at a judicial or tax sale which guarantees the deed of the parcel purchased, pending court confirmation.
A confirmation written by a title attorney or company stating that the title to a parcel of real property is legally vested in the present owner.
FHA form filled out by the Department of Veteran Affairs in order to establish a borrower's eligibility for an FHA Vet Mortgage.

Public Key Infrastructure term. A list of Digital Certificates that are revoked. CRLs are an important part of Public Key Infrastructure, as they validate that the certificate used by the Digital Signature on an Electronic Record has not been revoked and may be trusted. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
The date corresponding to the status of the certificate as indicated in the Certificate Status Type as assigned by the authority for this permit.
The status for the certificate.
A free-form text field used to describe the status of a given certificate issued by a local authority if Other is selected as the Certificate Status Type.
The type of certificate issued by a local authority for the property.
A free-form text field used to describe the certificate if Other is selected as the Certificate Type.

Certification Revoking List: If a certificate is no longer trustworthy (for example, because of a change in the status of the certificate holder, departure of the certificate holder from the company, or compromise of the holder's private key), it can be revoked prior to its expiration date.

A professional designation awarded by the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) to those in the industry who have demonstrated superior knowledge and skills in the field of real estate finance. Candidates must be employed by MBA member firms and meet various educational, experience and examination requirements.
A professional designation conferred by the Institute of Real Estate Management to recognize experienced members of the property management industry.
Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
A chronology of documents which have transferred title to a parcel of real property from the original owner to the present owner.
A document evidencing a change in the original plan of construction by a building owner or general contractor.
When true, indicates the disclosure or redisclosure was triggered by a changed circumstance.
The date changed circumstances as defined in Regulation Z altered information on the Loan Estimate or Closing Disclosure.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the reason for the changed circumstance altering information on the Loan Estimate or Closing Disclosure. As defined in Regulation Z, an extraordinary or unexpected event beyond control of any interested party, or any new information which affects the consumer or loan transaction, thereby changing information that the creditor relied upon when providing the Loan Estimate.

terms.term: Changed Circumstance Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Changed Circumstance Reason Type.
Bankruptcy filing which gives a trustee the power to distribute a debtor's assets to creditors. Also called a "liquidation."

A reorganization by a business allowing the debtor to maintain operating control of the business while restructuring debts and working out a repayment schedule acceptable to the creditors. Also called "debtor in possession."
A debt repayment plan where an individual debtor files a budget with the court and agrees to make partial payment to creditors over a three- to five-year period. Also called "wage earner plan."
Specifies the character encoding set used by the resource content.

terms.term: Character Encoding Set Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture the resource Character Encoding Set type if Other is selected for CharacterEncodingSetType.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list which determines basic eligibility requirements for receipt of VA benefits under Title 38 of the United States Code.

terms.term: Character Of Discharge Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field which specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Character of Discharge Type.
A free-form text field describing the characteristics that affect marketability.
The date the total charge off amount was charged off.
The dollar amount of the Charge Off Item Type.
Specifies the type of loss that is to be charged off.

terms.term: Charge Off Item Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Charge Off Item Type.
A description of the reasons for the charge off decision.
A unique identifier assigned by a party to specify a reason for the charge off. The party assigning the identifier can be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
For accounting purposes, a numerical designation assigned to each asset, liability and capital account of a business.
Development Process Document Only: A brief statement describing a WG's purpose and scope Policies and Procedures Only: See Work Group Charter
An artificial intelligence application that conducts conversations with users through text or voice interactions.
See PERSONAL PROPERTY.
An agreement between a secured party and a debtor creating a security interest in personal property.
In the cash or futures market, the specific rate security that can be purchased for the lowest total price and in sufficient quantity to meet the delivery requirements of a particular contract.
Represents money payable or paid (if cancelled). AKA: Checks, Cancelled Checks.

A number added to another number or code to detect errors. It is derived by calculating a value specific to the number or code. The integrity of the number or code may be verified by re-computing the check digit and comparing it with the included one. If the check digits match, the identifier was not altered.
Describes the list of action items, steps, or elements required to be consulted or completed to accomplish a task.
The exchange where futures and options contracts are traded. Residential mortgage bankers may use futures and options to hedge their inventories of mortgages.
The largest and most active organized options marketplace.
Describes the legal obligation of a parent to pay money toward the care and maintenance of his/her children.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the U.S. citizenship or alien status of the individual.
The name of the city or Military APO FPO designation.

terms.term: City Town Village Of Birth Name
terms.definition: The City, Town or Village of birth of the individual.

Policies written on a "claims made" basis only cover claims presented during the particular year the policy is in force, for incidents which occurred during the same policy year or for any previous year noted in the "claims made" policy (retroactive date). This form of coverage contrasts with an "occurrence" policy which responds to incidents regardless of when the claim is reported.

HUD program which authorized the payment of claims for insurance benefits without conveying title to the foreclosed property to HUD. Use of the CWCOT program is limited to cases involving deficiency judgments or other situations where HUD either requests or requires a mortgagee to obtain a property appraisal or to use CWCOT.

terms.term: Clear And Marketable Property Title Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the property has a title that is clear and marketable.
Process of reviewing documentation to confirm that all outstanding closing conditions are satisfied.
Unencumbered title to real property, free of liens or defects. Also, "free and clear."
A bank account used by a mortgage servicer for temporary, short-term deposit of mortgage payments collected for transmittal to investors or for deposit in escrow accounts.
A third-party participant in settling security trades by acting as a buyer to each seller and a seller to each buyer, ensuring performance.

As of fiscal year 2008, all agencies are required to utilize an automated counseling application of their choice. The application is generally referred to as the “Client Management System”. The purpose of the system is to automate counseling services, store client data, and interface with the Housing Counseling System's Agency Reporting Module to submit required data to HUD.
Requests that a line of credit be closed after receiving a payoff under a separate cover. AKA: account Closure Letter.
The right of one agent to be the only one, other than the owner, who may sell the property during a period of time.
The interval of time under a mortgage during which the loan cannot be prepaid.
Text comments about the closed sale information.
A mortgage under which the mortgagor is prohibited from borrowing additional funds under the same mortgage.
In real estate, the delivery of a deed, the signing of a note, and the disbursement of funds necessary to consummate a sale or loan transaction.
The dollar amount of the specified Closing Adjustment Item Type. A positive amount indicates a credit to the Buyer.

terms.term: Closing Adjustment Item Paid By Type
terms.definition: The role of the party making the payment for the closing adjustment item.

terms.term: Closing Adjustment Item Paid Outside Of Closing Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates payment of the closing adjustment item was paid outside of closing.
The type of adjustment made during the origination process.

terms.term: Closing Adjustment Item Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Closing Adjustment Item Type.
The start date for calculating the total number of days covered by the closing adjustment item.
The end date for calculating the total number of days covered by the closing adjustment item, inclusive of this date.
The identifying file number assigned to the transaction by the Closing Agent also known as a Settlement Agent.
This designates the type of the closing agent.
When Other is specified in Closing Agent Type, this data element contains the description.
Indicates that some or all of the closing cost were financed into the loan amount.
The dollar amount of funds supplied by a specified source at closing.
The costs which are incurred in order to purchase real estate. These may include points, taxes, settlement agent fees and more.

The date the closing documents were fully executed and the borrower becomes contractually responsible for the debt. Depending on the location (wet-sign, dry-sign, table-funded and/or escrow state) of the loan closing, the Closing Date may be the same date as either the Document Preparation Date and/or the Execution Date and/or the Recorded Date.
The CFPB Closing Disclosure document. Provides disclosures that help consumers in understanding all of the costs of the transaction.

terms.term: Closing Disclosure Waiting Period Waived Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that upon receipt of the Closing Disclosure, and due to a bona fide personal financial emergency, the consumer modified or waived the three-business-day waiting period that must be met prior to consummation of the mortgage loan transaction.

Closing Disclosure using the alternative disclosures and modifications permitted for transactions without a seller. Refers to Exhibit H 25(J) "Modification to Closing Disclosure for Transaction Not Involving Seller" in the CFPB Integrated Mortgage Disclosures Regulation.
For split disclosures, the borrower-only representation.

Closing Disclosure providing both borrower and seller sides of the real estate transaction. Refers to Exhibit H 25(A) "Mortgage Loan Transaction Closing Disclosure Model Form" in the CFPB Integrated Mortgage Disclosures Regulation.
For split disclosures, the property seller-only representation.
The date the mortgage loan closing document(s) was/were received by the Closing Agent.
The date on which the terms and conditions disclosed within the closing documents expire.
The time of day on the date on which the terms and conditions disclosed within the closing documents expire.
Free-form text to further define the execution location details (i.e. 3rd office on the left).
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that categorizes the location at which a closing event will take place.

terms.term: Closing Event Location Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Closing Event Location Type.

terms.term: Closing Event No Agent Present Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the signer will execute the documents without an agent physically present.
When true, indicates that the signer will use an internet based or online system to execute the documents.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains instructions about amending the closing document.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that categorizes the reasons a revision is being made to the closing event, instructions or documents.

terms.term: Closing Information Revision Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Closing Information Revision Reason Type.
The date the referenced closing instructions are issued and take priority over any previously issued closing instructions.
Describes the conditions that must be met in order to complete the closing. Provided by Lender to Closing Agent. AKA: Lender Closing Instructions, Settlement Agent Instructions.

terms.term: Closing Instructions Consolidated Closing Conditions Description
terms.definition: Consolidated description of all closing instructions. Use this field when the individual closing conditions are not represented in separate entries.

terms.term: Closing Instructions Property Tax Message Description
terms.definition: The text message to the closing agent regarding the status of tax payments for the subject property.

terms.term: Closing Instructions Termite Report Required Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that a Termite Report is a requirement of closing.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains the lender's current requirements for or acceptance of, the Closing Protection Letter.
The date and time the closing event is scheduled to take place.

A financial disclosure giving an account of all funds received and expected at closing, including escrow deposits for taxes, hazard insurance and mortgage insurance. All FHA, VA and most conventionally financed loans use a uniform settlement statement called the "HUD-1."
Process of Closing and Funding a mortgage loan.
Any outstanding claim or encumbrance which, if valid, would affect or impair title. It can be removed by a quitclaim deed, release or court action. Also called a title defect.
California Land Title Association

A zoning procedure where there is a prescribed amount of residential or unit density for an entire area. The developer is permitted to concentrate or disperse the density within the area in accordance with flexible site-planning criteria. This differs from a traditional zoning plan that dictates density on a lot-by-lot basis, prescribing the same maximum density for all single structure lots within the zoning district.
Constant Maturity Treasury

terms.term: Co Maker Endorser Of Note Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the Borrower answered "yes" to the declaration question: "Are you a co-maker or endorser on a note"
Second or additional person equally responsible for payments on a mortgage. A co-borrower does not have to take title to the property, but usually has to sign the mortgage note.

A second borrower who signs a mortgage loan with a mortgagor. The co-mortgagor's income, assets and debts are combined with the mortgagor's for underwriting and ratio analysis purposes. The co-mortgagor's name must appear on the FHA Certificate of Commitment and the mortgage or deed of trust. For full guarantee under the VA's program, the co-mortgagor must be either a spouse or another eligible veteran.
See COOPERATIVE.

One who agrees to assume a debt obligation if the principal borrower defaults on mortgage payments. A co-signer assumes only personal liability and has no ownership interest in the property; his or her income and obligations are used in the underwriting process to reinforce the credit of the principal borrower.
Council of Chairs. The CoC serves as a forum for all MISMO WGs to communicate and exchange information on topics of general and shared interest across all WGs.
Identifies the owner or publisher of the code associated with a MISMO term with the class word of "Code" by means of a URI. This is an XML attribute.
The date on which the value represented by the MISMOCode is effective as determined by the issuer or owner as specified by the CodeOwnerURI.

A type of insurance where the insured agrees to carry a specified proportion of the policy amount to the actual value of the property insured at the time of the loss. Thus, a portion of the property value is self-insured. In federal multifamily housing programs, a clause which forces an insured to share in a loss if he/she is underinsured at the time of the loss. For a reduced premium, the insured is obligated to carry an amount of insurance to a specified minimal level, usually prescribed to be a fixed percentage of the value of the insured property. Failure of the insured to insure to that level results in a penalty in payout equal to the amount deficient.
Under a HUD program, an eligible multifamily lender who is permitted to conduct the processing of multifamily projects from initial application through loan closing.

terms.term: Collaborate on CD Data and Update LOS
terms.definition: The process of collecting and confirming both internally and with third parties, the data that will be used to produce a Closing Disclosure (CD) while updating the Lender's system of record and/or Loan Origination System (LOS).
Process of reconciling the loan fees with the Settlement Agent to ensure accuracy of the final Closing Disclosure (CD).

Process of collecting and confirming data both internally and with third parties that will be used to produce a Closing Disclosure (CD) for the Borrower and the Uniform Closing Dataset (UCD) for GSE delivery.
Property pledged as security for a debt, for example, mortgaged real estate.
Specifies to whom the loan has been pledged as collateral.
When true, indicates the collateral property meets the acreage, use, and occupancy requirements set forth under the homestead exemption laws of the state in which the property is located.
The process by which a property's price is determined.
A value from a MISMO defined list that identifies the source used to obtain the value of the underlying collateral for the loan if the value does not come from an appraisal.

terms.term: Collateral Value Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Collateral Value Source Type.
The instrument that is actually delivered in fulfillment of the Chicago Board of Trade GNMA-CDR. Similar to warehouse receipts used for agricultural commodities.

Mortgage-backed security where payments on the underlying collateral are partitioned to provide for different maturity classes, called tranches. Investors choose to buy one or more tranches, with each tranche representing a different maturity. Investors receive payments of interest or principal prioritized according to tranche.
Process of obtaining Loan Application information from the Borrower(s).
The process of collecting loan-level data required for HMDA reporting, typically from multiple systems, depending on the Lender's or Servicer's business model.
Process of collaborating with appropriate parties to retrieve outstanding documents required for loan servicing.
The dollar amount of the collected other funds.
The percentage of the collected other funds.
Identifies the type of other funds not included in down payment or closing costs.

terms.term: Collected Other Fund Purpose Type Other Description
terms.definition: Used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Collected Other Fund Purpose Type.
The servicing procedure followed to bring a delinquent mortgage current and to file the required notices to begin foreclosure when necessary.
The date on which the collection contact was made.
The date and time that the collection contact was started based upon the time zone at the recipient contact location.
A unique identifier of the collection contact method. The party assigning the identifier can be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the method used to make contact with the party in a collection effort.

terms.term: Collection Contact Method Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Collection Contact Method Type.
When true, indicates that the collection contact was considered to be productive by the servicer or investor and results in an attempt to solve the delinquency.
A free-form text field capturing information conveyed to or from the borrower or authorized agent during the collection contact.

A document the collection officer uses to record all collections related to the Single Family Property Disposition Program (Section 204(g)). The document provides the initial point of an audit trail regarding all collections. Form HUD-235 (5/89).

The form used by a mortgage servicer in reporting collection from mortgagors, including payments in full, repayment of advances, tax and insurance funds for foreclosed mortgages and any other items not remitted as regular installment payments.
An act that indicates good title, but in fact contains some defect.
The principal balance of all mortgages on the property (including second and third trusts) divided by the value of the property.

terms.term: Combined LTV Ratio Considered In Decision Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the combined LTV ratio was used in the risk assessment or approval decision for a loan application.

The result of dividing the combined unpaid principal balance (UPB) amounts of the first and all subordinate mortgages, excluding undrawn home equity lines of credit amounts, by the value of the subject property.
In retail leasing, where a lease becomes effective when signed but rent payments do not begin until occupancy or opening of business.
Focused on real estate finance transactions related to the origination, sale, and servicing of multifamily dwellings, office buildings, and other non-residential development projects.
Short-term, negotiable, unsecured notes of highly reputable business firms.

Office buildings, shopping centers, apartment buildings and other property which is utilized for the production of income rather than as residences. If residential real estate has more than four units it is considered commercial real estate.
Fair, proper, just or suitable under generally accepted business (commercial) standards or circumstances.
Combining funds (such as escrows) into one account that should be accounted for and deposited into separate accounts.
An agent's compensation for negotiating a real estate or loan transaction, often expressed as a percentage of the selling price.
HUD's estimate of the fair market value of a property in foreclosure. Mortgagees must bid the CAFMV at the foreclosure sale to reserve the option to retain or convey the property to HUD.

An agreement, often in writing, between a lender and a borrower, to loan money at a future date, subject to specified conditions. In secondary marketing, an agreement, in writing, between a lender and an investor to buy and sell mortgages under specific terms.

An agreement by a lender to provide long-term financing to a builder, secured by an existing proposed building. The commitment usually provides for the substitution of a to-be-approved owner/occupant at a higher loan amount than committed to the builder.
The number of days after the commitment issuance, during which the commitment is effective, and the closing can take place.

Any fee paid by a potential borrower to a potential lender for the lender's promise to loan money at a specified date in the future. The lender may or may not expect to fund the commitment. In secondary marketing, a fee paid by the loan seller to the investor in return for the investor's promise to purchase a loan or package of loans at a future date.
An area owned by the owners or tenants of a complex or subdivision, for the common use of residents.
Expenses associated with the maintenance of the common areas.
Multiple ownership of an apartment in which each owner is a tenant-in-common.
A group composed of property owners that serves to protect and maintain a neighborhood or commonly owned properties.

Under Title 1 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, eight former categorical grant and loan programs were replaced by a system of unified block grants under which communities of over 50,000 people are entitled to receive funding, while other communities may apply for discretionary funding. Its purpose is to encourage more broadly conceived community development projects and expand housing opportunities for low- and moderate-income persons.

One of Fannie Mae's primary tools for neighborhood and community revitalization, the CHIML is designed for the low- to moderate-income homebuyer or homeowner who wishes to purchase or refinance a home that needs modest, rather than substantial, repairs.
Indicates that the property is located in a community land trust.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that classifies the community lending product or affordable lending product associated with the loan.

terms.term: Community Lending Product Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Community Lending Product Type.
Community of Practice. A COP represents the business or technology interests of an industry segment and is made up of subject matter experts for that particular segment of the industry.
In some states, a form of ownership under which property acquired during a marriage is presumed to be owned jointly unless acquired as separate property of either spouse.
When true, indicates the property is located in a community property state.
When true, indicates that the borrower lives in a community property state.
Federal legislation which requires every financial institution to help meet the credit needs of its entire community, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.

terms.term: Community Reinvestment Act Delineated Community Indicator
terms.definition: Indicates that the property is in an area defined by the Community Reinvestment Act.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that classifies the payment structure of the community second lending product associated with the loan.

terms.term: Community Seconds Repayment Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Community Seconds Repayment Type.
A shopping center with a gross leasable area of 100,000 to 300,000 square feet and classified between the smaller neighborhood center and the larger regional center.
The dollar amount of the adjustment associated with the identified Comparable Adjustment Type.
A free-form text field used to further describe a property feature which is identified in the Comparable Adjustment Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents an element of comparison between the subject property and comparable property.
A free-form text field used to capture additional information when other is selected for Comparable Price Adjustment Type.
A free-form text field used to describe the source of information for the comparable property.
Indicates whether the comparable property has prior sales history.
Identifies the positional location on the appraisal form in which the comparable appears.
Text comments about the listing information.

terms.term: Comparable Listings Price Range High Amount
terms.definition: Specifies the high listing value in the range of values within the group of comparable listing properties researched.

terms.term: Comparable Listings Price Range Low Amount
terms.definition: Specifies the low listing value in the range of values within the group of comparable listing properties researched.
Specifies the total number of comparable property listings researched.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the comparable property used in the application of the Sales Comparison approach to property valuation.
