The ratio of interest to the actual face value of the investment instrument.
Indicates that the property is currently listed for sale in MLS.
Specifies the order in which unscheduled principal payments are applied relative to the scheduled payment.

Unique identifier according to the standards set by Committee on Uniform Security Identification Practices. The CUSIP is registered with the SEC and the Federal Reserve.
Bank accounts for the deposit of funds belonging to others.
Usually a commercial bank which holds for safekeeping mortgages and related documents backing a mortgage-backed security. Custodians may be required to examine and certify documents.

Responsibility for a property, as when the mortgagee turns a foreclosed property over to VA. A specialized VA term, custody may, but does not necessarily, include the legal right to physical possession of the property.

Verifies the identity of any person seeking to open an account; maintains records of the information used to verify the person's identity; and determines whether the person appears on any lists of known or suspected terrorists. AKA: U.S. Patriot Act, Important Applicant Information.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains instructions and requirements pertaining to any refunds to the borrowers.
The date up to which loan collections are included in remittances to investors.
A period of time such as when the economy is growing or when it is in a recession.
The maximum number of points a contract is allowed to rise above or fall below the previous day's settlement price, at which point all trading stops for the day.
The timely and reliable access to and use of information or information systems.

A systematic error that causes a deviation from the expected or true values in the data. It can lead to an inaccurate or unfair representation of reality and often stems from two main sources: 1)Data: Bias can arise from the way data is collected, processed, or used. For example, if a dataset is not representative of the population it’s meant to reflect, it can introduce bias into the analysis 2)Human Element: Bias can also come from the individuals who collect, analyze, or interpret the data. Personal beliefs, assumptions, or errors can inadvertently affect the outcomes of data-driven processes
An atomic unit of data that has precise meaning or precise semantics.
An abbreviation for Data Encryption Standard and may include a 56-key or 128-key symmetric and asymmetric encryption methods.
A value from a MISMO-prescribed list that specifies the conversion method used to describe the data with respect to the view.

terms.term: Data Format Conversion Type Other Description

A free-form text field used to describe a standard pattern for presenting a data field in the view.

The date the specified value for the data item becomes effective.
The date the value for the specified data item is no longer effective.

A record of the data life cycle that includes the data's origins and where it moves over time.
An analytical process that attempts to find correlations or patterns in large data sets for the purpose of data or knowledge discovery.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the reason a specific data point is not included in the message.

A MERS eRegistry Request that includes a Digital Signature and Registration data. (No eNote is presented at Registration).
The degree to which data is fit for a given business process or operation.
The effective as of reporting date of the data in the file.

Specifies the data file version.
Identifies the type of data file.

An instrument, provided by the title company, indicating that no liens have been placed on the property since its original issuance of the title insurance policy, or since any prior date-down endorsement.

terms.term: Day Lighting Energy Efficiency Item Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Day Lighting Efficient Item.
The total number of days on the property has been on the market from the last material status date to the time listing selected for the valuation.

terms.term: Days Since End Of Prior Workout Count
terms.definition: A count of the number of days since a prior workout. This is the difference between the current date and the last status date of the prior workout.

terms.term: Days To FHA MI Eligibility Count
terms.definition: Specifies the number of days in which the borrower will be determined to be eligible for insurance under the National Housing Act.
The number of days between the current date and the estimated or scheduled foreclosure sale day.
Doing Business As
An unstructured name that identifies an alias under which a business entity operates.
The date and time the Deal Comment was made or entered.
A free-form text field describing the source of the Deal Comment.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains the text of the Deal Comment.
The dollar amount associated with the Deal Set Expense Type.
Specifies the type of expense for reimbursed tasks or services performed.

terms.term: Deal Set Expense Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Deal Set Expense Type.
The dollar amount associated with the Deal Set Income Type.
Specifies the type of income or fee that may be received for services rendered.

terms.term: Deal Set Income Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Deal Set Income Type.
An investment banker or firm in the business of buying and selling mortgage-backed securities not as an agent, but as a principal. Unlike brokers, dealers hold inventories of securities.
Confirms the date, location and cause of the death of a person. Issued by a government official.
An interest-bearing bond issued against the general credit of a corporation or government organization, with no specific pledge of assets.

A property policy extension of coverage which grants coverage for the expense of removing debris caused by damage to property by an insured peril. Property should be defined as both insured and uninsured.
Money loaned at an agreed interest rate for a fixed term of years; distinguished from equity capital, which is money invested by owners (shareholders) for use in business operations.

terms.term: Debt Collection Restriction Request Acknowledgment Date
terms.definition: The date the servicer acknowledged receipt of the request from the borrower to restrict collection contacts.

terms.term: Debt Collection Restriction Request Receipt Date
terms.definition: The date the servicer received a request from the borrower to restrict collection contacts.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that qualifies a request by a consumer to the servicer or debt collector to restrict or limit debt collections per the Fair Debt Collection Practice Act (FDCPA).

terms.term: Debt Collection Restriction Request Type Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Debt Collection Restriction Request Type.

terms.term: Debt Collection Restriction Request Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Debt Collection Restriction Request Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the servicer's response to the borrower's debt collection restriction request.

terms.term: Debt Collector Restriction Response Type Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Debt Collector Restriction Response Type.

terms.term: Debt Collector Restriction Response Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Debt Collector Restriction Response Type.
A ratio of effective annual net income to annual principal and interest payments. Also called debt service coverage.
A borrower's periodic mortgage payments comprised of principal and/or interest on the unpaid mortgage balance.
A factor that, when multiplied by the original loan amount, yields the annual debt service payment (principal plus interest) required to amortize a loan.
A ratio of effective annual net operating income to annual principal and/or interest payments. Also called "debt service coverage."
The lesser of the lease amount or market rent on a rental property compared to the housing expense of principal and interest, taxes, insurance and homeowners association assessment.
Relationship of a borrower's monthly payment obligation on long-term debts divided by gross monthly income, expressed as a percentage. Also called the "bottom ratio."
The proportion of capital borrowed to the amount of capital invested out-of-pocket or obtained through the sale of common stock. Also called "leverage ratio."

A written statement from the servicer to the borrower or their authorized agent, outlining the actions of the debtor is entitled by law to take or refuse to take when a debt is in collection. AKA: Statement of Rights
A free-form text field capturing explanations to a “yes” answer to any declaration on the loan application.
Identifies the particular question asked in the declarations section of the loan application. Used in conjunction with the text field to capture additional information.
A free-form text field used to describe the kind of declaration if Other is selected as the Declaration Explanation Type.

A method of depreciation by which each year's depreciation is a percentage of the reduced basis of the asset. In general, the declining balance rate may be 200%, 150%, or 125% of straight-line depreciation.
In a judicial foreclosure, the court decree of judgment that establishes the amount of the mortgage debt and orders the property sold to satisfy the debt.
The granting of land by the owner for some public use and its acceptance for such use by authorized public officials.
The document by which title to real property is transferred or conveyed from one party to another.

terms.term: Deed In Lieu Offer Expiration Date
terms.definition: The latest date that the deed in lieu agreement may be signed. The expiration date of the offer to accept a deed in lieu.
The date that the deed in lieu of foreclosure was recorded with the local government office.

terms.term: Deed In Lieu Recording Submission Date
terms.definition: The date that the deed in lieu of foreclosure was submitted for recordation with the local government office.
The date on which the deed in lieu agreement was signed.

terms.term: Deed In Lieu Transition Duration Type
terms.definition: The measure of time during which the borrower will remain in the property after a Deed In Lieu is completed. Duration is determined based on trading party policy guidelines.
The transfer of a legal title from the trustee to the trustor (the borrower) after the trust deed is paid in full.

A type of security instrument in which the borrower conveys title to real property to a third party (trustee) to be held in trust as security for the lender, with the provision that the trustee shall reconvey the title upon the payment of the debt and, conversely, will sell the land and pay the debt in the event of a default by the borrower. Also see MORTGAGE.
When true, indicates the party is a Trustee as identified on a Deed of Trust.
A condition placed in a deed limiting or restricting the use of the real property.
If true, indicates that the deed has associated restrictions.
A legally enforceable restriction recorded in the public record on land that supersedes ownership rights.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Deed Restriction Type.
A deed given by a borrower/mortgagor to a lender/mortgagee to satisfy a debt and avoid foreclosure.

A type of synthetic media where a person's face or body is digitally altered to appear as someone else, typically used maliciously or to spread false information. The technology leverages tools and techniques from machine learning and artificial intelligence, including facial recognition algorithms and artificial neural networks.
The nonpayment of a mortgage or other loan in accordance with the terms as specified in the note.

terms.term: Default Acknowledgment Of Cash Advance Against Non Homestead Property Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates an Acknowledgement for Non Homestead Property cash advance on default section of the security instrument.
Application Fees disclosed in the default section of the security instrument.
The preparation fee amount disclosed in the default section of the security instrument.
The interest rate stipulated by certain mortgage documents which is triggered by a breach or nonperformance of the terms of a note, the covenants of a mortgage, or the terms of other loan documents.

terms.term: Default Lending Institution Post Office Box Identifier
terms.definition: Lenders Post Office Box included in the default section of the security instrument.

A letter sent to the borrower indicating that a breach or nonperformance of the terms of a note, the covenants of a mortgage or the terms of other loan documents has occurred. This letter also advises the borrower of the rights of the lender under the note/mortgage and requires that the default be cured.

The occupancy level at which the effective gross income from an income-producing property is insufficient to pay operating expenses and debt service, thus creating the risk of default. The ratio is calculated by dividing the effective gross income into operating expenses plus debt service.
Indicates the default status of a particular loan.
Description of the current status of the loan payments when the type is "Other".
Indicates whether the loan experienced a first payment default.
A provision in a mortgage which allows the debtor to reclaim property that has been foreclosed, if certain conditions are met.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that identifies a specific component on the property where the defect, damage or deficiency has been observed.

terms.term: Defect Component Label Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Defect Component Label Type.

terms.term: Defect Cost To Repair Total Amount
terms.definition: The estimated total cost of the repairs to be performed on the property.

terms.term: Defect Item Affects Soundness Structural Integrity Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the identified defect, damage, or deficiency affects the soundness and/or the structural integrity of the improvement.
A free-form text field describing the defect, damage or deficiency.

terms.term: Defect Item Estimated Cost To Repair Amount
terms.definition: The estimated dollar amount to repair the identified defect, damage or deficiency.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that identifies the explicit location of the defect, damage or deficiency.

terms.term: Defect Item Location Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Defect Item Location Type.

terms.term: Defect Item Recommended Action Completed Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the defect, damage or deficiency has been resolved or satisfied.

terms.term: Defect Item Recommended Action Completion Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field describing the completion status and details of the resolution.

terms.term: Defect Item Recommended Action Inspection Date
terms.definition: The date that the defect, damage or deficiency item has been inspected.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the recommended action for the identified defect, damage or deficiency.

terms.term: Defect Item Recommended Action Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Defect Item Recommended Action Type.
An encumbrance on a title that is made a part of the public record. Some recorded defects are judgments, mortgages, other liens or easements.
The amount of borrower corporate advances deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven.
The amount of the escrow balance deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven.
Accrued Uncollected Interest.

terms.term: Deferred Interest Balance Amount Total Amount
terms.definition: Provides a arithmetic total of the Deferred Interest Balance Amount data items within the Loan container in this data set.
Indicates that any accumulated deferred interest is excluded from the principal balance when a new payment is calculated for an ARM loan with negative amortization.

Postponed, infrequent, or inadequate maintenance practices on a building or property, often resulting in physical depreciation and loss of value. Deferred maintenance can be an indicator of inadequate cash flow or lack of pride in the property. Also called "curable depreciation."
The amount of all other funds deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven. This may include late charges and fees.
For loans allowing deferred payments, this is the amount of the loan that is to be paid, in part or in full, at a later date.
For loans allowing deferred payments, this is the date that payments are due to resume.
The amount of principal or amounts capitalized to principal deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven.
The difference between the balance outstanding on a loan and proceeds from the sale of the loan collateral.
A court order to pay the balance owed on a loan if the proceeds from the sale of the security are insufficient to pay off the loan.
When true, indicates that upon the foreclosure sale completion deficiency rights against the borrowers are preserved.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of value used for this collateral valuation product.

terms.term: Definition Of Value Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Definition Of Value Type.
In mortgage securities, the time elapsed from receipt of mortgage payments from borrowers to remittance of pass-through cash flows to investors.
The delegation of underwriting authority from an investor or agency to the lender.
When true, indicates that the underwriting authority on a loan is delegated to the loan originator based on disclosed guidelines.

A Member of the MERS eRegistry that is authorized by the Controller to perform certain MERS eRegistry transactions on the Controller's behalf. The DT can initiate registrations and transfers of Control, but may not initiate change status transactions, or change data transactions except to remove themselves as DT. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Failure of a borrower to make timely payments specified under a loan agreement.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies how delinquency is calculated on a loan.

terms.term: Delinquency Calculation Method Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Delinquency Calculation Method Type.
The date that the delinquency of the loan started, could be at day 16 or day 30 depending on the Investor requirements.
The ratio of number of past due loans to total number of loans serviced.

terms.term: Delinquency Reporting Property Overall Condition Type
terms.definition: Used to report the overall condition of the property associated with this loan as identified through a property inspection or through direct contact with Borrower, Neighbors, Real Estate Agent, etc.

terms.term: Delinquency Reporting Property Overall Condition Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the data source type if Other is selected as the Delinquency Reporting Property Overall Condition Type.
A delinquent payment is an unpaid payment. This is a count of the currently unpaid payments.

terms.term: Delinquent Payments Over Past Twelve Months Count
terms.definition: The number of times during the past twelve months that the payment on the subject loan was delinquent.
Process of delivering an accurate Closing Disclosure (CD) to the Borrower via mail, electronically, or in person.
Process of securely delivering the closing documents package electronically, or as an exception in paper, to the Settlement Agent.

terms.term: Deliver Data from LOS to Doc Prep Provider
terms.definition: Process of delivering data from the loan origination system to the document preparation system when disparate systems are used to generate the closing documents package.
Process of delivering collateral documents to a Warehouse Bank (or its Document Custodian) to secure interim financing until the mortgage is sold to a permanent investor.
Process of delivering (pre-closing) an accurate and timely Closing Disclosure (CD) to the Borrower via mail, electronically, or in person meeting regulatory requirements.

terms.term: Deliver Loan to Purchaser or Guarantor
terms.definition: Process of transmitting mortgage loan data from the Loan Seller to the Purchaser or Guarantor to meet the contractual obligations of the purchase or guaranty agreement.
In mortgage banking, the physical transfer of loan documents to an investor or agent in conformance with the commitment.
The contracted date when the actual payment of funds and delivery of mortgage-backed securities occurs.
A free-form field used to describe sending or receipt of a supporting record set.
The date and time associated with sending of a supporting record set.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the means of delivery of the supporting record set.
A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Delivery Method Type.
A free-form text field used to capture the enumeration when Other is selected for Supporting Record Set Delivery Method Type.
The calendar month during which a given contract expires and delivery can be made; also called expiration month.

terms.term: Delivery Point Bar Code Check Value
terms.definition: A check digit calculated using the MOD 10 method on the total of all 10 digits that make up the bar code for use in the Delivery Point Bar Code (DPBC). The DPBC is an 11 digit (plus check digit) barcode, containing the ZIP Code, ZIP+4 Code, and the delivery point code. This is the predominant barcode in use currently (as of 2008), and it enables the Postal Service to sort mail into delivery point (address) sequence.

A code maintained by the USPS representing a delivery point (DP) which is a single mailbox or other place at which mail is delivered. This may be appended to the combination of zip code and zip+4 code for the purposes of creating a barcode.
The date and time associated with the receipt of a supporting record set.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the initial disposition of the delivery of the supporting record set.

terms.term: Delivery Received Status Type Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Delivery Event Status Type.

terms.term: Delivery Received Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture the enumeration when Other is selected for Delivery Event Status Type.

terms.term: Delivery To Lender Of Electronically Signed Documents Text
terms.definition: A free-form alphanumeric string which contains the lender's instructions and requirements for delivery of documents that have been electronically executed.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying a delivery as it moves through a carrier system to its destination.
The unit change in the price of an option (the premium) for a unit change in the price of the underlying security.
Demand deposits go into a demand deposit account, which is similar to a checking account. The demand deposit funds are liquid and may be withdrawn at any time without prior notice.
When true, indicates that the loan has a demand feature.

Correspondence sent to the borrower indicating that unless the loan is made current within a certain time frame, the lender can, by virtue of a default, declare the entire principal balance outstanding as well as all interest due under the note to be due and payable.
A note or mortgage that the lender can call due at any time and without prior notice.
The study of the characteristics of human populations such as size, growth, density, distribution and vital statistics. Also known as demographics.

Coverage extended to cover the cost of demolishing property damaged by an insured peril. Policies may be extended to cover the cost of demolishing undamaged property made necessary by a bylaw, court order, etc.
The ratio between total land area and the number of residential or commercial structures placed upon it. Local ordinances usually regulate density.

terms.term: Department Of Housing And Urban Development (HUD)
terms.definition: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development is a federal agency established in 1965 to address housing needs, improve communities, and enforce fair housing laws, ensuring equal access to housing and community-based employment opportunities.

A cabinet-level agency of the federal government. The Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944 authorized the agency to administer a variety of benefit programs designed to facilitate the adjustment of returning veterans to civilian life. Among the benefit programs is the VA Home Loan Guaranty program, which encourages mortgage lenders to offer long-term, low down payment financing to eligible veterans by partially guaranteeing the lender against loss upon foreclosure.
The number of years of age of a borrower's dependent.
The total number of borrower's dependents.
A sum of money given to (1) bind a sale of real estate or (2) assure payment or an advance of funds in the processing of a loan. Also called earnest money.
A form used to acknowledge the acceptance of the earnest money that binds an offer to purchase real property.
Tangible personal property or real property used in business or held for the production of income with a determinable useful life of more than one year.
The capital amount on which depreciation deductions are calculated.
The total amount of depreciated cost for all dwellings on the subject property.
The total amount of depreciated cost for all outbuildings on the subject property.
A decline in value of a building or other real estate improvement, resulting from age, physical wear and economic or functional obsolescence. This figure is deducted annually from net income.

The accounting charge made to allow for the fact that an asset may become economically obsolete before complete physical deterioration. The purpose is to write off the original cost by distributing it over the estimated useful life of the asset. It appears in the profit and loss statement and the balance sheet.
This dollar amount of the depreciation due to external factors impacting this improvement (e.g. economic trends, external obsolescence).
A portion of 100 that represents the percent of depreciation applied due to external factors impacting this improvement.
The dollar amount of the depreciation due this improvement's style, design and/or functional utility becoming outdated.
A portion of 100 that represents the percent of depreciation applied to this improvement due to style, design and/or functional utility becoming outdated.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the method used to derive depreciated building value.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Depreciation Method Type.
The dollar amount of the depreciation due to wear and tear of this improvement.
A portion of 100 that represents the percent of physical depreciation applied to this improvement for wear and tear.
The total amount of accumulated monetary loss in value for the reproduction or replacement cost of this improvement from all causes of depreciation.
Investments whose returns derive from the change in value of other securities or indexes, such as bonds, interest rates or stocks.
The process of deriving the data needed for the HMDA Loan Application Register (LAR).
To convey the DU recommendation.
Provides a more detailed description of the Credit Business Type.

terms.term: Detail Credit Business Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Detail Credit Business Type.
Process of determining how to sell the loan at the best available net price while giving consideration to effective trade execution and potential impact on investor relationships.

The process of determining eligibility criteria for digital mortgages at a transaction level. This includes state, county, and counterparty requirements for eNotes, eRecording, and electronic notarization including Remote Online Notarization (RON).

terms.term: Determine Lien Position and Relative Ownership
terms.definition: The process of determining the loan's lien position regarding the property. This may be performed multiple times within the Default Management process.
Process of validating loan limit(s) based on property location (state and county) and property type.
Process in which the Lender determines what loan products to offer based on market conditions, business strategy, and investor demand.
A person or entity who prepares raw land for building sites or rehabilitates existing buildings.
A short-term loan advanced before a construction loan, used by developers to acquire land and install basic utilities such as roads, sewers and water supply systems.

1) Development Process Document Only: The formal process, described in detail in this document, by which MISMO develops, tests, approves, and publishes its MISMO Products. 2) Policies and Procedures Only: The formal process, described in detail in the Development Process document, by which MISMO develops, tests, approves, and publishes its MISMO Products. 3) MBA Glossary: The process through which development projects are conceived, initiated, analyzed, financed, designed, built and managed.
The rights a landholder sells to improve a property or enhance the use of said property.
A free-form text field used to describe the phase or completion or incomplete status of the project.
Number of phases that exist in the project.

In a mortgage-backed security, the difference between the MBS security rate and the coupon rates of the underlying mortgages. The issuer retains the differential to pay for servicing costs and the guarantee.

An electronic file that contains the Public Key, the name of the certificate holder (which may be either a person or a system name), and a date range during which the certificate can be considered valid as well as the Digital Signature of a Certificate Authority for Authentication, which provides assurance that the Public Key belongs to the entity to which the certificate was issued. A Digital Certificate may also be referred to as a Public Key Certificate.

A mortgage loan where the process of gathering borrower qualifying information is performed in an automated and streamlined fashion such as through a borrower portal. Some of the loan documents, such as the loan application, may be created, accessed, presented, executed, transferred and stored electronically. A digital mortgage may or may not result in an eClosing.

A form of an Electronic Signature that is the result of calculating a Hash Value and encrypting with a Private Key and attaching to an Electronic Record so that, at a later date, there can be verification that the original content of the Electronic Record has not changed. A Digital Signature can also provide evidence of the authenticity of the Electronic Signature and the Electronic Record. Digital signatures in the mortgage banking industry are also known as Tamper Seals, Tamper seal Signatures, and Tamper Evident Signatures.
The hash value from the digital signature used to tamper-seal a document. It is included here to enable data integrity checking.
An asymmetric encryption transformation used to approve or sign an electronic record or detect alteration of an electronic record.

A handwritten signature that is converted upon execution into an electronic form. This is usually performed with a pen and a graphics drawing tablet used for sketching new images or tracing old ones. The user makes contact with the tablet with a pen or puck (mistakenly called a mouse) that is either wireless or connected to the tablet by a wire. For sketching, the user draws with the pen or puck and the screen cursor "draws" a corresponding image. This technology alone will not encrypt a document once signed. AKA Image Signature.
Labor and materials costs of construction, excluding overhead.
A HUD program that enables an eligible single-family lender to conduct the processing and closing of FHA single-family loan applications without HUD's prior review.
Method of payment wherein a check or other form of consideration is delivered directly to the investor's or servicer's place of business.
Member of the MISMO Board of Directors

terms.term: Directors And Officers Liability Insurance (D and O Liability Insurance)
terms.definition: Insurance that protects both a corporation and its key employees. The standard D & O policy usually includes corporate reimbursement, which covers expenses insured by the directors and officers for legal costs and judgments indemnified by the corporation, and personal coverage, which protects individual officers and directors against claims not indemnified.
When true, indicates at least one client/borrower or member of the household is disabled.
When true, indicates there is at least one disabled dependent in the household.
A deductible that disappears as the loss gets larger, i.e., a $500 deductible will not apply to losses over $10,000.
A free form description of the area affected by the disaster.
The date on which the disaster was declared by the government.
Indicates that the property is damaged as a result of a natural disaster, such as a hurricane, tornado, or earthquake.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a feature added to or a modification made to the property which is designed to prevent or reduce the impacts and risks of hazards caused by natural disasters.

terms.term: Disaster Mitigation Feature Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Disaster Mitigation Feature Type.
When true, indicates the potential client/borrower was referred to a housing counseling agency for mortgage or rental assistance after a natural disaster.
A value from a MISMO defined list that specifies the type of disaster that has affected the area.
A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Disaster Type.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Disaster Type.
The date the loan funds are disbursed to the borrower or another party on the borrower's behalf.
Actual payment of monies. Used to describe construction loan draws.
The value of the fully indexed interest rate, expressed as a percent, which must be disclosed to the borrower for adjustable rate mortgages.
The value of the financial index, expressed as a percent, used to calculate the Disclosed Fully Indexed Interest Rate that must be disclosed to the borrower for adjustable rate mortgages.

The number of percentage points to be added to the Disclosed Index Rate Percent to arrive at the Disclosed Fully Indexed Interest Rate that must be disclosed to the borrower for adjustable rate mortgages.
Information relevant to specific transactions that is required by law.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains a comment concerning the reason for disclosure or redisclosure.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the method or service used to deliver the disclosure documents to the borrower.

terms.term: Disclosure Delivery Method Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Disclosure Delivery Method Type.
An alphanumeric string identifying a specific version of the disclosure document.
The date the disclosure is due to be delivered to the borrower.
A value from a prescribed list that defines the point in time of the mortgage transaction when the disclosure was issued.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the version or timing status of the issued disclosure.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Disclosure Issuance Type.
The date the disclosure was mailed or delivered to the borrower as reflected on a single instance of the disclosure document.
A free-form text field describing the reason for disclosure or redisclosure.
The date the event occurred or inaccurate, changed, or new information specific to the borrower or loan transaction was provided.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that categorizes the reason for disclosure or redisclosure.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Disclosure Reason Type.
The date the borrower received the disclosure.
The process in which the lender discontinues credit file monitoring.

In loan originations, a discount refers to an amount withheld from loan proceeds by a lender. In secondary market sales, a discount is the amount by which the sale price of a note is less than its face value. In both instances, the purpose of a discount is to adjust the yield upward, either in lieu of interest or in addition to interest. The rate or amount of discount depends on money market conditions, the credit of the borrower and the rate or terms of the note.
Amount payable to the lending institution by the borrower or seller to increase the lender's effective yield. One point is equal to 1% of the loan.
The total dollar amount estimated or paid as discount points for this loan product.

The rate of return used to convert expected discounted cash-flow analysis (DCF): Method of applying an appropriate discount to cash to be received in the future to arrive at the present value of those future earnings.
See DISCOUNTED CASH-FLOW ANALYSIS.
Non Personally Identifiable Data used for research or under evaluation for use in the organization.
The date a client was referred for assistance after reporting they were a victim of discrimination.
A free-form text field that provides the name of the organiziation a client was referred to for assistance after reporting they were a victim of discrimination.
The flow of funds out of banks and savings institutions into short-term investments on which interest rates are higher.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of dismissal the court has made to end the litigated matter.
A free-form text field that provides a human-readable, display-ready representation for the corresponding enumerated value.

A free-form text field that identifies the specific region where the time value applies. Trading partners should agree on what time zone name values they will use. The recommended time zone name values should be based on the TZ database, also known as the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) timezone database.
To obtain physical possession of property by due process of law.
Indicates that the response is a result of a dispute.
The reason that a loan does not qualify for a particular product.
A measurement that specifies the approximate distance from the property to the environmental condition. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Linear Unit Of Measure Type.

Term that denotes property in trouble due to one of several reasons, such as: cost overrun, insufficient income, poor management or any other conditions which affect the mortgagor's ability to repay the loan on a timely basis.

An individual or organization who makes, has made, uses, distributes, sells, offers for sale, imports, modifies, reproduces, publishes, publicly performs, displays, or makes derivative works using, or that are compliant with, a MISMO Product where the individual or organization distributes or in any way provides the MISMO Product (including derivative and compliant works) to any person or entity outside of its own organization, whether or not a fee is received therefore.
To release an interest one has in property.

A stockholder's share of profits of a corporation. An insurance dividend is not a true dividend but a return of premium. Dividends from a savings and loan association, credit union passbook account or certificate are interest, and are not considered dividends.
Establishes the terms of the divorce. Provided by a court or legal authority. AKA: Final Judgment (divorce), Abridgment of Judgment (divorce).
Financial institution that contracts with a lender to maintain custody of certain mortgage documents in the lender's or investor's behalf.
Describes certification that a document has been delivered to the borrower.
Confirms that an appraisal report has been delivered, describes how delivered, to whom and when.
The party in whose name the documents were drawn.
The unique appraisal identifier generated by the Uniform Collateral Data Portal (UCDP). Also referred to as 'Doc File ID'.

A code provided by agreement between trading partners to identify the form/template contributor. The CodeOwnerURI attribute is used to disambiguate, for example between two cities having the same name but located in different states.
A free-form text description of the form/template contributor as identified by the Document Form Contributor Code.

terms.term: Document Form Issuing Entity Name Type
terms.definition: Identifies the organization that defined the document form/template.

terms.term: Document Form Issuing Entity Name Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Document Form Issuing Entity Name Type.

terms.term: Document Form Issuing Entity Number Identifier
terms.definition: The identifier that the issuer assigned to the document form/template. The identifier normally does not include the issuer identifier unless the document is generally known by that identifier.

terms.term: Document Form Issuing Entity Version Identifier
terms.definition: The version identifier that the issuer assigned to the document form/template.
The name of the organization that made the form/template available. Example: D+H, Wolters Kluwer.
The identifier that the publisher assigned to the document form/template.
The version identifier that the publisher assigned to the document form/template.
An actual XML or SGML file that contains data.

The title that appears on the document view. The name or label that is used for this document. It may be the same as the Document Type. For example, a promissory may have the document name "Gold Star Customer Agreement."
When true, indicates that the fully executed, authoritative instance of this document is a negotiable instrument.
Defines the type of the document set that is being requested. Identifies if the documents requested are to be an opening or closing document package.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of document package. This defines what documents are included.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Document Package Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the manner in which the documents will be packaged for delivery, grouped as a single VIEW or as individual VIEWs.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Document Packaging Type.
The PeriodEndDate is used for the ending date of the period covered in the document.

The starting date of the period covered in the document. For documents that cover an exact period, e.g. a year or a year and month, only provide those portions of the date. For an IRS tax document this is the tax year on the document.
The date the closing documents were prepared.
A process or a system for producing fully populated paper or electronic documents. This may be accomplished in house, or through a third party service, or some combination.
When true, indicates that a notification email should be sent to the requestor.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying a document preparation request. This might be used where the transactions are asynchronous.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of action that should be performed for associated document preparation request data.

terms.term: Document Preparation Requested Action Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Document Preparation Requested Action Type.

A Document Profile is a concept developed by the MISMO eMortgage Workgroup to distinguish features and characteristics of the Version 3 SMART Doc. The four profiles accommodate different usage scenarios. Each profile includes and extends the previous one. 1. Basic: The document receiver only needs the view, information related to signatures if the document is signed and the document type or name. 2. Retrievable: The document receiver wants to access data from the document and there is not a requirement to automatically verify that the data matches what is presented in the viewable image. The data in the Retrievable profile may or may not include all of the information contained in the view. 3. Tamper Evident: The document receiver wants to verify the integrity of the document. 4. Verifiable: The document receiver wants to verify that the data matches the information contained in the view.
Describes whether the document must be delivered to the recorder and recorded by the recorder.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains instructions from the lender regarding the return of completed documents.

A document that expresses the sequence in which documents occur within a document set. The investor often dictates the document sequence to simplify document processing. A document set sometimes includes the DocumentSequence document itself. AKA: Documentation Order, Stacking Sheet.
An identifier for the current instance of DOCUMENT_SET. The party assigning the identifier should be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
A code used between trading partners to identify a use of the DOCUMENTS contained in the DOCUMENT_SET. The party assigning the identifier should be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
A free-form text description of the process or usage of the containing DOCUMENT_SET as identified by the Document Set Usage Code within the same DOCUMENT_SET_USAGE container.
When true, indicates that a signatory must execute a signature on the document.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents either a category of document or a category and sublevel of a document combined into a single enumeration.
Document Type Definition: defines the structure of an XML document. DTDs define the elements, attributes, and relationships between elements.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Document Type.
A code provided by agreement between trading partners in order to identify a process or usage of the containing DOCUMENT. The attribute CodeOwnerURI identifies the issuer of the code.
A free-form text description of the process or usage of the containing DOCUMENT as identified by the Document Usage Code within the same DOCUMENT_USAGE container.
A mark "stamped" onto a deed certifying the amount of transfer tax paid.
Identifies the state of the documentation associated with the loan.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Documentation State Type.
Repurchase agreement in which a security is sold with an agreement that a substantially similar security will be repurchased at a later date at a given price.

When true, indicates that the borrower is in a civil union, domestic partnership, or registered reciprocal beneficiary relationship recognized by the State in which he/she currently resides or where the property is located.

The two-character postal representation of the US state, US Territory, Canadian Province, Military APO FPO, or Territory in which the relationship with an individual who is not a legal spouse was formed.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies a borrower’s relationship with an individual who is not a legal spouse but who has real property rights similar to those of a legal spouse.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Domestic Relationship Type.
When an owner of property is given certain rights to use another's property.
The rights a widow has to her husband's real property at his death.

A portion of the sales price paid a seller by a buyer to close a sales transaction, with the understanding that the balance will be paid at settlement. Also, the difference between the sale price of real estate and the mortgage amount.
The dollar amount of funds supplied by a borrower for a down payment.
The total amount the borrower received for down payment assistance from all sources.
When true, indicates that the borrower has received down payment assistance.
Specifies the type of option used to facilitate the borrower's down payment.

terms.term: Down Payment Option Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Down Payment Option Type.

The Development Process Document is a procedures guide that outlines the process for developing, reviewing and approving MISMO Products created within the MISMO framework. It also outlines the roles, responsibilities, and interdependencies of the various participants (contributors, committees, staff, etc.) within the MISMO organization tasked with the maintenance and on-going development of the MISMO Products.

Disbursement of a portion of the loan proceeds, usually at a predetermined point in the construction or rehabilitation schedule, to pay for work already completed. The balance of the proceeds is retained until the next scheduled draw or until completion of the construction or rehabilitation work to protect the lender against the contractor's failure to complete the work as scheduled.
A document which authorizes a person to operate a motor vehicle on a public roadway. Evidences a person's identity and driver's license identifier.
Any advance of new funds to a mortgage banker for funding or purchasing mortgage loans where the collateral package is in the possession of the collateral agent and is free of lien or bailment.

Document Type Definition. A file that defines the "markup language" that will be used to describe the data. It defines and names the elements that can be used in the document, the order in which the elements can appear, the element attributes that can be used, and other document features. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Debt to Income
Date which the borrower must pay the interest and/or the principal and interest due on his or her mortgage, as stated in the note, as well as any escrow payment.

An examination by a purchaser of a servicing portfolio. Generally the reviewer will look at credit quality and underwriting of the loan collateral underlying the servicing rights; correctness and completeness of the loan documents; the seller's servicing practices and methodologies; and the accuracy of the portfolio offering document. As used here, a re-underwriting of the loan in line with the borrower's request to determine the feasibility of the request by the lender.
A provision appearing in a mortgage providing for the acceleration of a loan upon the placement of additional mortgage liens on collateral already pledged/mortgaged to a lender.

A clause in a mortgage stating that if the mortgagor sells, transfers or in any way encumbers the property, then the mortgagee has the right to implement an acceleration clause making the balance of the obligation due.
A single structure designed with two separate housing units.

Data records with the same Duplicate Group Identifier value have been identified as being duplicate records from different sources. Within a set of records that have the same Duplicate Group Identifier, one record is marked with a Primary Record Indicator set to "True", indicating that this record has been identified as the record out of the group that should be used for evaluation of credit. The remaining records in the group should have a Primary Record Indicator set to "False".
An estimate of the volatility or sensitivity of the market price of a bond to changes in interest rates; it measures the weighted average time until cash flow repayment.
Compulsion, pressure or coercion under protest.
The total number of structures on the property, excluding outbuildings, that contains a living unit.
When true, indicates that the exterior of the dwelling has defect(s), damage(s) or deficienc(ies).
Living quarters occupied, or intended for occupancy, by a household.
Development Work Group. A DWG produces a MISMO Product, or set of Products, as specified in its Charter.
Electronic (as in E Mortgage)
The ability to rapidly build and deploy applications and processes to meet constantly changing customer, partner, and supplier needs.

Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act. On June 30, 2000, Congress enacted this Act to facilitate the use of electronic records and signatures in interstate and foreign commerce by ensuring the validity and legal effect of contracts entered into electronically.
Situation in which a buyer is permitted to take possession of real property before closing.
A letter issued by HUD or a Direct Endorsement lender deemed as an approval for mortgage insurance on the permanent financing before the beginning of construction.
A deposit made to bind the conditions of a sale of real estate.
A right to the limited use or enjoyment of land held by another, including, for example, an interest in land to enable sewer or other utility lines to be laid, or to allow access to a property.
A free-form text field describing the easement and/or its impact on the value and marketability of the property.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a nonpossessory right to cross or otherwise use a portion of another property for a specified purpose (e.g. utility, driveway).
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Easement Type.

A term that represents the entire contents of e-documents produced with an electronic mortgage transaction. The eBinder can be opened only by authorized parties and is separated into eFolders to organize the eDocs.

An eClosing is the act of closing a mortgage loan electronically. This occurs through a secure environment(s) where one or more required closing documents are accessed, presented, and signed electronically.
The loss of the value of real estate due to changes outside the particular property affected, e.g., a decline in the neighborhood or change in zoning.
A general term indicating projects designed to strengthen an area's economy and employment base.
The estimated period of time during which a property can be used by its owner to produce income.

terms.term: Economic Or Commercial Real Estate Weakness
terms.definition: An area exhibiting poor occupancies, low rents, plant or military base closings or low sales and appraised values.
The rent that a property would bring if offered in the open market. Same as market rent; often differs from the contract rent.
The condition of the property based on its earning potential.

The entity whose role it is to ensure the secure and accurate storage and archival of eDocuments; e.g., the person or entity charged with maintaining the Authoritative Copy of the Transferable Record.
The secure transfer of data and/or documents created electronically from one entity to another. There is also a product and service from MERSCORP Holdings named eDelivery see MERS eDelivery.
A document that is created, accessed, presented, and/or signed electronically. An eDoc may be a paper document that is converted to an electronic form.
One or more advanced degrees that may be important to an establishment such as an educational institution. (MD, Ph.D., JD, Ed.D.).
For purposes of appraisal, the physical age given to a building based on its present condition, which may differ from its actual age.
A free-form text field describing the effective age of the structure.

terms.term: Effective Age Range High Years Count
terms.definition: The highest number in the structure's estimated age range based on its utility and physical wear and tear.

terms.term: Effective Age Range Low Years Count
terms.definition: The lowest number in the structure's estimated age range based on its utility and physical wear and tear.
The estimated age of a structure based on its utility and physical wear and tear.
Stabilized income after vacancy and bad debt allowances that a property is expected to generate.
Normal annual income, principally salary, that is regular, significant and stable.
The stabilized income (after vacancy and bad debt allowances) that a property is expected to generate.
The actual rate of return to the investor, considering commitment fees, loan points or other fees. Also called yield.

The rental income generated by a lease computed over the life of the lease and expressed as an annual dollar amount or annual dollar amount per square foot. This figure is typically computed as the aggregate rent to be paid under the lease net of any abated rent and allowances, divided by the term of the lease. However, there has been a trend toward computing effective rent more realistically by using a time-value-of-money calculation. In this latter approach, sometimes called the "equivalent level rent calculation," a market discount rate is applied to all cash flows from the lease to obtain a present value which is then reduced by the cost of any concessions or inducements paid to put the lease in place. The resultant net value is then converted to the equivalent level payment stream which would produce an equivalent net present value at that discount rate.
The annual return expressed as the face interest rate divided by the amount invested, used when a mortgage or other debt instrument is bought at a discount or premium.
When true, indicates that the property has obtained an efficiency rating.
An unstructured name that identifies the efficiency rating.
An unstructured name that identifies the organization providing the efficiency rating.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains the specific value of the rating score.
Represents the divider/tabs in the e-binder that separates, in an organized fashion, like parts of the electronic mortgage documentation.
To go out. This term is used with the word ingress (to go in) to describe the right of access to land.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the delivery method of electricity to the property. Also used in conjunction with a type of utility ownership.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Electricity Source Type.

Intercompany electronic exchange (between computers) of business documents in standard formats using the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) Accredited Standards Committee's (ASC) data standards.
When true, indicates the lender will permit the loan closing to leverage electronic notarization of the signatures of the parties to the transactions as part of the closing event.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains specific directions around the electronic notarization requirements to meet the lender's expectations.
When true, indicates the lender will permit the loan closing to take place either partially or entirely using electronic signatures.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains specific directions around the electronic signing requirements to meet the lender's expectations.
Establishes a repeatable direct deposit of funds into an account of a borrower. Used by servicing. AKA: EFT, Automatic Funds Transfer.

terms.term: Electronic Note Vault or eNote Vault
terms.definition: An Electronic Note Vault is a secure storage solution that meets the requirements of eSignature Laws. The concept is analogous to a paper note vault administered by a document custodian in the industry today.
Electronic Online Transactions.
A contract or other record created, generated, accessed, sent, communicated, received, or stored by electronic means.

Information within a notarized electronic record that confirms the notary public's name, jurisdiction, identifying number, and commission expiration date and generally corresponds to information in notary seals used on paper documents.

An action by a person to electronically apply an electronic sound, a symbol, or process attached to or logically associated with a record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record. Electronic signatures in MISMO SMART Docs may be a typed name (a Text Signature), a digitized image, such as a "picture" of a written signature created by a signing pad or by other means (an Image Signature), or a Digital Signature. A SMART Doc that contains a scanned or digitized version of an executed paper document has a "Wet" (handwritten) signature type.

Certifies elevation information necessary to ensure compliance with community floodplain management ordinances, to determine the proper insurance premium rate, and to support a request for a Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) or Letter of Map Revision based on fill (LOMR-F).
Number of elevators.

terms.term: Eligible For Lender Paid MI Indicator
terms.definition: Indicates that the mortgage loan is eligible for lender-paid MI.
An advanced method of developing a capitalization rate based on the proportion of an investment represented by debt and equity.
The number of email attempts to contact the borrower in the current month.

The XML compatible byte stream in the encoding of the EncodingType that when decoded is a resource of the MediaType using characters from the CharacterEncodingSetType. If a binary EncodingType is not used (e.g. "None" or "EscapedXML") then the CharacterEncodingSetType must be the same as that used for the XML instance document.
The right of government bodies, public utilities and public service corporations to take private property for public use (e.g., schools and roads) upon payment of its fair market value.

A mortgage loan where the closing documents -- through an eClosing process that includes, at a minimum, the Transferrable records -- are created, accessed, presented, executed, transferred and stored electronically.
See MISMO ePackage.

Indicates if the physical place of employment of the borrower is located outside of the United States. If the employer of the borrower is a foreign entity and the place of employment of the borrower is located inside the United States this value would be false.
A document issued by an employer which evidences a person's identity and employee identifier.
Indicates if the loan is part of an employee loan program.
Adopted in 1974, the Act affects many aspects of pension and profit-sharing plans, and regulates the investments such plans can make and the conduct of their fiduciaries.
Indicates that in the referenced employment, the office of the borrower is within the primary residence.
When true, indicates that in the referenced employment the borrower is self-employed.
Indicates whether the employment for the borrower is primary or secondary.
The type of documentation used as a means of identifying or verifying the borrower's employment used in the transaction.
A free-form text field used to capture the Employment Document Type if Other is selected.
Identifies the extent or level of the employment documentation being collected to process and underwrite the loan.
The date the borrower left the position with the employer.
When true, indicates that the Income Type is from an employment source. When false, indicates that the Income Type is from a non employment source.
The amount per month of income associated with the borrower's employment.
The number of complete months of service to an employer from the start of employment until the date on which the employment is reported.
A free-form text field describing the borrower's employment position or title.
Indicates the date when the employment information was reported to the repository bureau.

terms.term: Employment Self Owned Business Operations End Date
terms.definition: The date the business owned by the borrower ended operations.

terms.term: Employment Self Owned Business Operations Start Date
terms.definition: The date the business owned by the borrower began operating.
The date that the borrower started the employment position with the employer.
The current employment status of the borrower.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Employment State Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the relative time frame of the employment (current or previous).

terms.term: Employment Time In Line Of Work Months Count
terms.definition: The total number of complete months the borrower has been employed in the line of work or type of business.

terms.term: Employment Time In Line Of Work Years Count
terms.definition: The total number of years the borrower has been employed in that reported occupation.
A free-form text field describing the line of work or type of business in which the borrower is employed.
An enumerated or coded value identifying the extent to which the obligor's employment was verified during the loan origination process.
The number of time periods as defined by the Employment Verification Range Type for which documentation is collected.
Specifies the period or range of time for which the specific type of Employment Document Type is collected.

terms.term: Employment Verification Range Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Employment Verification Range Type.
The number of complete years of service to an employer from the start of employment until the date on which the employment is reported.
An improvement that illegally violates another's property or right to use that property.
A free-form text field describing the encroachment and/or its impact on the value and marketability of the property.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the relation of the encroachment to an adjoining property.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of intrusion existing on a property when a stationary object crosses a neighboring property line (e.g. fence, shed, garage, tree).
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Encroachment Type.
The manipulation of a document's data in order to prevent any one but the intended recipient from reading the data. Encrypted data is often referred to as cipher data.
Anything that affects or limits the fee simple title to property, such as mortgages, leases, easements or restrictions.

Identifies a right to or interest in the property that may affect value. Certain restrictions require the appraiser to indicate with additional addendum text such as Deed Restrictions on Community Land Trust properties.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Encumbrance Type.
The final mortgage loan to the ultimate purchaser of a property, as opposed to a construction loan or other form of interim financing.
This is an enumerated list of values that identify how the charges will be billed for services related to Additional End-User processing.

terms.term: End User Billing Instruction Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for End User Billing Instruction Type.
The name of the party that has been identified as an Additional End-User of credit report data by the party requesting the credit report data.

An individual or organization who makes, has made, uses, distributes, imports, modifies, reproduces, publishes, displays, or makes derivative works using, or that are compliant with, a MISMO Product where the individual or organization uses the MISMO Product (including derivative and compliant works) either (a) for its own internal business purposes, or (b) within the confines of its organization without distribution to any third party.

A signature on a negotiable instrument by which title to property mentioned therein is assigned and transferred. Also, a notation added to an instrument after execution to change or clarify its contents. In insurance, coverage may be restricted or enlarged by endorsing a policy. In FHA loans, a notation placed on the note by the FHA indicating that the loan is insured under the National Housing Act.
The amount of the energy efficiency incentive.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list detailing the level of a governmental authority providing the financial incentive for an energy efficiency improvement or component.
A free-form text field of comments describing the energy efficiency financial incentive.
A free-form text field describing the energy efficient and green feature and/or its impact on the value and marketability of the property.
A free-form text field describing energy efficient items.
Determines loan amount for Energy Efficient Mortgage loan (loan to finance repairs that increase energy efficiency of the home). Required by HUD. Provided by Underwriter.
The dollar amount of each EnergyImprovementType financed as part of the loan.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a property energy improvement financed as part of the loan.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Agency Energy Improvements Type.
When true, indicates that the loan will include an amount for energy-related improvements.
A report rendered by an engineer stating the physical condition of property that has been inspected, with a summation or recommendation thereof.
Any notarial act performed electronically, that a notarial officer may perform under state law.
See Transferable Record. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Indicates whether the loan delivery data has been automatically certified against eNote data.
Additional terms in the text of the eNote to comply with ESIGN and UETA, also known as "eNote Language"
Indicates that an eNote is used as part of this loan.

The data record that is created when a Participant registers an eNote on the MERS eRegistry. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual as 'eNote Record' and is available at members.mersinc.org.

The process of creating the initial record in the MERS eRegistry for identifying the Controller, Location, and other key information of the eNote. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual as "eNote Registration Record" and is available at members.mersinc.org.

A file, database, digital signature process, or other electronic method for tracking information concerning use, access to, and Alteration (such as a loan modification) of Electronic Records and which includes identifying and tracking the transfer of ownership of Transferable Records. See MERS eRegistry and Transferable Record

An Electronic Note Vault is a secure storage solution that meets the requirements of eSignature Laws. The concept is analogous to a paper note vault administered by a document custodian in the industry today.

A depressed neighborhood, usually in an urban area, in which businesses are given tax incentives and are not subject to some government regulations. These advantages are designed to attract new businesses into the zone.

One of the many internet resource locations that the legal entity has chosen to be its home page. The Entity Home Page URL should be in URL format. When one browses to that location one expects to find a real resource page.
The date and time the action occurred. The time must always contain the proper time zone designator.
Contains additional information or details about the action performed.
The date the environmental condition was identified.
A free-form text field describing the environmental condition and/or its impact on the value and marketability of the property.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents proximity of the environmental condition to the property.
A type of environmental condition identified during the analysis of a lot or structure.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Environmental Condition Type.

A document required by many federal, state and local environmental land use laws, containing an analysis of the impact that a proposed change may have on the environment of a specific geographic region. It examines a wide variety of physical, social and economic conditions that would be affected by the proposed development. The analysis covers effects that cannot be avoided, alternatives to the proposed change, short-term versus long-term uses and long-term productivity, irreversible commitments of resources and the benefits to be derived from the proposed change.

A special form of insurance designed to protect an insured against claims for liability and clean-up costs related to pollution. Coverage may be granted for gradual and sudden and accidental pollution, and is always written on a claims made form.
The agency responsible for enforcing environmental liability.

A federal law that requires lenders and other creditors to make credit equally available without discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status or receipt of income from public assistance programs. Also called "Regulation B."
Informs the borrower that all consumers are entitled to an equal chance to obtain credit. AKA: Reg B, ECOA.
An instrument that, because of a technical defect, is not actually a mortgage, but because the intention of the parties is to create a mortgage, the instrument will be enforced by a court of equity.
The net value of an asset. In the case of real estate, it would be the difference between the present value of the property and the mortgage amount on that property.
Money invested by shareholders who are owners and who receive a share of profits.

The common law right to redeem property following default on a mortgage by paying the unpaid debt plus interest and costs prior to the foreclosure sale. In some states, the mortgagor has a statutory right to redeem property after a foreclosure sale.

The right of a lender to a share in the gross profits, net profits or net proceeds in the event of sale or refinance of a property on which the lender has made a loan. Also known as an "equity kicker."
See EFFECTIVE RENT.

1) The act of registering the security instrument electronically with the county recorder or similar jurisdictional authority. 2) An act of registering the security instrument and other recordable documents electronically with the county recorder or similar jurisdictional authority. eRecording does not require the security instrument to be electronically executed. A county often records a scanned image of the paper security instrument when it eRecords. For models of eRecording, see the PRIA Technology Committee Business Requirements Work Group: Models of eRecording - A Continuum of eRecording - https://www.pria.us/i4a/doclibrary
Identifies a user-defined category for an error.
A unique code associated with an error.
Identifies a user-defined category for an error message.
A unique code for a specific error message.
Text describing specific details of an error message.
Textual description of an error.

terms.term: Errors And Omissions Insurance (E and O Insurance)
terms.definition: Liability insurance coverage for errors, mistakes and negligence in the usual activities of a mortgage banker. Fraudulent behavior is not included.
A clause providing upward adjustments of rent payments to cover specified contingencies. Also, a provision in a lease to provide for increases in property tax and operating expenses.
A clause that allows a tenant to cancel a lease in situations that would not necessarily justify lease cancellation.
Property taken into state ownership in the absence of the original owner, or upon the owners death in that state, without heirs.

An item of value, money or documents, deposited with a third party to be delivered upon the fulfillment of a condition. For example, the deposit by a borrower with the lender of funds to pay taxes and insurance premiums when they become due, or the deposit of funds or documents with an attorney or escrow agent to be disbursed upon the closing of a sale of real estate. In some parts of the country, escrows of taxes and insurance premiums are called impounds or reserves.
Specifies the reason the loan does not have an escrow account.

terms.term: Escrow Absence Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Absence Reason Type.
The segregated trust account in which escrow funds are held.

terms.term: Escrow Account Activity Current Balance Amount
terms.definition: The current balance in the escrow account for the activity period, as projected during the closing documents preparation process.
The disbursement month of the escrow account for the activity period.
The disbursement year of the escrow account for the activity period.

terms.term: Escrow Account Activity Payment Description Type
terms.definition: A description of the escrow disbursement type included in a payment for the activity period.

terms.term: Escrow Account Activity Payment Description Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Account Activity Payment Description Type.

terms.term: Escrow Account Activity Payment From Escrow Account Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the disbursement for the activity period.

terms.term: Escrow Account Activity Payment To Escrow Account Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the payment to the escrow account for the activity period.
The initial total of all escrow amounts collected to establish the escrow account.
Identifies the escrow account status in terms of the requirements of the lender in the mortgage loan transaction.
The lowest escrow balance target amount determined by the allowable cushion.
When true, indicates that the establishment of an escrow account has been requested by the borrower(s) for the loan.
The amount of the previous escrow account balance being rolled into the escrow account for the subject loan.
