Amount the escrow account is or is anticipated to be short. (As determined by the originator of the modification.)

terms.term: Escrow Account Shortage Repayment Period Years Count
terms.definition: The number of years over which the Escrow Account Shortage Amount may be repaid.

The person or organization having a fiduciary responsibility to both the buyer and seller (or lender and borrower) to see that the terms of the purchase/sale (or loan) are carried out. Also called escrow company or escrow depository.
The amount of any adjustment made to the initial escrow account balance based on Regulation X requirements.
Establishes escrow accounts for taxes and insurance. Agreement between borrower and lender.
The periodic examination of escrow accounts to determine if current monthly deposits will provide sufficient funds to pay taxes, insurance and other bills when due.

An annual review and recalculation of the escrow account based on actual amounts paid into the escrow account and actual amounts disbursed from the escrow account as required by RESPA. The actual amounts are compared to the projected amounts from the prior year's disclosure.
The amount of the annual payment for the Escrow Item Type.
Escrow balance on the loan net of any escrow advances. May be a negative amount.
Provides an arithmetic total of the Escrow Balance data items within the Loan container in this data set.

terms.term: Escrow Collected Number Of Months Count
terms.definition: The number of months escrow to be collected at closing for the escrow item.
An organization established to act as an escrow agent.
A three-party agreement between the buyer, seller and the escrow agent, specifying the rights and duties of each.

terms.term: Escrow Cushion Number Of Months Count
terms.definition: Denotes the maximum number of monthly escrow collections allowed to be held as the projected lowest balance in the escrow account for the projection year. Escrow cushion months will have a value of 0, 1 or 2.
Establishes work to be completed on a property and the terms under which the funds for the work will be released. AKA: Holdback, Work Escrow Agreement.
Confirms work on the property has been completed and any funds held in escrow can be released. AKA: Work Escrow Mortgagee Assurance of Completion (2300).
Amount held back at closing by the lender or escrow agent until a particular condition has been met.
An enumerated list of values that describe the purpose of the escrow funds being held back.
A free-form text field used to capture the Escrow Holdback Type if Other is selected.
Indicates whether or not escrows are associated with this loan.
The identifier assigned to the insurance policy by the issuing company.
The actual dollar amount paid by a specific party at a specified time for a specified escrow item.
The actual total dollar amount paid for the escrow item by all parties.
Identifies the category of the escrow item type.

terms.term: Escrow Item Category Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Item Category Type.

The date the escrow disbursement amount for the associated escrow item disbursement date was actually disbursed to the payee for the indicated escrow item. If no date provided, indicates the escrow disbursement amount for the associated escrow item disbursement date has not been disbursed to the payee.
The premium to be paid for the associated escrow item and the due date.
The date the escrow item type is due in the aggregate cycle.

terms.term: Escrow Item Disbursement Term Months Count
terms.definition: The term expressed in months between each premium disbursement associated with the escrow item and the due date.
The estimated dollar amount paid by a specific party at a specified time for a specified escrow item.
The total estimated dollar amount to be paid for the escrow item by all parties.
Specifies the last disbursement date for the selected escrow item.

terms.term: Escrow Item Next Disbursement Due Date
terms.definition: Specifies the due date of the next disbursement for the selected escrow item.

terms.term: Escrow Item Next Projected Disbursement Amount
terms.definition: Specifies the projected amount of the next disbursement due on this escrow item.

terms.term: Escrow Item Payment Paid By Type
terms.definition: The role of the party making the escrow item payment.

terms.term: Escrow Item Payment Paid By Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Item Paid By Type.
Defines the point in time during the origination process when the escrow item payment was paid.

terms.term: Escrow Item Payment Timing Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Item Payment Timing Type.

terms.term: Escrow Item Total Reserve Collected At Closing Amount
terms.definition: The total amount collected at closing for escrow account reserves for the specified escrow item.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents an item that may be held and managed in an escrow account.
A free-form text field to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Item Type.
The monthly payment amount for the escrow item.
Defines the rounding method applied to the escrow payment.
When true, indicates that, under applicable law, a servicer may not establish an escrow account for the mortgage loan being modified.
The difference, determined by escrow analysis, between escrow funds on deposit and escrow funds required to make a payment when it becomes due.
The type of Party responsible for payment of the escrow item.

That portion of a mortgagor's monthly payments held by a lender or servicer to pay taxes, hazard insurance, mortgage insurance, lease payments and other items as they become due. Also called "impounds" or "reserves" in some states.
Payment period covered by escrow item. If item were paid once a year the payment frequency type would be annual.

terms.term: Escrow Payment Frequency Type Other Description
terms.definition: When Other is specified as the Payment Frequency Type, this data element contains the description.
The dollar amount of the escrow premium for the escrow item type.
The number of months covered by the related premium.
The type of party responsible for the payment of the escrow premium amount.
The payment method of the premium for the escrow item. Paid Outside of Closing (POC), Waived or Collect at Closing.

The percentage rate used to calculate the amount of the Escrow Premium. This is used in conjunction with the Escrow Premium Percent Basis Type to determine a total dollar amount of the Escrow Premium.

terms.term: Escrow Premium Rate Percent Basis Type
terms.definition: Defines the amount upon which the Escrow Premium Percent is calculated.

terms.term: Escrow Premium Rate Percent Basis Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Escrow Premium Percent Basis Type.
The additional monthly escrow payment amount as the result of a shortage at the last escrow analysis.

terms.term: Escrow Specified HUD1 Line Number Value
terms.definition: The line number on the HUD-1 where the Escrow Item is to be disclosed.
Total amount disbursed for the escrow item from closing to the current date.
An instrument transferring escrow funds (and obligations under an existing escrow agreement) held by the lender to a third party upon transfer of property.

Confirms the lender agrees to waive collecting a monthly payment for taxes and insurance (escrow or impound account). Informs the applicant of their responsibilities to pay tax/insurance bills when due, whether an escrow waiver fee will be imposed, and information regarding lender placement of insurance. AKA: Notice Regarding Payments For Homeowners Insurance And Property Taxes, Escrow Account Notice.
When true, indicates the borrower has elected to establish an escrow account.

The servicing of an electronic mortgage. To date the implications of servicing electronic mortgages seem minimal on a performing loan. The nuances of pursuing foreclosure using electronic mortgage documentation need to still be addressed.
ESIGN and UETA.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains specific directions around which Lender Documents can be signed electronically and the requirements to meet the lender's expectations.
When true, indicates the lender will permit some or all lender documents to be electronically signed as part of the closing event.

terms.term: ESigned Non Lender Document Permitted Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the lender will permit some or all non-lender documents to be electronically signed as part of the closing event.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains specific directions around which Non-Lender Documents can be signed electronically and the requirements to meet the lender's expectations.
The process of converting a non-escrowed loan into an escrowed account due to non-payment of taxes or insurance or non-compliance with the note.
Establish a plan to cure a short term delinquency by temporarily increasing the amount or frequency of the payment without changing the terms of the loan.
The ownership interest an individual has in real property. The sum total of all the real and personal property owned by an individual at the time of death.
Indicates the significance of the restriction is considered to have for the purpose in which it is being reported.

terms.term: Estimate Of Closing Costs Paid To Third Party
terms.definition: Informs the borrower of estimated loan closing costs.
The estimated annual savings in utilities bills for the home as a result of the incentivized energy-related improvements.
The estimated amount of cash that the borrower may receive at closing based on a calculation agreed to by the parties to the transaction.
The dollar amount of the estimated loan fees, title fees, appraisal fees and other closing costs associated with the subject transaction excluding discount points.
The estimated dollar amount of the contribution.
The estimated dollar amount of the insurance claim that will be filed.
The estimated dollar amount of the insurance proceeds.
The estimated dollar value of the market monthly rent for a living unit or residence.

terms.term: Estimated Market Monthly Rent Effective Date
terms.definition: Specifies the effective date of the estimated market monthly rent.
This is the estimated number of odd days for prepaid interest that are to be included in the prepaid charges.

terms.term: Estimated Prepaid Days Paid By Type
terms.definition: Party responsible for payment of estimated odd days interest.

terms.term: Estimated Prepaid Days Paid By Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture the prepaid days contributor type if Other is selected as the estimated prepaid days paid by type.
A free-form text field describing the analysis that led to the remaining economic life conclusion.

terms.term: Estimated Remaining Economic Life Years Count
terms.definition: The estimated number of years of the structure's remaining useful life.
Establishes that certain statements of fact are correct as of the date of the statement and can be relied upon by a third party (including a prospective lender or purchaser).
A written statement setting forth certain facts which cannot later be repudiated (frequently given by a lender or a tenant relative to a loan or lease, respectively).
Legal term meaning "and wife;" sometimes abbreviated "et ux."

The act of underwriting a loan through electronic means. Today, automated underwriting tools allow the credit package of a loan to be underwritten and electronically scored. The future of electronic mortgages expands this opportunity to obtaining income documentation and validation through electronic interface, asset validation through electronic interface and collateral assessments through electronic documentation and interface.
Dollar denominated deposits in a bank or bank branch outside the United States.
The lender decision that the application threshold requirements have been met, triggering the disclosure requirements.
Process of determining whether the loan satisfies Ability-to-Repay (ATR) requirements and/or meets the definition of a Qualified Mortgage (QM).

Process in which the Servicer follows the mandatory, hierarchical sequence of steps to evaluate borrowers who are in default or imminent risk of default for options to avoid foreclosure. Also referred to as the Default Waterfall.
A type of valuation report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent person.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent person and includes the development of a value conclusion without a physical inspection and may rely on expert systems and data.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent person and includes the development of a value conclusion and includes an exterior inspection of the property and may also rely on expert systems and data.
The unique alphanumeric string identifying an event as assigned by the recipient at the time of event initiation.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the function that the participant plays in an event. A participant may have multiple functions in an event.
A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Event Participant Type.
A free-form text field used to capture the enumeration when Other is selected for Event Participant Type.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains a summary of the understanding and or details of an event from the perspective of the event participant identified as the recipient.
For a step in a process, contains the type of action or state.
A free-form text field used to describe the type of action or state if Other is selected as the Event Type.
The lawful expulsion of an occupant from real property.

terms.term: Eviction Avoided With Rental Counseling Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that a household avoided eviction after receiving rental counseling.
Proof of ownership of property.

The committee member representative recommended by the committee and approved by the Board to serve on the Board of Directors. Ex Officio Directors receive all Board communications and attend and participate in all Board meetings. However, they may not vote and do not count toward a meeting quorum.
The review of the chain of title as revealed by an abstract of title or public record.
In legal descriptions, that portion of land to be deleted or excluded. The term is also used to describe an objection to title or encumbrance on title.

terms.term: Exception Interest Adjustment Day Method Type
terms.definition: The day basis on which the exception interest adjustment is computed based on the servicing contract.
An amount of income derived from the operation of a property or business after deducting or paying all expenses.
A coverage designed to be in excess over one or more primary policies, which will not pay out until the primary limits of liability are exhausted.
Cash flows from servicing portfolios which are greater than the costs incurred to service the loans contained therein.

The portion of interest payments made by the mortgage borrower that a loan servicer is entitled to retain in consideration for performing mortgage servicing activities for the owner of the mortgage loan (the mortgage servicing spread) over the portion representing reasonable compensation for services performed by the loan servicer.

The portion of interested party contributions that exceed the limit when those funds are used to pay typical borrower financing fees, closing costs and pre-paids or provide a benefit to the borrower in financing the transaction. Excessive financing concessions are treated as sales concession for qualifying purposes.
Process in which the Lender communicates loan application data with business partners.

A written contract giving one licensed real estate agent the exclusive right to sell a property for a specified time, but reserving the owner's right to sell the property alone without the payment of a commission.
A written contract giving one real estate agent the right to sell a piece of real property and entitling that agent to a commission upon sale, regardless of who finds a buyer.
A clause in a contract holding a specified party harmless in the event of default. For example, the provision in a note that the debtor will not be held personally liable in the event of default.
Recordation of the appropriate signatures on a document such as a mortgage note, to render it "in effect."
Process in which the Borrower signs the closing documents, either electronically, or using pen and paper.
The process of transferring serviced loan(s) from one Servicer to another.
A judicial order directing an appropriate officer of the court to enforce a judgment against the property or person of the judgment debtor, in an attempt to satisfy the judgment.

Part of a 3-part process necessary to fully execute an EOLT. This is the second part, and represents the actual closing or contracting part of the transactions where parties involved electronically review and sign documents.
The date the signature was or will be affixed to the document.
The date and time the signature was affixed to the document.
The name of the judicial district where documents were signed (executed).
The type of judicial district where documents were signed (executed).

terms.term: Execution Judicial District Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Execution Judicial District Type.
Specifies the type of execution through which the loan was purchased by an investor.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Execution Type.
A person named in a will to administer an estate. The court will appoint an administrator if no executor is named. Executrix is the feminine form.
Real estate not subject to property taxes. Religious, educational and charitable organizations generally hold exempt property.

Strike price. The price at which an option seller has agreed to buy or sell securities. Also, the price at which the underlying security or commodity will be delivered in the event an option is exercised.
In HUD/FHA transactions, a house that was not approved by HUD/FHA or VA before the beginning of construction, but which has been completed more than one year.
The price at which property might be sold at some future date. Generally, the price used to calculate internal rate of return.
The dollar amount paid monthly for rent less the amounts paid monthly for utilities and furniture.
Specifies the broad category into which individual Expense Claim Types may be grouped. The party assigning the identifier should be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
Identifies a user-defined classification to which the expense claim line item belongs.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on some aspect of the expense claim.
A unique identifier assigned by a party to specify an expense claim form that is used to request reimbursement. The party assigning the identifier should be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
A unique identifier for the expense claim. The party assigning the identifier should be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
For maintenance, service, or activities performed over a period of time, the date that it was cancelled.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on some aspect of the expense claim item.
For maintenance, service, or activities performed over a period of time, the date that it was completed.
The number of times a service or activity was performed or delivered over a range of time.
When true, indicates that the associated claim expense item is escrowed.
For maintenance, service, or activities performed over a period of time, the date that it began or will begin.
Specifies the type of maintenance, service or activity that was performed and is being claimed as an expense. The party assigning the identifier should be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.

terms.term: Expense Claim Item Insurance Placed Type
terms.definition: Specifies the party who placed the insurance associated with the expense claim.

terms.term: Expense Claim Item Insurance Placed Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Expense Claim Item Insurance Placed Type.
The date the expense claim item was paid by the submitter to the service provider.
The dollar amount requested per occurrence of the service or activity.
For maintenance, service, or activities performed over a period of time, the date that it ended or will end.

terms.term: Expense Claim Item Unit Price Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount that is allowed per occurrence of the service or activity.
A unique identifier assigned by a party to an expense claim submission. The party assigning the identifier can be provided using the IdentifierOwnerURI.
Specifies the reason for the expense claim submission.

terms.term: Expense Claim Submission Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Expense Claim Submission Reason Type.
Specifies the occurrence of the claim being submitted.

terms.term: Expense Claim Submission Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Expense Claim Submission Type.
Total amount of all line items in the claim.

terms.term: Expense Claim Total Non Reimbursable Amount
terms.definition: Total amount of all non-reimbursable items associated with the claim.
A text description that further defines the expense. This could be used to describe the job related expenses.
When true, indicates the expense is to be excluded from calculations associated with processing the loan.
The dollar amount of the monthly payment required on borrower's Expense Type.
The number of months the borrower must make payments in order to satisfy the identified expense.
See BASE STOP.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies items commonly listed as borrower expenses on a mortgage loan transaction.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Expense Type.
When true, indicates the borrower cannot make mortgage payments due to an increase in expenses.
Automated system that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to make decisions based on parameters built into the system, rather than analysis of data.
A set of processes and methods that allows human users to comprehend and trust the results and output created by machine learning algorithms.

The total amount a lender has tied up in a loan. Usually the outstanding principal balance of the loan plus accrued interest, and any capitalized costs including legal fees and expenses, appraisal and environmental fees and all other costs associated with securing the lender's interest in the property.

A common extension of insurance coverage beyond the normal fire and lightning perils. Damage caused by windstorm, hail, explosion, riot, vehicles, smoke, aircraft and other falling objects are the additional perils insured by this coverage. In secondary marketing, a market position characterized by uncovered or unhedged mortgage pipeline and/or inventory risk that may result in a financial loss, due to fluctuations and other market factors.
An endorsement that may be attached to insurance policies, which extends the breadth of coverage.
Mortgage rate commitments which are for longer than the typical 60-day lock-in term.
A family of document types, schemas, and modules that reproduce, subset, and extend HTML. XHTML conforms to the XML standard.

Extensible Markup Language is a simple, flexible text format. It is essentially a set of rules or convention for putting structured data in a text file. It is platform independent which allows the computer to generate or read files easily. XML uses tags to delimit pieces of data, but leaves the interpretation of the data up to the application.
Continuation past original maturity date; continuation of a commitment.
An enumerated or coded value that represents the exterior condition rating of the structure.
A free-form text field used to describe the exterior feature.
Specifies one exterior feature of the property.
A free-form text field used to specify the exterior feature if Other is selected as the Exterior Feature Type.
Indicates that an exterior only inspection is sufficient.
An enumerated or coded value that represents the exterior quality rating of the structure.
The number of face to face interviews with the borrower in current month.
Par value or the actual selling price of a security; the amount the issuer contracts to repay.
When true, indicates that this loan or mortgage was made to facilitate the sale of a Servicing REO property.
Fair And Accurate Credit Transaction Act

Informs the borrower of their credit score, range of possible scores, key factors affecting score, reporting agencies used, contacts for obtaining a report copy, and includes a statement that terms offered are based on consumer report information.
When true, indicates that a factory-built certification is present and has been examined for a modular home.

Informs the borrower that it is illegal to discriminate in lending practices. This is different that the Equal Credit Opportunity Act. AKA: The Housing Financial Discrimination Act of 1977 Fair Lending Notice.
An amount determined by HUD to be the cost of modest, non-luxury rental units in a specific market area.

The price at which property is transferred between a willing buyer and a willing seller, each of whom has a reasonable knowledge of all pertinent facts and neither being under any compulsion to buy or sell.
The percentage of loans in the pipeline expected not to close.

The nation's largest mortgage investor, created in 1968 by an amendment to Title III of the National Housing Act (12 USC 1716 et seq.). This stockholder-owned corporation, a portion of whose board of directors is appointed by the President of the United States, supports the secondary market in mortgages on residential property with mortgage purchase and securitization programs. aka Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA).
A lender designated by Fannie Mae who originates, underwrites, closes and services Fannie Mae approved multifamily mortgage loans.

A former government agency within the Department of Agriculture that operated under the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act of 1921 and Title V of the Housing Act of 1949. This agency provided financing to farmers and other qualified borrowers who were unable to obtain loans elsewhere. See RURAL HOUSING SERVICE.
The commencement of construction before design drawings are complete.
Fair Debt Collection Practices Act
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
A detailed investigation and analysis conducted to determine the financial, economic, technical or other advisability of a proposed project.
Informs the borrower that the lender is offering an insurance product or annuity in connection with an extension of credit. AKA: AntiCoercion Disclosure.
A payment system operated by the Federal Reserve for the transfer of Federal Funds balances between financial institutions maintaining accounts at U.S. Federal Reserve Banks.
Federal legislation empowering state and local governments to issue tax-free bonds to fund mortgages for low- and middle-income borrowers.

Originally established by the Banking Act of 1933 to protect depositors from loss. As a result of the Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery and Enforcement Act of 1989 (FIRREA), the FDIC administers the Bank Insurance Fund (BIF) and the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF).

Federal agency which, among other things, directs the activities of the Federal Insurance Administration and establishes flood insurance rates and terms of coverage, issues policies, processes claims and identifies and maps flood-prone areas.

A federal agency within the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that provides mortgage insurance for residential mortgages and sets standards for construction and underwriting. The FHA does not lend money, nor does it plan or construct housing.
Independent five-member federal agency regulating the credit activities of the 11 Federal Home Loan Banks.

terms.term: Federal Information Processing Standard (140-2) or FIPS (140-2)
terms.definition: Federal Information Processing Standard (140-2), which specifies the security requirements that will be satisfied by a cryptographic module, providing four increasing, qualitative levels intended to cover a wide range of potential applications and environments.
See Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Commonly referred to as the Fed.
Informs the borrower that the lender is selling credit insurance as part of the loan transaction.
Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
The actual dollar amount paid by a specific party at a specified time for a specified fee or cost.
The actual total dollar amount paid for the fee by all parties.
Appraiser who is an independent contractor and is paid a fee on a case-by-case basis by lenders or others for performing a property appraisal.
The dollar amount of a fee or cost charged against a loan.
The date a fee or cost was charged against a loan.
When true, indicates that the fee is collected post-consummation (post-closing). For example, fees collected as construction services are performed.
The description of the fee.
The estimated dollar amount paid by a specific party at a specified time for a specified fee.
The total estimated dollar amount to be paid for the fee by all parties.
Identifies the category or type of payee to which the fee or payment will be paid.

terms.term: Fee Paid To Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field to capture the description when Other is selected as Fee Paid To Type.

terms.term: Fee Payment Allowable FHA Closing Cost Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the fee is an allowable FHA Closing Cost.
Identifies the role of the party collecting the fee.

terms.term: Fee Payment Collected By Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field to capture the description when Other is selected as Fee Payment Collected By Type.
The portion or remaining amount of the fee payment still due from the Borrower or Seller, after application of Paid Out Of Closing and Paid Through Closing fee payment amounts.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the role of the party paying a fee or cost.

terms.term: Fee Payment Paid By Type Third Party Name
terms.definition: The name or description of the party paying the fee when Third Party is the selected enumerated value for Fee Payment Paid By Type.
The date a fee or cost was credited or paid.

terms.term: Fee Payment Paid Outside Of Closing Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates payment of fee was paid outside of closing.
The portion of the Fee Total Percent that is to be paid by the specified party. The party is identified in the Fee Payment Paid By Type.
Processing - typical buyer paid fee to be disclosed on GFE; Closing - typical seller fee not disclosed on GFE.
The amount of the fee that is refundable.
A description of the conditions under which the fee is refundable.
When true, the fee may be refundable under certain conditions.
Identifies the fee payment as the responsibility of the Buyer, Seller or other party of the loan transaction.

terms.term: Fee Payment Responsible Party Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the party responsible for the fee payment when Other is selected as the Fee Payment Responsible Party Type.
Defines the amount upon which the Fee Total Percent is calculated.

terms.term: Fee Percent Basis Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Fee Percent Basis Type.
The previously disclosed amount of the fee or charge associated with a redisclosure to the borrower.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a category for a fee or cost associated with a real estate transaction or the ongoing servicing of a loan.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Fee Process Type.
A document furnished by a Title Agent/Closing Agent to disclose closing costs that may be associated to the transaction. Also known as a Preliminary Fee Sheet or Quote.
The greatest possible interest a person can have in real estate, including the right to dispose of the property or pass it on to one's heirs.
An alphanumeric string that identifies the specification name and version of the source of the Fee Type Other Description.
The specified fixed dollar portion of the Fee Total Amount. This is used when the Fee Total Amount is made up of a percentage (stated in the Fee Total Percent) plus a specified fixed dollar amount.

terms.term: Fee Specified HUD1 Line Number Value
terms.definition: HUD-1 Line Number for fee items that pertain to miscellaneous sections of the HUD-1 document where there is not a one-to-one mapping between the line number and the line description.
The numeric or alphanumeric value used to identify the placement, location or sequence of fee information.

terms.term: Fee Summary Approximate Cost Of Funds Percent
terms.definition: The approximate cost of the funds used to make the loan transaction. Either the most recent ten-year Treasury constant maturity rate or the creditor's actual cost of borrowing the funds used to extend the credit, at the creditor's option.

terms.term: Fee Summary Disclosed Total Sales Price Amount
terms.definition: Total amount required as part of the TIL Disclosure document for REO sales. (Fifth box of the disclosure section.)

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Amount Financed Amount
terms.definition: The amount of the Total Amount Financed as disclosed based on the accepted industry standard defined by Regulation Z.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total APR Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of all fees charged included in the APR calculation.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Deposited Reserves Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of escrow reserves to be deposited.
The total dollar amount of fees that have been charged across all payers and payees.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Fees Paid By Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of fees paid by a party in the transaction.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Fees Paid By Type
terms.definition: A party to the transaction by whom a fee or fees have been designated paid.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Fees Paid By Type Other Description
terms.definition: A description of the party who fees were paid by when Other or Third Party are selected in Fee Summary Total Fees Paid By Type.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Fees Paid To Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of fees paid to a party in the transaction.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Fees Paid To Type
terms.definition: A party to the transaction to whom a fees have been paid.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Fees Paid To Type Other Description
terms.definition: A description of the party to who fees have been paid when Other is selected in RESPA Summary Total Fees Collected By Type.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Filing Recording Fee Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of filing fees, or recording fees, as required to be disclosed on the TIL Disclosure document.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Finance Charge Amount
terms.definition: The amount of the Total Finance Charges as disclosed based on the accepted industry standard defined by Regulation Z.
The total amount of interest paid by the borrower over the term of the loan as a percentage of the loan amount.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Loan Origination Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount of fees, for both the seller and the buyer, that have been charged on the loan at the time of origination. It is the total of the 800 series of lines on the HUD1.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Net Borrower Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount of fees still due from the borrower after the deduction of amounts paid by or on behalf of the borrower toward fees charged to the borrower.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Net Proceeds For Funding Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of proceeds required for funding after subtracting lender defined fees or charges.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Net Seller Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount of fees still due from the seller after the deduction of amounts paid by or on behalf of the seller toward fees charged to the seller.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Non APR Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of all fees charged not included in the APR calculation.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Of All Payments Amount
terms.definition: The amount of the Total of All Payments as disclosed based on the accepted industry standard defined by Regulation Z.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Paid To Others Amount
terms.definition: The amount determined by Regulation Z as the Total Paid To Others as disclosed on the Itemization of Amount Financed.

terms.term: Fee Summary Total Prepaid Finance Charge Amount

Code identifying the county. (Designator Code based on Federal Information Processing Standard Publication 6-4)

The Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) County Subdivision Code identifies all county subdivisions in the 50 states, District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. The Minor Civil Division (MCD) and Census County Division (CCD) are geocodes that are part of the FIPS 55 system, developed by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and now maintained by the U.S. Geological Survey. The FIPS 55 system identifies named entities with a unique five-digit numeric locality code. The FIPS 55 locality codes identify governmentally functioning MCDs within a numeric range from 00001 to 89999. The codes in this range also represent incorporated places, Census Designated Places (CDP), and Alaska Native and American Indian areas, together with other entities not included in the tabulations of the decennial census, such as named localities, military installations, and National Parks. All these entity names are combined and listed in a single alphabetic sequence. The FIPS code range, 90000 to 98999, is reserved for CCDs and nonfunctioning MCDs where they cover whole States, whole counties, or their statistically equivalent entities.
The formal name or description for a county subdivision that is referenced by the FIPS County Subdivision Code. For example, Jones Township.

A legal or statistical division of a county recognized as part of the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 55 system. The two major types of county subdivisions are census county divisions and minor civil divisions. This information is used by the US Census Bureau.

A five-digit numeric code assigned by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and maintained by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), to identify populated places, primary county divisions, and other locational entities within a State. The NIST assigns the codes based on the alphabetic sequence of the entity names; it documents the codes in FIPS PUB 55. This information is used by the US Census Bureau.

The formal name of a statistical entity as defined by the by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and maintained by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), that is referenced by the FIPS Place Code. Place includes Census Bureau designated places, consolidated cities, and incorporated places. This is also represented by the 5-digit FIPS Place Code. This information is used by the US Census Bureau.

A unique two letter alpha code to identify each State and State equivalent entity. These State codes are part of the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS), an official coding system developed by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST, formerly the National Bureau of Standards), U.S. Department of Commerce, and maintained by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The FIPS state alpha code for each U.S. states and the District of Columbia is identical to the postal abbreviations by the United States Postal Service. Since September 3, 1987, the same has been true of the alpha code for each of the outlying areas, with the exception of U.S. Minor Outlying Islands (UM) as the USPS routes mail for these islands indirectly.

A unique two digit numeric code to identify each State and State equivalent entity. These State codes are part of the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS), an official coding system developed by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST, formerly the National Bureau of Standards), U.S. Department of Commerce, and maintained by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).

Used as a verb, hashing is the process to calculate a "digital fingerprint" of an electronic document with a mathematical algorithm. The digital fingerprint is unique and entirely based upon the specific content of the electronic document, including any signatures. Any change to the electronic document -- even something as small as the insertion or deletion of a single character -- will create two distinct and unlike digital fingerprints. Comparing the fingerprint and the recalculation of the digital fingerprint at a later date provide evidence of tampering.

The result of a Hashing Algorithm. A Hash Value is a unique, fixed-sized computed value that represents any arbitrary length string (such as a document). Hash values are also known as Message Digests, hash codes, hash sums, or hashes.

A mathematical function that is used to calculate an electronic Hash Value or "digital fingerprint" of an eDocument. Since this value is unique to the document, if the document were altered, the result from applying the Hashing Algorithm to the altered document would be different from applying the mathematical function to the original document. The difference in results indicates that the integrity of the original document has been compromised.
