A free-form text field used to collect additional information or a description of the Lock Status Type when Other is selected as the value.

The process by which a lender commits to lend at a particular rate as long as the mortgage transaction closes within a specified time period. The document which specifies the terms of the lock-in is called a rate commitment or lock-in agreement.
A fee charged by some lenders at the time of lock-in.
The number of days during which a lender guarantees a borrower a specific interest rate and terms on a mortgage.

A postal address, maintained by the firm's bank, that is used solely for the purpose of collecting checks. A major goal of a lockbox is to reduce collection float, since the receipts are immediately credited to the firm's bank account.

To document the XML Reference Model, MISMO creates a Logical Data Dictionary (LDD) that defines each XML data element used for electronic transactions. The result is a single, common data set for the mortgage industry. The borrower, employment, property and other commonly used information have a common data definition, no matter which mortgage industry segment is using the data. A catalog of key components of the MISMO Reference Model, including terms, containers, data attributes, and ARCROLES.

The Logical Data Model (LDM) will make it easier for organizations to communicate regardless of the technologies they choose to use for communicating with business partners. The LDM will support XML and JSON, which is the technology of choice for mobile transactions. The LDM was built using Unified Modeling Language (UML) 2.5, a common standard created by the Object Management Group. UML consists of an integrated set of diagrams that helps users specify, visualize, construct and document software or business systems. MISMO has also created a set of user guidelines to help industry participants adopt and implement the LDM in their business processes.
A logical, technology agnostic business focused representation of the MISMO Standards - essentially provides a business oriented point of entry to the LDM.
A logical, technology agnostic representation of the MISMO standards - essentially a technology agnostic, logical, blueprint for the standards.

A logical representation of the MISMO Standards created for a specific technology such as XML or JSON. The platform specific LDM can be used to forward engineer platform specific physical models such as the MISMO XML Reference Model or similar physical models for new technologies.
Letter Of Map Amendment
Letter Of Map Revision
The median average the bid rate and the offered rate (LIBOR).

The rate at which banks in the foreign market lend dollars to one another. LIBOR varies by deposit maturity. A common interest rate index; one of the most valid barometers of the international cost of money.
A marketing position in which a mortgage banker has mortgages in inventory or pipeline that are in excess of commitments.
A mortgage or deed of trust with a term of 10 years or more.
A lease with a term of 10 years or more.

The geographic coordinate most commonly used in cartography and global navigation for east-west measurement. It is the angular distance measured east or west and usually expressed in degrees (or hours), minutes, and seconds, from the prime meridian, defined to be at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich, in England, to the meridian passing through another position on the surface of the earth.
Loan Origination System. A piece of software that automates the end to end loan manufacturing cycle.
Mortgage reserves maintained by mortgage insurers sufficient to cover catastrophic losses.
Insurance payments in settlement of a claim for damage to mortgaged property. Drafts are generally made out to both the mortgagee and mortgagor.
See RENTAL INCOME INSURANCE.
An insurance policy provision for payment of a claim to someone other than the insured, who holds an insurable interest in the insured property.

The party named in a loss payable clause to whom insurance proceeds are to be paid in the event of damage to property in which the loss payee has an insurable interest. Loss payees include automobile lienholders and property mortgagees.
Specifies the general types of loss payees associated with the mortgage loan.
A free-form text field used to capture the loss payee type if Other is selected as the loss payee type.
Indicates whether or not a lost note affidavit (LNA) is associated with the loan.
A measured parcel of land having fixed boundaries as shown on the recorded plat.
An identifier created through the application of a reversible algorithm to a real estate parcel and in which the source of parcel identity is defined by the URI owner.
A measurement that specifies the total area of the site, including all parcels. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Area Unit Of Measure Type.
Quick qualifying program for residential mortgages that eliminates many verification documents and speeds up the approval process. These programs typically require a substantial down payment.
Loan To Value
The date the LTV was calculated.

terms.term: LTV Property Value Calculation Method Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO defined list that identifies the method used to determine the property value used for the LTV calculation.

terms.term: LTV Property Value Calculation Method Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for LTV Property Value Calculation Method Type.
The ratio of the (outstanding) loan amount to the appraised value, estimated value or purchase price of the property.
A technique used by computers to take data as input, find patterns, and summarize the pattern in a mathematically precise way.
The first private secondary market for the sale of conventional mortgages insured by the Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Corporation (MGIC).
Uniquely identifies an individual or office within a private company for the purposes of internal mail distribution. USPS calls this a MailStop Code (MSC).

The process of creating, maintaining documentation evidencing the servicer's response to a qualified written request (QWR) from a consumer. The QWR is a request for action or information as outlined in the National Servicing Rules and supplemental guidance from the CFPB or other regulator(s). Per the National Servicing Rules, a servicer must be able to communicate their compliance actions to regulators, transferees or interested third parties when requested.
In commercial property, firms which are key lessees/tenants because of their high credit standing, the amount of space they occupy and/or the percentage of gross rent they pay.
Process of providing the results of the underwriting analysis. Results may include Approval, Denial, or Counteroffer of the loan request.

The process of extending and recovering advances for Property Taxes, Hazard Insurance, HOA dues, Leasehold payments and Property Preservation expenses. Some of these processes are part of the Escrow Management function however they may also be a part of default management.
Process in which the Lender monitors locked and closed pipeline for the identification of commitment modifications to achieve good delivery through pair-offs, upsizing, or extensions.

The process of managing all activities related to non-performing loans. These activities maybe driven by the borrower willingness to participate, loan documents, investor regulations, servicer requirements and state and federal regulations.

The process of establishing and managing any required trust accounts where funds are allocated for payment of taxes, insurance and other items as they become due. In addition, the process of tracking the status of tax and insurance payments on non-escrowed loans.
The process of obtaining hazard insurance on a secured property when there is no existing policy in force.
The process of tracking damage notifications, repairs, disaster declaration driven claims, management of insurance proceeds and the interaction between insurance companies and borrowers.

The process of assigning and managing loans made under alternative loan programs and products such as state bond programs, ARMs, HELOCs, Buydowns or loans made to an acknowledged VIP. Includes compliance with Servicemember's Civil Relief Act (SCRA).
Process in which the Lender administers lock policies, facilitates inquiries, and remediates issues related to lock commitments through the end-to-end lifecycle of interest rate locks.
Process in which the Lender oversees the flow of loans from origination to sale, ensuring locks are managed, extensions are handled, and loans are delivered efficiently.
The process of identifying, evaluating and quantifying risks followed by coordinated and economical application of resources to minimize, monitor and control the probability or impact of that risk.
The process of posting premiums received and remitting payments to mortgage insurers.
The process of protecting the loan's lien position in situations where borrowers are not current on applicable Property Taxes, Hazard Insurance, HOA dues, Leasehold payments.
The process of removing MI coverage based upon investor guidelines. This may be automatic or upon the request of the borrower and includes appropriate notifications.
An agreement between buyer and seller for the purchase and sale of specified mortgage product in which both parties are obligated to perform.
Factory-built or prefabricated housing, including mobile homes.

A secondary reference to a regionally specific map document that assists in locating a property. May refer to locally available published map products (e.g. Thomas Map in CA) or a county tax map.

(1) In futures trading, an amount set by each exchange that buyers and sellers must deposit as a guarantee of performance. In this case, margin requirements are set by the Federal Reserve Board and are expressed as a percentage of the purchase price or market value. A call by a clearing organization of an exchange for the deposit of additional funds or collateral to offset trading losses on an outstanding position that is subject to margin.
The number of percentage points to be added to the index to arrive at the new interest rate.

Current supply and demand characteristics of a commodity in a given geographic/economic setting.
The dollar value of the estimated market rent of a comparable rental property determined by applying market driven rent adjustments during the application of a Rent Schedule Comparison.

A free-form text field that describes geographic boundaries of the area that is defined as the market (e.g. streets, waterways, county or state lines or other natural boundaries).

The lowest dollar amount for all properties in the real estate market inventory results.

Specifies the trend of the real estate market inventory type.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the price trend of properties in the defined market.
The price a tenant pays a landlord for the use and occupancy of real property based on current rent for comparable property.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the reconciliation of the final value for Estimated Market Monthly Rent Amount for a living unit or property.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the market rental data used in the determination of the Estimated Market Monthly Rent Amount for a living unit or property.

The projection of demand for a specific type of property or project, obtained by analyzing data on sales volume, rents, vacancies, turnover, consumer preferences and real estate prices in the surrounding area for similar properties.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the housing supply in the defined market.
Specifies the date range of the real estate market analysis.
Indicates that a trend toward adverse financing conditions is occurring.

Specifies the historic trend of sales prices in a neighborhood (e.g. Increasing, Stable, or Decreasing).
Specifies the mortgage interest rate trend (e.g. Decreasing, Stable, or Increasing).

The highest price that a buyer and the lowest price that a seller would accept, neither one being compelled to buy or sell. Also called "fair market value."
A title that may not be completely clear, but has only minor objections that a well-informed and prudent buyer of real estate would accept.
The sale of mortgage loans in the pipeline or in inventory to investors in the secondary market through investor commitments.
The total number of days the property would have been offered on the market prior to a hypothetical sale at market value as of the appraisal report effective date.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the range of time needed to sell the property.

Allows you to give meaning to any specific piece of data within a document. Without markup, computers see a document as one long string of text, with each character having equal importance to every other character.
Confirms that a marriage has occurred.

The basic condominium document that must be registered by the originating property owner prior to conveyance of the first unit sold. The master deed thoroughly describes the entire condominium entity, including each unit and all common areas, and specific essential elements of ownership that permanently govern its operation. Also called the "condominium declaration."
A lease under which the leasehold is further subleased by the tenant to one or more subtenants.
A form of ownership in which ownership interests are publicly traded on securities exchanges, and are therefore liquid.
A standard form mortgage recorded in the public record to help reduce recording fees, as mortgage documents thereafter refer to the record and the master mortgage.
A document evidencing that materials needed to complete construction work will be provided by the supplier who posts the bond to the contractor as beneficiary.

A free-form text field used to describe in detail the material used in the identified component.

The date on which an agreement expires; termination of a promissory note.
When true, indicates that the current use of the property is maximally productive.

The maximum amount the borrower is able to contribute to reduce investor losses for a workout where the borrower is permitted to remain in the property during a transition period. The borrower may make the contribution in cash or a contract.
The maximum number of percentage points by which the interest rate can decrease from the original interest rate over the life of the loan.
The maximum number of percentage points by which the interest rate can increase from the original interest rate over the life of the loan.
Highest loan dollar amount allowed under federal or conventional guidelines. In commercial real estate, the highest loan dollar amount that a property can support based on projected income.
The number of maturity term extensions that a borrower is allowed to exercise over the life of the loan.

The maximum promissory note payment amount the borrower can afford based on investor guidelines.

The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) is the national association that represents the real estate finance industry. It is a member-based nonprofit organization. The national MBA is headquartered in Washington D.C., though it works closely in collaboration with local and state mortgage bankers associations around the country.

The book entry depository for Ginnie Mae mortgage-backed securities.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of mechanical system.

When true, the mediation process ended successfully.

A MISMO Engineering Guideline (MEG) is published to assist the work groups in creating their specifications and to assist developers of MISMO Products to achieve consistent and technically appropriate products that meet the needs of the user community. The MEGs shall be adhered to during the development process without any deviation. MISMO has developed a series of MEGs to guide the process and production of Version 3.x Reference Model. In the event of a conflict between the MEGs and the DPD, the DPD takes precedence.
Any organization that has submitted the MISMO subscription application and the appropriate subscription fees and has been accepted as a member to MISMO.
The highest professional designation awarded by the American Institute of Real Estate Appraisers.
Any employee of a Member organization. May also be a consultant to a Member if designated by the Member in writing to MISMO.
Any employee of a Member organization. May also be a consultant to a Member if designated by the Member in writing to MISMO. See also Voting Representative.
The method of service fee calculation where each function the servicer performs for the lender has a corresponding fee.
Generally expressed in basis points ("bp") and calculated using the loan balance.
A title that a court of equity considers so clear that it will force acceptance of it by a purchaser. Also referred to as a "marketable title."

Identifies the method used by the servicer to notify the mortgagor to remit the mortgage payment.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that identifies the frequency with which statements are sent to the borrower.

terms.term: Payment Billing Statement Frequency Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for PaymentBillingStatementFrequencyType.

terms.term: Payment Billing Statement Lead Days Count
terms.definition: The number of days between the billing statement date and the payment due date.
The limitation on increases or decreases in the payment amount of an adjustable rate mortgage or fixed rate hybrid.
Time lag between the receipt of mortgage payments from borrowers and the remittance of monies payable to mortgage-backed security (MBS) investors.
Reports the delinquency status of the specific delinquency event.
The number of days the borrower payment is currently past due.
When true, indicates that the payment of any portion of the fee was financed into the original loan amount.
The number of months in which the forbearance period will last.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies how often the obligor must make the financing payments.
A free-form text field used to capture the payment frequency type if Other is selected as the payment frequency.
Describes history of payments on a loan. AKA: Loan History.
A representation of the history of payments applied to a loan.
When true, indicates fee is to be included in APR calculations.

terms.term: Payment Included In Jurisdiction High Cost Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the amount of the payment is included in the points and fees calculation appropriated to the jurisdiction of the subject property.
When true, indicates that the payments on the loan can increase after the closing.

terms.term: Payment Intangible Applicable Law State Code
terms.definition: The two-character abbreviation of the US State or Territory that the loan origination company uses to govern their lending agreements.
Describes the terms of a loan and loan payments, often emphasizing timing and amount of the first payment. AKA: Loan Payment Information Sheet, First Payment Letter.
The minimum dollar amount increase between two successive calculated principal and interest payments that requires an optional principal and interest payment to be offered.

When true, indicates a limited principal and interest payment should only be calculated if the new Interest rate is greater than the original interest rate. If false, the limited principal and interest payment is always calculated.
A portion of 100 that represents the minimum percent increase between two successive calculated principal and interest payments that requires an optional principal and interest payment to be offered.
A free-form text field describing the limited principal and interest payment option.
Specifies that the loan instrument allows the borrower(s) to determine and change on a month-to-month basis the amount of any payment to be paid on the loan for a specified period of time.

The date of the first scheduled recalculation (i.e., recast) of the payment options. Because of the unpredictability of the principal payments, it is necessary to periodically recalculate the payments needed to meet the defined amortization periods.

terms.term: Payment Option Minimum Payment Calculation Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field describing the method or formula used to calculate the minimum payment.

terms.term: Payment Option Minimum Payment Limit Payment Count
terms.definition: The maximum number of times the borrower is permitted to make the minimum payment within the time period specified by Payment Option Minimum Payment Limit Period Months Count.

terms.term: Payment Option Minimum Payment Limit Period Months Count
terms.definition: The number of months in the time period for which a limit to the number of minimum payments is prescribed.

terms.term: Payment Option Period Actual End Date
terms.definition: The payment due date when the set of payment options ceases to be in effect. This may be the result of either a scheduled recast of the payments or of an unscheduled recast that is triggered by other rules, such as a limit on the number of times a borrower can make the minimum payment in a period of time.

terms.term: Payment Option Period Scheduled End Date
terms.definition: The payment due date when the set of payment options is scheduled to no longer be in effect. This is based on the Payment Option Recast Frequency Months Count.
The payment due date when the set of payment options goes into effect.

terms.term: Payment Option Principal And Interest Payment Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the principal and interest payment associated with the payment option.

terms.term: Payment Option Pull The Note Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the payment option terms on the mortgage note are of an exceptional nature and require manual review by the servicer.

terms.term: Payment Option Recast Frequency Months Count
terms.definition: The number of months between scheduled recalculations (i.e., recasts) of the payment amounts for the various options.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of event that triggers a recalculation (i.e., recast) of the set of payment options.

terms.term: Payment Option Recast Trigger Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Payment Option Recast Trigger Type.
The payment due date for which the limited principal and interest payment option was elected.
The payment due date for which the limited principal and interest payment option period ends.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies an option that is available to the borrower for the payment amount for each installment on the loan.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Payment Option Type.
Identifies which system of rating codes is used within the Credit Liability Payment Pattern Data text string.

terms.term: Payment Pattern Rating Code Type Other Description
terms.definition: When Payment Pattern Rating Code Type has a value of Other, this element identifies the rating code system applied to the Credit Liability Payment Pattern Data text string.
If the proposed workout provides a reduction in the borrower's monthly payment, the pre-workout monthly payment minus the post-workout monthly payment.
The pre-workout monthly payment minus the post-workout monthly payment divided by the pre-workout monthly payment, expressed as a percentage.
The percentage of borrower monthly payment reduction shared by the program sponsor.
The day of the month on which the loan payment is to be remitted under the terms of the Mortgage.
The dollar amount of the payment reflected in the payment schedule on the TIL Disclosure document.

The date used to indicate the first date a scheduled payment is due. This date is used to indicate the start dates of any payments within a sequence of scheduled payments that may be reflected on the TIL Disclosure document.

terms.term: Payment Schedule Payment Varying To Amount
terms.definition: The lower payment amount of the monthly loan payment as reflected in the Payment Schedule on the TIL Disclosure document. This field is used to reflect the lower monthly payment amount in a range of monthly payment amounts typically calculated in an FHA transaction or a declining method PMI transaction and is required to be disclosed on the TIL Disclosure document.
The total number of payments due of a particular dollar amount reflected in the payment schedule of the TIL Disclosure document.

terms.term: Payment Schedule Principal And Interest Payment Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the portion of the total payment amount which is applied to the principal and interest due on the loan as reflected on the Payment Schedule for the loan.

A scenario in which monthly mortgage payments on an adjustable rate mortgage (ARM) rise so high that the borrower may not be able to afford the payments. Consumer protection guidelines regarding extremely low initial "teaser" rates, lifetime ceilings and annual caps are designed to prevent payment shock.
Specifies the state of the payment that is being reported.
Specifies the state of the payment that is being reported when Other is selected for Payment State Type.
The number of payments between the index values that should be used for index averaging.

terms.term: Payments Between Interest Rate Values Count
terms.definition: The number of payments between Interest Rate values that should be used if rate averaging is applicable.

terms.term: Payments Between Principal and Interest Payment Changes Count
terms.definition: The number of payments between scheduled principal and interest payment changes.

terms.term: Payments Between Rate Change Notices Count
terms.definition: The number of payment periods between interest rate change dates that notices are generated, if notices are not sent to the mortgagor for every change. If a loans interest rate changes every month but notices are only mailed once a year, 12 will be entered in this field.
The number of payments between rate changes.

terms.term: Payments To First Index Value Count
terms.definition: The number of payments from the interest rate change payment due date to the date of the first index rate to be used in index averaging.

terms.term: Payments to First Interest Rate Value Count
terms.definition: The number of payments from the interest rate change payment due date to the date of the first interest rate to be used if the rate averaging is applicable.
The account number associated with the debt that is being paid off as part of the closing transaction.
Specifies the type of action related to the liability payoff.
Specifies the other type of action related to the liability payoff when Other is selected.
The dollar amount for the debt that is being paid off as part of the closing transaction.
Specifies the order in which the payoff is applied relative to the scheduled payment.
The unpaid principal balance and escrow amounts to be used for payment in full of the mortgage or for closing sale of the property.
A statement detailing the unpaid principal balance, accrued interest, outstanding late charges, legal fees and all other amounts necessary to pay off the lender in full.
The date and time that a payoff order was submitted to the existing lien holder.
When true, indicates that the amount being paid does not fully satisfy the liability.
The payoff amount as a per diem (daily) dollar amount.
The dollar amount of the Prepayment Penalty charged on the account being paid in full.
A collection of values that specify the party making the request for payoff of the loan.

terms.term: Payoff Requested By Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the Payoff Requested By Type.
The date that the payoff was requested.

terms.term: Payoff Specified HUD1 Line Number Value
terms.definition: The line number on the HUD-1 where the Payoff is disclosed.
Confirms the remaining principle balance of a loan that is being paid off or refinanced, based on a defined close or pay date. AKA: Demand, Demand Statement.
The last valid date that is covered in the payoff amount.

The Prioritization Committee (PC) is responsible for providing guidance on organizational priorities and key initiatives. This includes overseeing the Business Executive Team; Senior Advisors; and the New Product Incubator. It further includes recommending to the MISMO Board of Directors which products should be MISMO Standards and which should be MISMO Collateral.

Adobe's Portable Document Format (PDF), which allows for exchange of documents between computer systems in an International Standards Organization (ISO) format (ISO 32000-1 ratified in January 2008). PDF is a file format for representing documents in a manner independent of the application software, hardware, and operating system used to create them and of the output device on which they are to be displayed or printed. ISO owns the copyright.
An ISO standard for an electronic document file format that enables long-term preservation.

An ISO standard for the long-term preservation of documents. In PDF/A-1: All fonts must be embedded, all color spaces must be device-independent, Javascript, embedded files, encryption, external content references, transparency, layers, and XFA forms data are prohibited, and standards-based metadata must be used.

An ISO standard for the long-term preservation of documents. Adds support for a number of additional features that are not allowed in PDF/A-1. Specifically: Transparency, Layers (also referred to as "optional content"), JPEG-2000 compression, Embedding of OpenType fonts, Digital signatures in accordance with the PAdES standard, Embedding of other PDF/A-2 documents
An ISO standard for the long-term preservation of documents. Adds to PDF/A-2 specification the ability to embed arbitrary documents in PDF/A-3 (such as XML data) in PDF/A files.

An institution that holds assets invested in long-term mortgages and high-grade stocks and bonds having acceptable yields and security. The purpose of a pension fund is to accumulate funds to hold and invest in such a manner that will provide retirement income to participating and eligible employees.
The stated maximum, expressed as a percent, to which the interest rate can increase to in this adjustment period.

terms.term: Per Change Factor of Index Percent
terms.definition: The percentage by which the new index is multiplied to arrive at a new interest rate. Most commonly used for Fannie Mae STABLE ARM products.
The stated minimum, expressed as a percent, to which the interest rate can decrease to in this adjustment period.

terms.term: Per Change Interest Rate Rounding Timing Type
terms.definition: Describes when the rate is rounded relative to checking other rules.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Decrease Rate Percent
terms.definition: The maximum number of percentage points by which the rate can decrease from the previous interest rate.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Increase Rate Percent
terms.definition: The maximum number of percentage points by which the rate can increase from the previous interest rate.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Principal And Interest Payment Amount
terms.definition: The maximum dollar amount of the principal and interest payment possible for the specified payment change.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Principal And Interest Payment Decrease Amount
terms.definition: The maximum dollar amount by which the principal and interest payment can decrease from the previous principal and interest payment.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Principal And Interest Payment Decrease Percent
terms.definition: The maximum number of percentage points by which the principal and interest payment can decrease from the previous principal and interest payment.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Principal And Interest Payment Increase Amount
terms.definition: The maximum dollar amount by which the principal and interest payment can increase from the previous principal and interest payment.

terms.term: Per Change Maximum Principal and Interest Payment Increase Percent
terms.definition: The maximum number of percentage points by which the principal and interest payment can increase from the previous principal and interest payment.

terms.term: Per Change Minimum Decrease Rate Percent
terms.definition: The smallest calculated interest rate decrease in a single adjustment period that requires an interest rate change. If the decrease is less than this percentage, then the interest rate will not change at the time of calculation.

terms.term: Per Change Minimum Increase Rate Percent
terms.definition: The smallest calculated interest rate increase in a single adjustment period that requires an interest rate change. If the increase is less than this percentage, then the interest rate will not change at the time of calculation.

terms.term: Per Change Minimum Principal And Interest Payment Amount
terms.definition: The minimum dollar amount of the principal and interest payment possible for the specified payment change.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Calculation Type
terms.definition: Describes the method employed to calculate the principal and interest payment of the loan.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Calculation Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Per Change Principal And Interest Payment Adjustment Calculation Method Type.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Payment Adjustment Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount by which the principal and interest payment adjusts.

terms.term: Per Change Principal and Interest Payment Adjustment Effective Date
terms.definition: The payment due date when the principal and interest payment per change adjustment rule first becomes applicable. The per change rule remains in effect unless another per change rule with a later date is present on the loan.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Payment Adjustment Effective Months Count
terms.definition: The number of months over which the set of note terms governing principal and interest payment adjustments are in effect.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Payment Adjustment Frequency Months Count
terms.definition: The number of months between payment adjustments, if the payment on the subject loan can change.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Payment Adjustment Percent
terms.definition: The percent by which the principal and interest payment adjusts.

terms.term: Per Change Principal And Interest Payment Minimum Decrease Rate Percent
terms.definition: The minimum percentage by which an ARM loans principal and interest payment must decrease relative to the prior principal and interest payment before it is actually changed on the loan. If the new principal and interest payment does not decrease by at least than this amount, the principal and interest payment remains the same.

terms.term: Per Change Principal and Interest Payment Minimum Increase Rate Percent
terms.definition: The minimum percentage by which an ARM loans principal and interest payment must increase relative to the prior principal and interest payment before it is actually changed on the loan. If the new principal and interest payment does not increase by at least this amount, the principal and interest payment remains the same.

terms.term: Per Change Rate Adjustment Calculation Method Description
terms.definition: Indicates how interest rate changes are to be calculated.

terms.term: Per Change Rate Adjustment Effective Date
terms.definition: The date when the interest rate per change adjustment rule first becomes applicable. The per change rule remains in effect unless another per change rule with a later date is present on the loan.

terms.term: Per Change Rate Adjustment Effective Months Count
terms.definition: The period of time, expressed in months, that the Interest Rate Per Change Adjustment Rule is in effect.

terms.term: Per Change Rate Adjustment Frequency Months Count
terms.definition: The number of months between rate adjustments, if the interest rate on the subject loan can change.

terms.term: Per Change Rate Adjustment Payments Count
terms.definition: The number of payments for which the Interest Rate Per Change Adjustment Rule is applicable.

A lease in which the rent on a property is determined as a percentage of gross receipts from the business. Although a straight percentage lease is occasionally encountered, most percentage leases contain a provision for a minimum rent amount.
Rent, computed as a percentage of retail sales above a breakpoint, paid by tenants under typical retail leases. Usually paid instead of or in addition to a specified minimum base rent.
A test performed on soil to determine its ability to absorb liquid, for either septic tank or construction purposes.
The elimination of claims against title.
Perfection is frequently used in the context of a security interest, and means those steps legally required to give a secured party an interest in property against a debtor's creditors.
The process of performing activities that occur throughout the lifecycle of a loan in servicing.

The process of handling the assumption of an existing loan by a new party. The servicer and/or investor underwrites and approves the assumption. The servicer retains information on the original borrower and adjusts the loan information to reflect the new borrower.
The process in which the regulated institution determines where AVMs in use have been aligned with the minimum protocols for the mandated AVM test criteria, as promulgated by the Dodd-Frank Act.

The process of writing off a full or partial loan balance that is unlikely to be collected. This is an accounting event where the creditor/investor no longer considers the amount owed as a source of profit but rather counts it as a loss.

Process of completing various functions related to performing a closing; including but not limited to gathering additional requirements as specified in the approval, generating and delivering the closing package to the Settlement Agent, and execution of the closing documents by the Borrower(s).
The process of generating and executing documents to secure the loan collateral, and disbursing the proceeds.

The process of collateral reconciliation must be performed on a monthly basis for certain MBS portfolios. This is the reconciliation of the normalized actual principal balance to the scheduled principal balance. If there is a discrepancy, the loan or pool is either overcollateralized, or undercollateralized. An undercollateralization must be resolved immediately. An overcollateralization must be resolved as soon as possible, using unscheduled principal collections.

The process of using debt collection activities in an attempt to bring a non-performing loan current, which includes establishing a QRPC contact with the borrower(s). QRPC is a uniform standard for communicating with the borrower, co-borrower, or a trusted advisor (collectively referred to as "borrower") about resolution of the mortgage loan delinquency. The servicer must make every attempt to achieve QRPC. The collections process may include short term repayment plans if conditions warrant.
Process in which the Document Custodian validates that loan data matches the collateral received.
The process of customer relationship management (CRM) between a servicer and borrower(s) including notifications, customer service, collections and statements.
The process of addressing borrower and associated customer concerns and requests to maintain a positive relationship. Examples: correspondence, required notifications.
Process of establishing formal management of business data assets, involving people, process and technology.
Process of establishing formal management of business data assets, and achieving access to the delivery of data across the enterprise to meet data consumption requirements.
Process of applying the practices, techniques and tools for achieving access to the delivery of data across the enterprise to meet data consumption requirements.

The process of transferring ownership of a property from the borrower to the servicer or investor to prevent foreclosure. If the Deed in Lieu is deemed a taxable event, this process includes reporting to both the Borrower and the IRS.

The process of removing a loan from the records of a servicer and investor by applying funds received as a result of a liquidation event. Includes ensuring that any appropriate third party notifications are made. In addition, the property may move into REO Administration.
Process of delivering the loan to the Investor.
Process of accounting for and obtaining documentation needed for the servicing or sale of the loan.
Process in which a mortgage loan is closed electronically through a secure environment in which closing documents are accessed, presented, and signed digitally.
Process in which the Notary Public and the Borrower(s) sign and notarize documents electronically while being in the same physical location.

Process of tracking, managing, certifying and safekeeping tamper evident authenticated copies of Electronic Notes (eNotes) and other electronic mortgage documents on behalf of Note owners and/or holders.

Process of delivering recordable documents to the appropriate government agency (typically the County Recorder or County Clerk) in an electronic format so that they become part of the public land records system.
The process of determining the sufficiency of escrow account funds per RESPA guidelines, including correspondence to the appropriate party.
The process of returning excess escrow funds to the borrower after application of payoff funds.

The process of taking the legal steps necessary to liquidate the loan and extinguish the debt. Federal and State regulations dictate this process. In addition, if HUD insured the loan, HUD guidance for Claims Without Conveyance of Title (CWCOT) may apply. State regulations vary substantially and it is common practice to utilize third party legal counsel where the property is located. Loss Mitigation efforts and Bankruptcy filings could have an impact on the timing of the foreclosure efforts.
Process of validating that closing has occurred, all closing conditions have been met, the wire amount is confirmed, and the disbursement of funds via wire transfer has been performed.
Process of obtaining the required government guaranty or government insurance.

terms.term: Perform GSE Presale Data Quality Check
terms.definition: The process of using GSE systems (Fannie Mae EarlyCheck or Freddie Mac Loan Quality Advisor) to check loan data for consistency, accuracy, and eligibility before the loan is sold.
Process in which the Lender uses financial strategies to preserve margin and protect from interest rate fluctuations before loans are sold.
Process of collecting loan-level data, deriving the Loan Application Register (LAR), and submitting the LAR to the CFPB.
The process in which prospective borrower(s) may attend homeownership education and/or counseling.
Process of closing a mortgage loan in which certain documents are printed and 'wet' signed on paper while other documents are electronically signed.
Process in which the Lender underwrites the loan using internal resources.
The process of verifying those items which are required to be escrowed per the terms of the note or the investor. In addition, HOA and Leasehold requirements are determined and set up for monitoring.
The process of reporting non-performing loan activities according to the terms of the servicing agreement. Non-performing loan activities are spelled out in the Default Management processes.
The process of ensuring that previously reported information accurately reflects the status of the loans in the investor's portfolio.
The process of remitting funds and reporting loan activities to investors according to the terms of the servicing agreement.

The process in which a servicer and/or investor works with a delinquent borrower to determine an alternative to foreclosure. This may be a liquidation or retention workout. Arriving at the solution is largely governed by the mortgage documents and/or investor rules. Federal and State regulations drive the timing of many default management efforts. Servicers are not permitted to move forward on a foreclosure if other loss mitigation efforts are underway.
Process of completing underwriting analysis, including credit and collateral, outside of an automated system.
The process of promoting the property for sale.
Perform registration and/or update of ownership of beneficial and/or servicing rights to MERS Registry as loans are acquired, assumed, modified, transferred, sold, paid-off or deactivated.
The process of reporting non-performing loan activities according to the MI contract. Non-performing loan activities are spelled out in the Default Management processes.
The process of reconciling loans in a servicer's portfolio with the associated mortgage insurer.

terms.term: Perform Mortgage Insurance Reporting Cycle Activities
terms.definition: The process of remitting funds and reporting loan activities to mortgage insurance companies based on the terms of the mortgage insurance company policies.
The process of verifying that the loan origination data was loaded accurately to the servicing system.
Process in which the Notary Public joins the Borrower(s) physically in the same location to execute ('wet' sign) and notarize documents using pen, paper, and where applicable, a notary stamp.
Process of tracking, managing, certifying and safekeeping paper Promissory Notes and other paper mortgage documents on behalf of Note owners and/or holders.

The process of assessing late charges, performing NSF reversals, and resolving suspense applications. Examples: Payoffs, Curtailments, Partial Payments. This process may vary depending on a loan's default status.
Process in which the Document Custodian confirms that it has examined and has in its possession the required documents for the loan, and has resolved any data discrepancies.
Process of preparing a closed loan to service or to sell.
The process of conveying the property to a third party buyer, back to the borrower or into REO administration.
Process of reviewing and collecting documents and data for accuracy to confirm the loan is ready for closing.
The process in which the lender verifies the accuracy of the loan file (such as title fees, insurance, and employment) prior to closing.

The process of securing and monitoring real estate acquired by a lender or investor which includes physical maintenance as well as any financial obligations to maintain the lien position on the property. This may include periodic claims for expense reimbursement of allowable maintenance costs.
The process of inspecting and maintaining a property to ensure value retention, comply with local laws and preserve marketability.
The process of tracking and paying escrowed items and other required items.
Process of validating the loans in a contract (pool) prior to settlement.
The process of reporting structured finance deals to the SEC under Regulation AB II according to the terms of the servicing agreement.

The process of assuring compliance to the servicing rules as published by regulatory agencies. This includes required notices, reporting to regulators, responding to consumer complaints, and tracking of activities.
The process in which the Notary Public and the Borrower(s) sign and notarize documents via a real-time online audio/video connection, without being in the same physical location.
Process of ensuring that the loan(s) meet investor and regulatory guidelines and are likely to be saleable.
Process of transferring funds associated with a whole loan or MBS contract.

The process of allowing a borrower to sell a property to a third party where the owner of the beneficial rights agrees to accept less than the amount owed to pay off the loan. The difference between the amount owed and the short sale amount may be a reportable tax event for the borrower.

terms.term: Perform State and Federal Compliance Tests
terms.definition: Process in which the Lender performs compliance tests throughout the origination life cycle.
Process of assessing the risks that arise from contractual third party relationships, in order to meet Regulatory Guidance.
Process of delivering recordable documents to the appropriate government agency (typically the County Recorder or County Clerk) so that they become part of the public land records system.
The process by which the servicer facilitates the transfer of beneficial rights from one party to another.
Process of tracking, managing, certifying and safekeeping Promissory Notes and other mortgage documents on behalf of Note owners and/or holders.

terms.term: Perform Verbal VOE or Verify in File
terms.definition: Process of completing a verbal, or reviewing a written, verification of employment.
A bond to guarantee performance of specified acts, such as the completion of construction of a property or off-site improvements.
Contains the name of the organization that performed the action.
Contains an identifier that was assigned by the system that performed the action.
Contains the name of the system used for performing the action.
A loan which has and continues to fulfill all of the terms, covenants, conditions or obligations required under the mortgage.
Indicates how many times the account was late 30 days during the Periodic Late Count Type specified.
Indicates how many times the account was late 60 days during the Periodic Late Count Type specified.
Indicates how many times the account was late 90 days during the Periodic Late Count Type specified.
Indicates how many times the account was late 120 days during the Periodic Late Count Type specified.
The base rate used to determine the periodic interest rate caps. All calculated interest rates are compared to this base rate to determine whether a limit has been reached for the interim period.
The payment due date when the periodic adjustment parameters begin.
The period of time, expressed in months, that the Adjustment Rule is in effect.
Indicates the time interval for the Late Count data. Possible intervals are First Year. Second Year, Third Year.

terms.term: Periodic Late Count Type Other Description
terms.definition: When Periodic Late Count Type is set to Other, enter the value here.
The maximum number of percentage points by which the interest rate can decrease from the Periodic Base Rate until the next base rate selection date.
The maximum number of percentage points by which the interest rate can increase from the Periodic Base Rate until the next base rate selection date.

terms.term: Periodic Next Base Rate Selection Date
terms.definition: The date on which a new base rate is to be determined for future periodic interest rate calculations.
The day of the month on which the borrower's payment is due.

terms.term: Periodic Payments Between Base Rates Count
terms.definition: The number of payments between interest rate changes for which the periodic cap is in effect. At the end of the period a new base rate is established.

A mortgage loan, usually covering development costs, interim loans, construction loans, financing expenses and marketing, administrative, legal and other costs. This loan differs from the construction loan in that financing goes into place after the project is constructed and open for occupancy. It is a long-term obligation, generally for a period of 10 years or more.
Confirms a person's permanent legal residency. AKA: Green Card, Temporary Permanent Residence ID, Residence Alien Card, Alien Registration.

Injury other than those arising out of bodily injury such as false arrest, malicious prosecution, wrongful entry or eviction, libel or slander or violation of privacy. The extent of such coverage may vary from policy to policy.
When true, indicates the appraiser performed a personal inspection to determine if the conditions or requirements stated in the appraisal have been satisfied.
Any property that is not real property. Also called "chattel."
The dollar amount of personal property included in the Sales Contract Amount.
Describes personal property and provides and estimation of value.
Indicates if there is personal property included in the contract for sale.
A basic study conducted to evaluate the environmental condition of real property and/or improvements.
A study of the environmental condition of property/ improvements that is more detailed and in-depth than a Phase I audit. May include groundwater testing or testing of soil.
An appraisal method whereby property value is derived by estimating the replacement cost of improvements, less estimated depreciation, plus the estimated land value. Synonymous with cost approach.
When true, indicates that the status for the property's physical soundness and livability is not acceptable. When false, indicates no deficiencies are present.
Decline in the value of a physical asset or real property resulting from normal usage, age, wear and tear, disintegration or action of the elements. Depreciation can be curable or incurable.
When true, indicates that the highest and best use of the property is physically possible.
A loan made jointly by two or more lenders on the same property under one mortgage or trust deed.
Indicates a second lien being carried under the same loan number as a first mortgage. Generally one mortgage is covered by two notes and the borrower makes one combined payment.
Loan applications in process that have not yet closed.
Percentage of loan applications which fail to close, usually because of changes in interest rates.
Principal, Interest, Taxes and Insurance
The ratio of principal, interest, taxes and insurance to income.
See Public Key Infrastructure.
The process of reviewing a loan to determine need for placement of appropriate payment application stops based on default status. Funds received are typically applied to a suspense account.
A bond with a fixed paydown schedule over a specified period of time, which eliminates cash flow uncertainty due to prepayments.

A comprehensive development plan for a large land area. A PUD usually includes residences, roads, schools, recreational facilities, commercial, office and industrial areas. Also, a subdivision having lots or areas owned in common and reserved for the use of some or all of the owners of the separately owned lots.

A local or regional organization, normally a government agency, responsible for the preparation and adoption of comprehensive long-term general plans for the physical development of property within its jurisdiction.
Architectural and engineering drawings and specifications for construction of a building or project. They include a description of materials to be used and the manner in which they are to be applied.
A map representing a piece of land subdivided into lots with streets, boundaries, easements and dimensions shown thereon.
The block number assigned to a parcel of real property on a subdivision plat.
A book showing the lots and legal descriptions of the subdivisions of an area, usually recorded and kept in city and county government offices.
The number of the plat book where the plat map is stored in the office of the county recorder.
A unique number assigned to each building on a condominium plat.
A computer index code assigned by the county to identify the plat in the tract index database.
The unique number assigned to a plat map by a county recorder at the time of recording.
The lot number assigned to a parcel of real property on a subdivision plat.
The name used to identify the plat in the legal description of the property (assigned to the plat by the party platting the land).

Indicates that the property is subject to Inclusionary zoning, a land-use concept in which builders include a certain amount of affordable housing units for eligible borrowers, in exchange for considerations, such as a "density bonus" along with other incentives from the jurisdiction.
A free-form text field describing the purpose, function or contents of a property information report.
Indicates the name or title of the property information report.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies a particular property information service.
The physical review/evaluation of a property to determine its current structural condition, to report any deferred maintenance and/or environmental problems and to verify leasing status.
The date the property inspection was ordered.
Identifies the scope of the inspection performed and the type of inspector that is performing the inspection.

terms.term: Property Inspection Purpose Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form field used to capture additional information when the selection for Property Inspection Purpose Type is Other.

Describes the condition of the subject property, or any of a variety of building systems or interior or exterior elements of the structure, or aspects of the surrounding property (such as water or soil).
Free form commentary about the request for the inspection.
Free form commentary about the results of the inspection.
Specifies the extent of the inspection.
A free-form field used to capture additional information when the selection for Property Inspection Type is Other.
Indicates whether a documented inspection of the property has been waived.
Establishes a commitment to issue property insurance pending payment.

Describes the information regarding the risk covered by the insurance policy, including the name of the insurance company, its address, name of the policy holder, starting and ending dates of coverage, the actual coverage given in the contract, including locations and amounts.
Establishes the terms and conditions of the contract for insurance covering the subject property.
Explains lenders right to approve a borrower's choice of insurance company and the required specifics of the insurance such as deductible, premium and term. AKA: Agreement to Provide Insurance.

Identifies the components of the bundle of rights inherent in the ownership of real estate is what is bought and sold in a real property transaction. In an appraisal, the rights being appraised must be stated, because any limitation on the rights of ownership may affect property value. This observation is at the property level versus the party level (individual or entity) named as the owner of such right. This is different than the ownership rights that may be recorded with the lien transaction.

terms.term: Property Interest Rights Appraised Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Interest Rights Appraised Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the method by which the interior inspection was conducted.
The type of license or certificate to operate as a right of use issued by a local jurisdiction for the property.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property License Type.
An individual or company responsible for the daily and long range management of the operations of a property.
Indicates whether the market value of a property has decreased. Generally used when updating a previous appraisal on the same property.
When true, indicates the property includes commercial space set aside to operate a business.

terms.term: Property Most Recent Valuation Order Date
terms.definition: The date that the most recent valuation of the property was ordered.

terms.term: Property Non Conforming To Surrounding Area Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that describes why the property does not conform or is not similar to other properties in the surrounding area.

terms.term: Property Non Conforming To Surrounding Area Reason Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the reasons the property does not conform or is not similar to other properties in the surrounding area.

terms.term: Property Non Conforming To Surrounding Area Reason Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Property Non Conforming To Surrounding Area Reason Type.
A positive, whole number that identifies the position of the property in the valuation analysis.
The original cost of acquiring the entire property - land and structure. This is used for refinance loans.

Any person who owns an interest in the real property securing the mortgage loan, either before or after the loan is originated, other than a person whose only interest in the real property is as a lien holder.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the time frame of a party's ownership of a property.
Indicates the specific type of Partial Ownership Interest on the property as evaluated in the appraisal process. May also be referred to as a fractional ownership interest.

terms.term: Property Partial Interest Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Partial Interest Type.
When true, indicates that photo of the property is required as part of the inspection.
Specifies the type of photo desired or included with the inspection.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Photo Type.
The date the property preservation efforts were completed.
Specifies the action taken to preserve and protect the property.

terms.term: Property Preservation Action Type Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the PropertyPreservationActionType.

terms.term: Property Preservation Action Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Preservation Action Type.
The date of the property preservation status.
Specifies the status of the Property Preservation Action Type.

terms.term: Property Preservation Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Preservation Status Type.
Indicates that the property has been previously occupied.
When true, indicates that the property's use is primarily residential when the property includes commercial space set aside to operate a business.

terms.term: Property Primary Entry Exit Method Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the primary ingress and/or egress method for the property.

terms.term: Property Primary Entry Exit Method Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Property Primary Entry Exit Method Type.

terms.term: Property Proposed Clean Energy Lien Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the property will be subject to a property clean energy lien that could take precedence over the first mortgage lien including PACE loan or other similar liens.
Property Records Industry Association: Country recorders who developed a DTD for recording closing information only.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the existence or likelihood of rent control on the property.
The dollar amount that would be needed to replace or restore the property to its original condition.
A technique for estimating the value of property as a whole, when neither the value of the land nor the building can be estimated by itself.
A free-form text field describing the different types of property rights not included as part of the valuation.
When true, the property has been seized and no longer available for foreclosure.
Indicates whether some or all of the down payment was funded by the Property Seller either directly or indirectly through a community or religious nonprofit.
The month in a calendar year in which the construction of the structure was completed.
The calendar year in which the construction of the structure was completed.

terms.term: Property Structure Built Year Estimated Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the calendar year in which construction of the structure was completed is an estimate.

terms.term: Property Structure Habitable Year Round Indicator
terms.definition: Indicates that the structure or improvement is habitable year round.

terms.term: Property Tax Abatements Or Exemptions Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that a tax reduction or exemption has been granted.
The end of year of the assessment (tax authority valuation) used for this tax year.
The start year of the assessment (tax authority valuation) used for this tax year.
A free-form text field used to describe atypical taxes or special assessments.
This is the date the tax certificate was issued signifying the assessment cutoff date for the upcoming year, e.g. the cert date in CA is always the first of the year. Other states may vary.
A free-form text field used to further describe taxes paid to a tax authority.

terms.term: Property Tax County Rate Area Identifier
terms.definition: The tax area or region identifier used by the county tax authority for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier).
When true, indicates that the real estate taxes are deferred.
Indicates that the owner is delinquent on taxes from a taxing authority or jurisdiction.
The end year of the Subject property tax year for the information.
Describes the type of tax exemption (e.g. Homestead, Senior, Disabled, etc.) this property has for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier).
Indicates that the subject property has a tax exemption for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier). See Property Tax Exemption.
The taxable value of the structure or structures on the property as separate from the land itself for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier).
The taxable value of the property land without improvements for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier).

terms.term: Property Tax Paid By Borrower Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the real estate taxes were paid directly to the taxing authority by the borrower.
Records the amount of the special tax specified by Property Tax Special Description.
A free-form text field used to describe a category of special tax for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier).

terms.term: Property Tax To Value Rate Percent
terms.definition: The ratio of the property value (Property Tax Total Taxable Value Amount) to this year tax amounts (Property Tax Real Estate Total Tax Amount). For example, a $500,000 property paying $2,500.

terms.term: Property Tax Total Assessed Value Amount
terms.definition: Combined value of the assessed land and improvements of the property (I.e. structures) for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier).

terms.term: Property Tax Total Special Tax Amount
terms.definition: The total of all of the special real estate taxes of the property for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier) across all tax jurisdictions and authorities. This is the amount assessed for the tax year, not the amount paid. (see Property Tax Special).

The total of all of the real estate taxes of the property for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier) across all tax jurisdictions and authorities. This is the amount assessed for the tax year, not the amount paid. This amount includes all special taxes (see Property Tax Special).

terms.term: Property Tax Total Tax Without Special Assessments Amount
terms.definition: The total of all of the real estate taxes of the property for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier) across all tax jurisdictions and authorities. This is the amount assessed for the tax year, not the amount paid. This amount DOES NOT include special taxes (see Property Tax Special Amount).

terms.term: Property Tax Total Taxable Value Amount
terms.definition: Combined total taxable value of the land and improvements of the property for this tax year (Property Tax Year Identifier) across all tax jurisdictions and authorities. This value is the total value less the exemption and any other adjustments.
Indicates that the real estate taxes of the subject property are typical for the area and type of property.
The tax year of the subject property associated with the information provided.

terms.term: Property Title Transfer Inspection Required Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to comment on the title transfer inspections of the property.

terms.term: Property Title Transfer Inspection Required Indicator
terms.definition: Indicates that an inspection of the property is required before the title can be transferred.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains a colloquial phrase to describe the property type. (e.g. Single Family Detached, SFD)

terms.term: Property Typical Marketing Days Duration Type
terms.definition: Specifies the estimated marketing duration in terms of days for the subject property before it is sold. The use of days to indicate the marketing duration is specific to the Employee Relocation Appraisal Forms.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the intended usage of the property by the borrower.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Usage Type.
The date the property was first determined to be vacant as determined by the date reported on an inspection report.
An unstructured name that identifies the municipality where the vacant property has been registered.
The date associated with the specified PropertyVacancyRegistrationStatusType.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the registration status of a vacant property with the applicable municipality.

terms.term: Property Vacancy Registration Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the PropertyVacancyRegistrationStatusType.
The age of the property valuation expressed in days, calculated by taking the current date minus the Property Valuation Effective Date.
Statement of value of the property from a valid property valuation source.
A free-form text field used to provide commentary on the property value analysis.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the conclusions of the appraisal that there may be a dependency on future repairs or activities.

terms.term: Property Valuation Conditional Conclusion Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Valuation Conditional Conclusion Type.
Effective date of the property valuation on the subject property.
The name or number assigned to a form by the form author.
Specifies the form used to provide the property valuation.

terms.term: Property Valuation Form Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Valuation Form Type.
The version identifier for the property valuation form, as assigned by the publisher of the form.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the method by which the property value was assessed.

terms.term: Property Valuation Method Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture a description of the Property Valuation Method Type when Other is selected.
Provides a categorization for valuation products in terms of USPAP compliance and level of professional services required.

terms.term: Property Valuation Service Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field which contains the description of the categorization for valuation products when Other is selected as the Property Valuation Service Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies that the subject property valuation amount is the amount at the point of origination or a subsequent evaluation.
Specifies the property zoning category. The zoning category is not the official legal description.

terms.term: Property Zoning Category Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Property Zoning Category Type.
A free-form text field describing the terms of the loan or financing proposed in the sales transaction as determined in the analysis of the Sales Contract or transaction details by the appraiser.
Type of lease used in cooperative buildings that defines the rights of a tenant or shareholder to occupy a particular dwelling unit.
The dollar amount of the Proration Item Type.
The start date for calculating the total number of days covered by the proration item.
The end date for calculating the total number of days covered by the proration item, inclusive of this date.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a cost already paid by one party that must be prorated at the time of loan closing and allocated between a property seller, homebuyer, or other parties to a real estate transaction.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Proration Item Type.
A written proposal or offering to sell an investment that outlines all details pertinent to the investment.
The date of the Coastal Barrier Resources Area (CBRA) or Otherwise Protected Area (OPA).
Indicates if the building/mobile home is within a Coastal Barrier Resources Area (CBRA) or Otherwise Protected Area (OPA).
Rules governing transmitting and receiving of data.
Process of generating all required loan disclosures and documents and providing them to the Borrower(s) within a specified number of days after application.
The actual amount of a provided service.

terms.term: Provided Service Borrower Can Shop For Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the specified service can be selected independent of any lender recommendation.
A free-form text field describing a provided service.
The estimated amount of a provided service.

terms.term: Provider Chosen From Lender List Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the borrower chose the service provider from the lender's service providers list.
A free-form text field used to describe the proximity of a comparable property to the subject property.

terms.term: Proximity To Subject Distance Linear Measure
terms.definition: A linear measurement that specifies the linear distance the comparable property is from the subject property. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Linear Unit Of Measure Type.
A public agency created by state or local governments to finance or operate low-income housing.

Public Key Infrastructure term. The published or publicly available key of a two- Key Pair that are mathematically linked. By encrypting a message with the Public Key, only the holder of the Private Key can decrypt the message. Likewise, the holder of the Private Key can encrypt messages that can only be decrypted by the Public Key, thus proving that a person is the holder of the Private Key.
See Digital Certificate.

Public Key Infrastructure term. A method requiring two unique software keys for decrypting data, one public and one private. Data is encrypted using the published Public Key, and the unpublished Private Key is used to decrypt the data.

A cryptographic framework that provides the basis for establishing and maintaining a trustworthy networking environment through the generation and distribution of keys and Digital Certificates. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
A report normally issued by a state agency before the sale of lots in a subdivision. The report is a factual description of the subdivided property.
An association of investment banking firms that trades certain kinds of government-related securities, including mortgage-backed securities.

terms.term: Public Sewer Utility Available Not Connected Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that there is a public sewer system available but not connected to the subject property. When false, indicates that a public sewer system is not available.
A person appointed or required by law to execute and administer a trust.

terms.term: Public Water Utility Available Not Connected Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that there is public water available but not connected to the subject property. When false, indicates that public water is not available.
A value from a MISMO list that represents the name of the guide and its publisher used as a data source in a valuation process.

terms.term: Published Valuation Source Guide Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Published Valuation Source Guide Type.
Planned Unit Development

When true, indicates that the property is located within a Planned Unit Development (PUD). A PUD is a project or subdivision that consists of common property and / or improvements that are owned and maintained by an owners’ association for the benefit and use of the individual unit owners.
A written agreement between a buyer and seller of real property, setting forth the price and terms of sale.
The dollar amount of the Purchase Credit Type that is on the loan application.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the party contributing credits to the transaction exclusive of the mortgage financing.

terms.term: Purchase Credit Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture a description of the Purchase Credit Source Type when Other is selected.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies monetary credits commonly accepted as valid sources of borrower funds to close a mortgage loan transaction excluding adding amounts to the note amount.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Purchase Credit Type.
The total dollar amount paid by the borrower for the property. The purchase price is presented on the offer to purchase.
The result of subtracting financing and sales concession amounts above those allowed by guidelines from the Purchase Price Amount of the subject property.
A mortgage a purchaser of real property gives a seller as all or part of the consideration in the sales transaction.

Aggregate value of a servicing portfolio obtained from a source outside the purchasing company. It is classified as an intangible asset for both financial accounting and regulatory reporting purposes.
The process, if allowed by law, where an unsecured money judgement is filed against the borrower because the foreclosure sale funds are insufficient to pay the total debt.
A contract granting the right, but not the obligation, to sell the underlying security at a specified price (the strike price) at any time prior to the expiration date. See CALL OPTION.
The acquisition of additional properties through the refinancing of properties already owned.
Qualified Mortgage
