The difference between the annual percentage rate (APR) and the average prime offer rate (APOR) for ATR/QM analysis.
The process which determines whether an applicant can be approved for a mortgage loan.
A home loan that meets standards set forth by the federal government that prohibit or limit certain high-risk products and features.

terms.term: Qualified Mortgage Highest Rate Debt Expense Ratio Percent
terms.definition: The ratio of all debt payments of the borrowers, including proposed housing expenses, to the qualifying income of the borrowers (back-end ratio) based on the highest interest rate that may apply during the first five years of principal and interest payments. Specific to Qualified Mortgage only.
When true, indicates the loan is determined to be a qualified mortgage under Regulation Z requirements.

terms.term: Qualified Mortgage Minimum Required FICO Score Value
terms.definition: Specifies the minimum FICO Score required for purposes of determining if the loan is exempt from Ability To Repay.

terms.term: Qualified Mortgage Short Reset ARM_APR Percent
terms.definition: The annual percentage rate for the loan based on the accepted industry standard defined by Regulation Z (Section 12 C.F.R. 1026.43(e)(2)(vi) used for Qualified Mortgages that have an interest rate change within the first five years after the date on which the first regular periodic payment is due.
Specifies the GSE Guidelines by which Temporary Qualified Mortgage eligibility was determined.

terms.term: Qualified Mortgage Total Points And Fees Threshold Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of points and fees dollar amount limit established by Regulation Z, Truth in Lending. This amount is used in calculations for Qualified Mortgage purposes.

terms.term: Qualified Mortgage Total Points And Fees Threshold Percent
terms.definition: The total amount of points and fees percentage limit established by Regulation Z, Truth in Lending. This amount is used in calculations for Qualified Mortgage purposes.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the specific standard used to satisfy Regulation Z Qualified Mortgage standards.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Qualified Mortgage Type.
When true indicates that this issue was determined by a party to be a Qualified Written Request (QWR) per RESPA regulations.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of mortgage payment used to qualify the obligor(s) for the loan.
A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the Qualifying Method Type.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is selected as the Qualifying Method Type.
The MI payment amount used to qualify the borrower for a loan.
The PITI used to qualify the borrower for a loan, calculated using the investor or regulator specified interest rate that is higher than the initial rate.

terms.term: Qualifying Principal And Interest Payment Amount
terms.definition: The principal and interest payment amount used to qualify the borrower for a loan; calculated using an investor or regulator specified interest rate.
The rate used to calculate the borrower's payment (PITI) to qualify the borrower for the subject mortgage.
Indicates what interest rate was used to qualify the borrower in correlation with the note rate.
A free-form text field used to capture the Qualifying Rate type if Other is selected.
Policies and procedures designed to maintain optimal levels of quality, accuracy, and efficiency in the production, selling and servicing of mortgage loans.
A free-form text field used to describe in detail the quality rating of the identified component.
A rating of the quality of the identified component type.
A system of projecting construction costs through a detailed estimate of required materials, overhead and labor to be used in new building construction.

Surveying Sections (one mile by one mile) are divided into quarters that are half-mile by half-mile (160 acre) squares. These are identified as the Northeast, Northwest, Southwest and Southeast quarter sections. Quarter sections can also be divided into individual quarters resulting in quarter-quarter sections containing 40 acres.
An asset that is immediately convertible to cash. Also called a "liquid asset."
The right of an owner to the use of property without disturbance.
Legal action taken to eliminate any interest or claim to property by others; the procedure used to perfect title when a quitclaim deed is unobtainable.
A deed relinquishing all interest, title or claim an owner has in a property. A quitclaim deed implies no warranty.
See BID.
When true, indicates the Borrower answered "yes" to the statement: "I do not wish to furnish the HMDA information."
An invisible, odorless gas that may enter a structure through cracks or holes in basement floors. Radon is a suspected carcinogen.
A rise in price following a sudden decline.

Surveying demarcations used in the Public Land Survey System. Range lines run north and south so as to measure east and west distances in columns. Range lines are spaced every six (6) miles. Commonly used in a grid along with Township and Section to describe an area of land at the county level.
Percentage to be added to current or original interest rate, if the interest rate on the subject loan can change.
A document that notifies the borrower that the interest rate on the ARM loan has changed.

Establishes that the parties to a loan transaction have fixed (locked) specific proposed terms of the loan for a specified period. Terms may include such items as interest rate, yield, term, points, fees, expiration and product type.

terms.term: Rate Lock Agreement: Business To Business
terms.definition: A written rate lock agreement between two business parties.

terms.term: Rate Lock Agreement: Business To Consumer
terms.definition: A written rate lock agreement between a broker or lender and a consumer.
Specifies the method by which the rate lock period will be determined.

terms.term: Rate Of Return On Total Capital (ROR)
terms.definition: The ratio of net operating income to total capital investment. Often called the "free and clear return" or the "overall rate."
Indicates to the MI provider that requesting organization desires all appropriate MI products be considered and returned in the rate quote response.
Indicates to the MI provider that all available comparison calculations be executed comparing various MI products being requested.
Indicates the type of data set included with the request. Initial limited data, or complete detail data.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Rate Quote Type.
The refinance of an existing mortgage balance solely to lower the interest rate.
A residential underwriting procedure used to compute the proposed housing expense plus other long-term debt expenses as a percentage of monthly income.

Method of qualifying which divides the monthly mortgage payment by the gross monthly income of the borrower (housing or first ratio) and then divides the monthly mortgage payment and monthly debt payments by the gross monthly income (debt or second ratio).
Land in its natural state, having no physical improvements such as grading, sewers or structures.
Establishes that the borrower will reinstitute a mortgage debt after bankruptcy proceedings are completed.
See REAL PROPERTY.
A count of the number of real estate agents that are involved in the transaction based on the sales contract.
Describes the type of real estate agent.

terms.term: Real Estate Agent Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to describe the type of real estate agent if Other is selected as the real estate agent type.

terms.term: Real Estate Finance Security Management Organization (REFSMO)
terms.definition: Real Estate Finance Security Management Organization, the security workgroup of the Mortgage Industry Standards Maintenance Organization (MISMO), created to develop, promote, and maintain voluntary electronic commerce security standards for the mortgage industry.
An investment vehicle where title to real estate assets is held and managed by one or more trustees who control acquisitions and investments much like a mutual fund.
A vehicle for issuing multiclass mortgage-backed securities which allows the issuer to treat the security as a sale of assets for tax and accounting purposes.
Property a lender acquires as the result of foreclosure.

Federal law which regulates the settlement practices within the real estate industry. This law requires the provision of Good Faith Estimates of Closing Costs, prohibits kickbacks for referrals of related services and standardizes the closing with a required form and format (HUD-1). RESPA also regulates the administration of escrow accounts.
A group of investors who pool funds for investment in real property.
Local government taxes levied on the ownership of real estate. Also known as "real estate property taxes."
Land and improvements permanently attached to it, such as buildings. In some states, this term is synonymous with the term "real estate."
The dollar amount of real property included in the Sales Contract Amount.

A person licensed to sell and/or lease real property, acting as an agent for others, and who is a member of a local real estate board affiliated with the National Association of Realtors (NAR). Realtor is a registered trademark of the NAR.
Code values exchanged between business partners relating to the reason for a service request or response.
A free-form text field describing the Reason Code.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains additional details about the reason for a service request or response.

terms.term: Reason For MI Policy Cancellation Type
terms.definition: The reason for the cancellation of Active/In Force MI Coverage.

terms.term: Reason For MI Policy Cancellation Type Other Description
terms.definition: Used to further define ReasonForMIPolicyCancellationType when Other is selected.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the reason the appraiser did not include the property in the Sales Comparison Approach.

terms.term: Reason Property Not Used Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Reason Property Not Used Type.
The revaluation of property for ad valorem tax purposes.
The rate at which an equity investment will be recouped over the life of the investment; the return of investment capital.
Modification of the terms of an existing mortgage to cure delinquency.
Confirms the payment or exchange of a good or service.
Process of accepting documentation required to satisfy outstanding closing conditions.

terms.term: Receive Final Title Insurance Policy and Endorsements
terms.definition: Process of receiving and reviewing the requested Title Insurance Policy and Endorsements

Process of receiving Closing Disclosure (CD) updates via a secure collaboration portal, email, or phone. The Closer reconciles the CD updates to the loan origination system in order to produce the final CD for Closing.

An impartial person appointed by the court to administer properties involved in foreclosure or other litigation, to receive its rents and profits and apply or dispose of them at the direction of the court.

terms.term: Recertification Of Family Income And Composition
terms.definition: The Recertification of Family Income and Composition document is used in HUD Section 235(b) loans. It is sent by lenders to individual borrowers to obtain the information necessary to determine family income and composition. Mortgagees maintain copies for audit purposes. HUD-93101 (4/91).

terms.term: Recertification Of Family Income Statistical Report
terms.definition: Recertification of Family Income and Composition Statistical Report. HUD-93101-A (12/91). Used in HUD Section 235 loans.

The ability of AI systems to identify and classify data, objects, patterns, speech, images, or other inputs. It involves processes such as: 1) Pattern Recognition: Detecting patterns and regularities in data. 2) Image Recognition: Identifying and classifying objects within digital images and videos. 3) Speech Recognition: Interpreting and processing human speech into digital text for further analysis or action.
A type of machine learning system that analyzes patterns in user behavior to suggest items that the user is likely to find interesting or relevant.
The last step in the appraisal process in which all data are compared and the approaches to value considered to arrive at a final estimate of value.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the outcome of the reconsideration of value.
When true, indicates that a reconsideration of value has been requested.

terms.term: Reconsideration Of Value Requested By Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the party that initiated the request for reconsideration of value.
The date the appraiser completed the reconsideration of value.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents whether the reconsideration of value request resulted in a change to the Opinion of Market Value.
An instrument used to transfer title from a trustee to the equitable owner of real estate, used when the performance of debt is satisfied under the terms of a deed of trust.
Information that is inscribed on a tangible medium or that is stored in an electronic or other medium and is retrievable in perceivable form.
When true, indicates the user requested a detailed combination of Return Transcripts and Account Transcripts which contain supplemental financial status. Used on the IRS Form 4506T and 4506-C.
Process of recording the security instrument in the public land records
Fees charged by a local government to record the documents of a real estate transaction.
Date and time the document was recorded by recorder.
The filing of documents or details of a legal document to make them a matter of public record. Usually requires the witnessing and notarizing of the document or instrument to be recorded.
Amount of Exemption from recording fees.
A coded value defined by the recording jurisdiction that represents a valid exemption.
Description of exemptions for document recording.

The total amount of all fees exempted from remittance to the county recorder for recording a single document. (Depending on state laws and local ordinances there may not be a direct relationship between Recording Endorsement Exemptions and RESPA Fees.)

The amount of a fee required for recording a document. Multiple fees could be required for a single document. (Depending on state laws and local ordinances there may not be a direct relationship between Recording Fee and RESPA Fees.)

Description of an individual fee required for recording a document. This could include document recording fees, mortgage taxes, various conveyance taxes, etc. (Depending on state laws and local ordinances there may not be a direct relationship between Recording Fee and RESPA Fees.)

The total amount of all fees required to be remitted to the county recorder for recording a single document. (Depending on state laws and local ordinances there may not be a direct relationship between Recording Endorsement Fees and RESPA Fees.)
Endorsement identification number assigned to each recording transaction, such as an audit number. This differs from the Recording Endorsement Instrument Number.
Describes the source and purpose of the recording endorsement information.
A free-form text field used to capture the Recording Endorsement Type if Other is selected.
A free-form text field for a description of the exact error.
Code used by recorder in indexing software. Specific to county where document is recorded.
The name of the Recording Jurisdiction in which the subject property resides.
The type of Recording Jurisdiction in which the subject property is located.
The description of the Recording Jurisdiction Type when Other is selected from the enumerated list.
Name of the County Recording Official.
Number of pages in document being recorded.
The actual identifying alphanumeric entry.
This enumerated attribute identifies what agency the transaction is intended for.

terms.term: Recording Transaction Identifier Type Other Description
terms.definition: A description of the type of transaction when Other is selected in the enumerated list.

A type of mortgage loan in which the lender's remedies in the event of borrower default are unlimited, extending beyond the property to the borrower's personal assets. In secondary marketing, a loan that the lender must repurchase in the case of loan default or other defect.

terms.term: Recoverable Corporate Advance Balance from Borrower Amount
terms.definition: Monies advanced on the loan (i.e. delinquency expense, tax penalty, repairs, etc.) that are recoverable from the borrower.

terms.term: Recoverable Corporate Advance Balance from Third Party Amount
terms.definition: Monies advanced on the loan (i.e. delinquency expense, tax penalty, repairs, etc.) that are recoverable from a third party.

terms.term: Recoverable Corporate Advance From Borrower Amount Total Amount
terms.definition: Provides an arithmetic total of the Recoverable Corporate Advance From Borrower Amount data items within the Loan container in this data set.

terms.term: Recoverable Corporate Advance From Third Party Amount Total Amount
terms.definition: Provides an arithmetic total of the Recoverable Corporate Advance From Third Party Amount data items within the Loan container in this data set.
Tangible, depreciable property held for the production of income.
Time by which services must be resumed to business-critical activities and/or their dependencies and any relevant data recovered and restored.
A warning term used to indicate further analysis is warranted.
Arbitrary denial of real estate loan applications in certain geographical areas, without considering individual applicant qualifications.
When true, indicates the borrower's right to redeem the property has been exercised.
The time allowed by law in some states during which mortgagors may buy back their foreclosed properties by paying the balance owed on their delinquent mortgages, plus interest and fees.
The date the redemption period expires in applicable states.
The number of months the borrower can redeem the property after a foreclosure sale has occurred. The redemption period is based on the property's geographic location.
A mortgage which carries a higher interest rate in exchange for no points and/or a credit towards other closing costs from the lender.

terms.term: Refer To Closing Disclosure For Loan Fees Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that the Closing Disclosure document should be used to get a reference list of fees.
The process in which the servicer begins the foreclosure activities.

The Reference Model in is an abstract framework or domain-specific ontology consisting of an interlinked set of clearly defined concepts produced by an expert or body of experts in order to encourage clear communication. A Reference Model can represent the component parts of any consistent idea, from business functions to system components, as long as it represents a complete set. This frame of reference can then be used to communicate ideas clearly among members of the same community.

Technology specific physical implementation of the MISMO Platform Independent Logical Data Model. Most likely created as a derivative from a Platform Specific LDM. Represents a technical organization of information including data and documentation needed to support mortgage industry business processes. The Reference Model includes implementation specific schema and a Logical Data Dictionary.

The XML Reference Model is an industry standard organization of information, including data and documentation, needed to conduct a real estate transaction. It includes the MISMO XML Logical Data Dictionary, an XML Schema representation of data and relationships, and other supporting material

This attribute describes how the content of a REFERENCE or ObjectURL element is signed using XML digital signatures. This instructs systems about which transformation, if any, needs to be applied to the REFERENCE or ObjectURL element before validating existing SYSTEM_SIGNATURES or applying new ones and what transformations are prohibited.

Money or a gift a company furnishes to another company as a reward for directing borrowers to it for services. The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) prohibits payment of certain referral or finder's fees and requires disclosure of others.
The dollar amount applied to assets acquired with the proceeds from a refinance transaction.
The amount of cash the borrower will receive at the closing of the loan on a refinance transaction.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that classifies a refinanced loan.
Percentage of Base Loan Amount that will be dispersed as cash to the borrower.
Documentation showing how the total cost of refinancing was calculated.

Documentation showing how the total cost of refinancing was calculated in accordance with the Anti-Churning Disclosure form to ensure that the mortgagor is not being induced to refinance his/her existing HECM without benefit to the mortgagor and/or solely for the benefit of the mortgagee.
The dollar amount applied to debt reduction from the proceeds from refinance transaction.
The dollar amount applied to home improvements from the proceeds from a refinance transaction.
The total dollar amount of improvements that are either made or to be made at time of refinance.
Specifies whether the improvements associated with a refinance have been made to the property or if they are planned.

terms.term: Refinance Including Debts To Be Paid Off Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of all debt that is to be repaid with funds from refinancing the mortgage loan on the subject property.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies who initiated the refinance.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Refinance Initiator Type.
Specifies the primary purpose of the refinance.

terms.term: Refinance Primary Purpose Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Refinance Primary Purpose Type.
Identifies the refinance program associated with the loan as identified by a specific entity.
A free-form text field describing the improvements to be made on property being refinanced.
When true, indicates that the subject loan is refinanced with the current holder, current servicer or an affiliate of either.
The repayment of a debt from the proceeds of a new loan using the same property as security.

terms.term: Refund Of Overpaid Interest Calendar Year Amount
terms.definition: The amount of overpaid interest refunded to the borrower for the calendar year.
When true, indicates the refund of any fees related to the request for copy or transcript of tax return, will be made to the third party identified within the related IRS Form 4506.
Indicates whether the Application Fee is refundable.
A shopping center with a gross leasable area of 300,000 to 1,000,000 square feet or more, and having one or more major department stores as anchor tenants.
Process in which the Lender registers the eNote on the MERS eRegistry
Process of registering a loan with Mortgage Electronic Registration Systems (MERS) and obtaining a Mortgage Identification Number (MIN).

A domain name is an identification label that defines a realm of administrative autonomy, authority, or control in the Internet, based on the Domain Name System (DNS). The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) has overall responsibility for managing the DNS. Domain names are often seen in analogy to real estate in that (1) domain names are foundations on which a website (like a house or commercial building) can be built and (2) the highest "quality" domain names, like sought-after real estate, tend to carry significant value, usually due to their online brand-building potential, use in advertising, search engine optimization, and many other criteria. Because Domain names are registered, it provides authoritative identification of the legal entity. The URI can be in URN or URL format.

The transaction used to send required information to the MERS eRegistry to report that an eNote has been originated with the MERS eRegistry language. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

An entity approved by an Issuing Authority to assist Digital Certificate applicants in applying for certificates, and to approve or reject certificate applications, revoke certificates, or renew certificates. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
The transaction used to reverse an eNote Registration that was registered on the MERS eRegistry. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org

A file, database, digital signature process or other electronic method for tracking information concerning use, access to and alteration of electronic records, including tracking the transfer of ownership of promissory notes and servicing among note holders and servicers, which is logically associated with the related electronic records.
A statistical method to analyze relationships between two variables and model future relationships.
Federal Reserve regulation prohibiting discrimination against consumer credit applicants, and establishing guidelines for collecting and evaluating credit information.
Regulation written by the Federal Reserve Board to implement the Truth-in-Lending Act, requiring full written disclosure of the credit portion of a purchase, including the annual percentage rate.

terms.term: Regulation Z Excluded Bona Fide Discount Points Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that excluded bona fide discount points were charged for this loan.

terms.term: Regulation Z Excluded Bona Fide Discount Points Percent
terms.definition: The bona fide discount points, expressed as a percent, that are excluded from points and fees calculated in accordance with Regulation Z, Truth in Lending.

terms.term: Regulation Z High Cost Loan Disclosure Delivery Date
terms.definition: The date the Regulation Z (Section 32) High Cost Disclosure was delivered to the borrower.

terms.term: Regulation Z High Cost Loan Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the loan is determined to be high cost under Regulation Z.

terms.term: Regulation Z Points And Fees Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that item is included in the Regulation Z Points and Fees calculation.

terms.term: Regulation Z Total Affiliate Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of fees, expressed in dollars, paid to an affiliate(s) of the creditor.
The total loan amount, expressed in dollars, calculated in accordance with Regulation Z, Truth in Lending. This amount is used in calculations for both Qualified Mortgage and HOEPA.

terms.term: Regulation Z Total Points And Fees Amount
terms.definition: The total amount of points and fees, expressed in dollars, calculated in accordance with Regulation Z, Truth in Lending. This amount is used in calculations for both Qualified Mortgage and HOEPA purposes.

terms.term: Regulation Z Total Points And Fees Percent
terms.definition: The total amount of points and fees, expressed as a percent of the Total Loan Amount, calculated in accordance with Regulation Z, Truth in Lending. This percent is used in calculations for both Qualified Mortgage and HOEPA purposes.
An arm of the state or federal government that has the responsibility to license, pass laws, regulate, audit and monitor industry related issues (i.e., NAIC, FHLBB, HUD).

Identification of the lender funding the loan. The identification is as follows: FDIC-insured lenders indicate their FDIC Insurance Certificate Number; Federally-insured credit unions indicate their charter/insurance number; Farm Credit institutions indicate their UNINUM number. Other lenders who fund loans sold to or securitized by FNMA or FHLMC enter FNMA or FHLMC seller/servicer number.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the regulatory agency.
A free-form text field used to describe the amenity if Other is selected as the Regulatory Agency Type.
Contains disclaimer text associated with the product.
Indicates which information about the borrowers in the file matched the regulatory database information.

terms.term: Regulatory Product Match Type Other Description
terms.definition: Contains the regulatory status when the Regulatory Product Status is "Other".
Either the branded name or description of the product provider of the regulatory product.
Indicates the result of the current product request.

terms.term: Regulatory Product Result Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: Contains the regulatory status when the Regulatory Product Status Type is "Other".
Contains text information result associated with the product.
Identifies the regulatory product provided by the federal government. These products are used to screen borrower names to see if they match any names listed in the regulatory product.

terms.term: Regulatory Product Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: Contains the text description of the product when the Regulatory Product Source Type is "Other".

The process of reconstructing or improving property which is in the state of disrepair, and bring it back to its full potential or use. A mortgage for such purpose would be referred to as a rehab mortgage.
The date the rehabilitation should be completed (six months from 203K authorization date as specified on FHA 203K worksheet).
Percentage of loan amount that has been designated as a reserve to cover possible overages in repair costs. Applies to 203K and HomeStyle loans.
The estimated value of the property when rehabilitation is complete.
Total amount of rehabilitation funds included in the loan.
The dollar amount of fees that will be reimbursed to the servicer by the investor, including notary fees, property valuation, and other required fees.

An area of machine learning that focuses on how an intelligent agent should take actions in a dynamic environment to maximize some notion of cumulative reward. It is one of the three basic machine-learning paradigms, along with supervised learning and unsupervised learning. In RL, an agent learns to make decisions by trial and error, interacting with its environment without the need for labeled input/output pairs. The agent’s goal is to find a balance between exploring new actions and exploiting known actions that yield high rewards. This process involves learning a policy that maps states of the environment to the actions that the agent should take.
The curing of all loan defaults by a borrower to return it to current status.

The practice of one insurance company (the reinsure) accepting risks or business from another insurer (the ceding company). It allows insurers to maintain a larger spread of risk and avoid large catastrophes.
Organizations are defined as "Related Entities" if: 1. One directly or indirectly controls or is controlled by the other, or 2. One is under direct or indirect common control with the other.
Identifier of a loan from a related or original transaction. May be used for modifications and conversion of existing loans.
Specifies the investor of the associated loan.

terms.term: Related Loan Investor Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Related Loan investor Type.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies a type of real property ownership by one or more parties. This defines the rights of the parties to occupy, sell their interest in the property to others, to will the property, or to sever joint ownership of the property.
The description of the Relationship Vesting Type when Other is selected as the option from the enumerated list.
The discharging of secured property from a lien.
A stipulation in a blanket encumbrance, mortgage or deed of trust under which a portion of the security may be released from lien if certain amounts are paid or conditions are met.
Notes associated with a release/publication of a Standard that identifies variances or information related to the release.
An agreement by a lender to terminate personal obligation of a mortgagor in connection with payment of a debt.
When true, indicates the property seller has been released from liability for the assumed loan.
An instrument discharging secured property from a lien.
The act of recording a release deed or satisfaction of a mortgage.
The amount of compensation, either partial or full, needed for a mortgagee to remove a lien.
Describes terms and conditions of the relocation package.

Establishes the terms between a relocation company and an employee to purchase a home based on the appraised value. It describes what happens if a home does not sell within a certain period (usually 60 or 90 days), and the circumstances in which a relocation company will buy a home.
Indicates if the loan is part of a corporate relocation program.
One of three major parties involved with SISAC, the relying parties trust in the credentials to approve and process business transactions using electronic signatures.
An individual entitled to the remainder of an estate.
Current remaining buydown balance.

terms.term: Remaining Buydown Balance Amount Total Amount
terms.definition: Provides an arithmetic total of the Remaining Buydown Balance Amount data items within the Loan container in this data set.

terms.term: Remaining Economic Life Range High Years Count
terms.definition: High end of the range of the estimated remaining economic life.

terms.term: Remaining Economic Life Range Low Years Count
terms.definition: Low end of the range of the estimated remaining economic life.
The amount of the remaining partial claim balance after applying the most recent payment supplement amount from the partial claim subsidy account.
The remaining amount of interest scheduled to be paid on a rule of 78s loan.
The process by which contaminants are removed from a building or site.
The means by which a right is enforced or the violation of a right is prevented, redressed or compensated.

A document provided to the remitter for cash received related to the Single Family Property Disposition Program (Section 204(g)) that shows the remittance amount, case number and the date that the collection took place. HUD-235.1 (4/89).
The description of the remittance policy product being reported.
The date that the title insurance policy coverage begins or becomes effective for the remittance record.

This is typically referred to as the Policy Number associated with the policy which is also referred to as the Jacket Number. This number is in two parts this data element is for the Prefix part of that number which is commonly used as the form identification (ex. OP - Owner's Policy, MP - Mortgage Policy, etc.).

This is typically referred to as the Policy Number associated with the policy which is also referred to as the Jacket Number. This number is in two parts this data element is for the Suffix part of that number which is commonly used as the serial number / unique identifier to that policy.

Remittance record transaction code is the code used in calculation to further qualify the rate being used in the calculation. The party assigning the code can be provided using the CodeOwnerURI associated with a MISMOCode.
A description of the remittance record transaction code.
Specifies a type of remittance record.
A free-form text field used to describe the remittance record type if Other is selected as the Remittance Record Type.
A report detailing the respective funds sent to the lender.
The dollar amount of the policy coverage for the referenced remittance record if there is coverage (e.g. Loan Amount for loan policy, sales price for owner's policy, none for Endorsements).
Remote notarization of paper documents via audio-video communication platform (Skype, Facetime, etc.)
When true, indicates the lender will permit the loan closing to leverage remote or remote online notarization of the signatures as part of the closing event.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains specific directions around the remote or remote online notarization of the signature requirements to meet the lender's expectations.

A Notarial Act performed by means of an electronic device or process that allows one or more Principals, who are not in the same physical location as the notary public, to complete a Notarial act and communicate with each other via a real-time online audio/video connection.
Remote online notarization of electronic documents with use of multi-factor authentication.
When true, indicates an online notarial act was performed between a notary public and a principal using audio-visual technology instead of being physically present.
The entity that owns or operates the Remote Online Notarization System, or is contracted with or through to provide access to the Remote Online Notarization System. AKA RON Provider.
The technology solution used to facilitate the Remote Online Notarization.
When true, indicates a request to remove a loan from a prior servicing transfer request.
When true, indicates that the property has renewable energy component(s).
When true, indicates that the renewable energy component is subject to a financing arrangement.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that identifies the type of ownership for the renewable energy component.

terms.term: Renewable Energy Component Ownership Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Renewable Energy Component Ownership Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of renewable energy component present on the site.

terms.term: Renewable Energy Component Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Renewable Energy Component Type.
When true, indicates that all or part of the subject loan proceeds will be used to finance the renovation of an existing property.
The dollar amount of the sales price adjustment.
A free-form text field used to describe a property feature which is being used during the application of the Rent Schedule Comparison approach to estimate the market rent.

Specifies the type of rent adjustment that is made when using the Rent Schedule Comparison approach to estimate the market rent of a property. Each type corresponds to a property feature that may affect the market rent.
A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Rent Adjustment Type.
Legal limitation of rent increases.
Description of the existing or proposed rent controls for a property.
Specifies the existence or likelihood of rent controls such as controls on businesses and apartment complexes.
Specifies the type of utility that is included in the monthly rent.

terms.term: Rent Includes Utility Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Rent Includes Utility Type.

terms.term: Rent Per Gross Building Area Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of the rent per square foot of gross living area determined by dividing the Gross Monthly Rent by the Gross Building Area of the property.
A list of tenants leasing a property, which details terms of lease, area leased and the amount of rent being paid.
When true, indicates a rent schedule will be included in the appraisal report.
The dollar value of the total adjustments made to a comparable rental during the application of a Rent Schedule Comparison in the process of determining the monthly market rent of the comparable.
The percentage of the gross rent adjustments (i.e. sum of the absolute adjustment values) to the Expense Adjusted Monthly Rent of a comparable rental property.
The percentage of the net rent adjustments to the Expense Adjusted Monthly Rent of a comparable rental property.
Indicates whether the total market rent adjustments made to a comparable property during the application of the Rent Schedule Comparison were positive.
The period after construction that a rental property requires to achieve projected stabilized income and occupancy levels.
The area of a property, measured in square feet, upon which rent can be collected.

terms.term: Rental Actual Additional Monthly Income Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of additional monthly income derived as a result of renting property.

terms.term: Rental Actual Gross Monthly Rent Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of the gross monthly rental income derived from a single rental unit or property.

terms.term: Rental Actual Total Monthly Income Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of the total monthly income including rental and other supplemental income.

Establishes the rights and duties of the landlord and tenant in a rental transaction. At a minimum identifies the parties, the property, the term of the rental, and the amount of rent for the term. AKA: Lease Agreement.
A clause in a mortgage commitment requiring a minimum occupancy level in a project before the full amount of the mortgage is advanced.
A landlord's agreement to forego part of the advertised rent in an effort to attract tenants.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on the lease schedule of a rental property or unit.

terms.term: Rental Estimated Additional Monthly Income Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of estimated additional monthly income derived as a result of renting property.

terms.term: Rental Estimated Gross Monthly Rent Amount
terms.definition: The amount of the estimated gross monthly rental income derived from a single rental unit or property.

terms.term: Rental Estimated Net Monthly Rent Amount
terms.definition: The amount of the estimated net monthly rental income derived from a single rental unit or property.

terms.term: Rental Estimated Total Monthly Income Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of the total estimated market income including estimated market rental and supplemental income.
A free-form text field used to describe or comment on a particular feature used in determining the estimated market rent of rental unit or property.
Specifies a feature of a rental unit or property used in determining the estimated market rent of that unit or property.
A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for Rental Feature Type.

A provision in a takeout commitment that requires that only a portion of permanent financing be funded on completion of construction, with the balance held back until specified occupancy levels or cash flow figures are met.

Evaluates the rental potential of a property and establishes its value. AKA: Operating Income Statement, FHLMC 998, FNMA 216, One to Four Family Investment Property and Two to Four Owner Occupied Property.

A form of property insurance that pays the owner of a building (or other designated loss payee) for the amount of rent lost due to damage from an insured peril. Also known as "loss of rents coverage."
The dollar amount paid monthly for utilities associated with a rental property or unit.
The adjusted total amount of the rent after accounting for overall differences between the comparable and the subject.

terms.term: Rental Unit To Subject Comparison Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the overall rating of the differences between the comparable and the subject.
Real Estate Owned
Identifies the party responsible for marketing the property in case of default.

terms.term: REO Marketing Party Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for REO Marketing Party Type.
An unstructured name that identifies the person or entity that estimated the repair.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that identifies the provider of a repair estimate.

terms.term: Repair Estimate Provider Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for RepairEstimateProviderType.
The dollar amount added to the repair set aside total for administration of the required repairs.
The dollar amount of the cost to perform a particular repair on the subject property.
A free-form text field describing a particular repair to be performed on the subject property.
A portion of 100 that represents the percentage by which repair item costs are multiplied to calculate the dollar amount set aside for repairs in a reverse mortgage.
The total dollar amount set aside for each repair item in a reverse mortgage property.
A free-form text field describing the repairs to be performed on the subject property.
The dollar amount of the total cost of the repairs to be performed on the subject property.
The cost of repairs required to bring the property to good and habitable condition as a percentage of the property's estimated market value.

An agreement between a servicer and a borrower in which the servicer agrees not to exercise its legal right to foreclose and the borrower agrees to a payment plan that will, over a certain time period, bring the borrower current on the loan.
The initial lump sum amount paid prior to the first monthly payment for the Repayment Plan.
The scheduled end date of the repayment plan.
The maximum length in months for the repayment plan.
The Repayment Plan monthly payment amount. The amount of repayment scheduled to be paid each month under the Repayment Plan.
The date on which the next payment in the repayment plan is due.
The percent of the contractual payment which the Repayment Plan Scheduled Payment Amount may not exceed.
The dollar amount that the borrower would pay to satisfy the existing delinquency when using the Repayment Plan Maximum Months Count.
The date on which the repayment plan begins.
The duration in months of a repayment plan agreement established with the borrower.
The cost to replace a structure with one of equivalent value and function, but not necessarily identical in design or materials.
An insurance endorsement used with a policy to insure that coverage is on a replacement cost basis.
When true, indicates the note specifies that there is an option to replace the index on the loan when the original index is no longer available.
The estimated dollar amount to reproduce or replace a given area associated with this improvement.

terms.term: Replacement Or Reproduction Cost Area Measure
terms.definition: A measurement that specifies the area of the identified item being replaced or reproduced. The applicable unit of measurement is specified by the Area Unit Of Measure Type.

terms.term: Replacement Or Reproduction Cost Area Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the area, associated with this improvement, whose costs to reproduce or replace are being estimated.

terms.term: Replacement Or Reproduction Cost Area Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Replacement Or Reproduction Cost Area Type.
A cash reserve for the replacement of fixed assets.
See REPURCHASE AGREEMENT.
The process of generating and submitting IRS 1098 forms due to a taxable event to the borrower occurring as a part of the liquidation process.

terms.term: Report Of Home Loan Processed On Automatic Basis (VA Form 26-1820)
terms.definition: A form used instead of the certificate of loan disbursement (VA Form 26-1826) when the mortgagee has processed and closed the loan under the VA Direct program.
The process of reporting loan payment status and payoffs to the credit bureaus.
The process in which the Lender uses VA Form 26-1820 to report the closing of the loan to the VA, and obtains a Loan Guaranty Certificate (LGC).
A generic placeholder for a value to be associated with a reporting and/or billing description for the Receiving Party to utilize for a transaction exchange.
A generic placeholder to add reporting and/or billing descriptions for the Receiving Party to utilize in transactions.
The end date of the period of time the report covers.
The start date of the period of time the report covers.
The year for the reporting period.
An entity that makes assurances and assumes liability for the accuracy of the loan details in the Private Placement Memorandum or Offering Memorandum.
The party that the attorney represents.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Represented Party Type.

The money required to reproduce a building using the same or equivalent materials, design and construction methods, less an allowance for depreciation. An element of the cost-approach method of appraisal.
An agreement between a buyer and seller of securities whereby the seller agrees to buy back the securities at a specified future date and price.
The dollar amount paid to repurchase the loan.
When true, indicates that the appropriate party has received a demand to repurchase or replace the subject loan for breach of representations and warranties.
The date associated with the Repurchase Demand Status Type.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the current status of the repurchase or replacement demand.

terms.term: Repurchase Demand Status Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Repurchase Demand Status Type.
The process of re-purchasing beneficial or servicing rights from a subsequent servicer or investor due to breach of representations and warranties or loan delinquency.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the reason for the repurchase or replacement.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Repurchase Reason Type.
An unstructured name that identifies the party who was requested to repurchase or replace the loan.
A unique identifier assigned to a batch of loans for a request submission.
A system generated date and time stamp enclosed within each request to identify the initiation time of the request.

terms.term: Request For Agreement Of Short Sale
terms.definition: A contract between a buyer and seller (borrower) has been reached and the borrower is requesting approval from the servicer for the short sale prior to the execution of the sales agreement. (Also known as: RASS).

terms.term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return
terms.definition: Authorizes taxing authority (such as IRS) to provide certified copy of borrowers tax return

terms.term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return: IRS 4506
terms.definition: Request for Copy of Tax Return

terms.term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return: IRS 4506T
terms.definition: Request for Transcript of Tax Return

terms.term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return: IRS 4506TEZ
terms.definition: Short Form Request for Individual Tax Return Transcript. IRS Form 4506T-EZ Rev. January 2012.

terms.term: Request For Determination Of Eligibility And Available Loan Guaranty Entitlement (VA Form 26-1880)
terms.definition: The form used to request a certificate of eligibility. It is forwarded to the local VA office with proof of the veteran's military service.

terms.term: Request For Determination Of Reasonable Value Of Real Estate (VA Form 26-1805)
terms.definition: The basic application to VA, requesting appraisal of the property and determination of its eligibility for guaranty.
Establishes a requirement for a senior lien holder to inform a junior lien holder in the event of a default on the common property. Required to be recorded. AKA: Notice of Default.
When true, indicates that the party has requested not to be contacted by this electronic method.

terms.term: Request Payoff Quote for Existing Loan
terms.definition: The process of requesting the amount to satisfy an existing mortgage as of a specified date.

Process in which a party, authorized by a taxpayer, submits a paper or electronic request to the IRS for a Tax Return Transcript that is used for Tax Return Verification (TRV). The request includes the signed copy of the IRS Form 4506-C or other form as required by IRS that authorizes the request. The response includes data from the Borrower's tax return.

Process of requesting confirmation from the US Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) of the Borrower's Loan Eligibility and Entitlement for active-duty service members, veterans, reservists, national guard and surviving spouses of veterans.

The process in which the Lender requests the VA Certificate of Commitment, also referred to as the VA Report and Certification of Loan Disbursement (VA Form 26-1820) for loans that require prior approval from the VA.
The name of the end user requesting the service.
The requested date for when the loan will be closed with the borrower.
The requested time on the requested date for when the loan will be closed with the borrower.
A unique alphanumeric string identifying the document to be prepared.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that identifies the version of the Uniform Residential Loan Application (URLA) specified in a document request.

terms.term: Requested URLA Version Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for URLA Version Type.
The identification code of the requesting party for the branch number associated with the loan.
Identifies the ordering of multiple requesting parties.

Indicates whether a deposit balance is required to be maintained at an account at the lending institution as a condition of the loan. This does not affect the Annual Percentage Rate or any fees. This is disclosed on the TIL Disclosure document.
When true, indicates a required Provider of Service is associated with this fee or payment.

The number of authorized representatives required to sign documents on behalf of the legal entity. To be used in conjunction with Signatory Role Type. If the rule varies per document, this information must be provided under DOCUMENT/DEAL_SETS.
When true, indicates that the loan closing transaction has a period of time in which the transaction can be cancelled.
The cancellation of a transaction or contract by law or by mutual consent.
The last date that borrowers have to cancel a mortgage transaction. Normally applies to second mortgages and refinances. Usually three business days following closing or document execution date.
Funded or non-funded accounts set up at either the property or portfolio level in anticipation of periodic or non-periodic capital expenditures or cash needs.
Focused on real estate finance transactions related to the origination, sale, and servicing of one-to-four unit single family dwellings.
A portion of 100 that represents the residential use of the property.
A procedure used in underwriting residential loans that evaluates the adequacy of an applicant's monthly income after the proposed housing expense has been deducted.
A worksheet showing the calculation of residual income.
Excess income generated by the underlying mortgage collateral of certain mortgage-backed securities, which is not needed to meet contractual obligations to security holders.
A letter sent to a consumer detailing the investigation and resolution of a complaint or inquiry.

A government agency responsible for managing and resolving the affairs of insolvent savings and loan associations placed into receivership by the FDIC. This includes the liquidation, operation and sale of thrift institutions and thrift assets.
Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the version of RESPA regulation under which the loan was originated.

terms.term: RESPA Conforming Year Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for the RESPA Conforming Year Type.
Process in which the Lender responds to requests for loan origination data from state or federal regulators.
The identifier created and used by the responding party to track a transaction or associated interactions.
A unique identifier assigned to a batch of loans for a response.

An approach to developing, assessing, and deploying artificial intelligence systems in a safe, trustworthy, legal, and ethical way. The principles of Responsible Artificial Intelligence include fairness, transparency, privacy, security, inclusive collaboration, and accountability. Responsible AI is used to guide the design, development, deployment, and use of AI to build trust in AI solutions.

The dollar amount of funds available in an escrow account that is set aside for customary and industry-accepted purposes (e.g., insurance proceeds, construction draws, etc.) and can only be accessed once established requirements are met.

terms.term: Restricted Escrow Balance Amount Total Amount
terms.definition: Provides an arithmetic total of the Restricted Escrow Balance Amount data items within the Loan container in this data set.
A free-form text field describing the restriction and/or its impact on the value and marketability of the property.
A type of restriction that could impact the value or use of the property.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Restriction Type.
A clause in a deed or lease that denies the buyer or lessor full rights to the property in question.
A loan for which the basic terms, such as interest rate, maturity date, collateral or guaranty, have been modified as a result of actual or anticipated delinquency. Also known as a "workout."
When true, indicates that one or more liabilities on the subject property will be re-subordinated to the subject loan at closing.
The amount of payments withheld from contractors or subcontractors per contractual agreement to ensure final and satisfactory completion of a job.
Evidences transactions recorded and account balances for a restricted individual investment account during a specified period.
A planned community for those of retirement age, providing attractively sized and priced dwelling units, and offering construction features, amenities and locations for aging residents.

An artificial intelligence framework for improving the quality of LLM-generated responses by grounding the model on external sources of knowledge to supplement the LLM’s internal representation of information.
The percentage of profit returned in relation to the original capital invested in a project. Equity divided by cash flow.
The ratio of cash flow to the equity investment.
The refund of an unearned advance premium resulting from cancellation of a hazard insurance policy prior to its expiration.
When true, indicates the user requested a traditional tax return as originally filed with the IRS for 1040s, 1065s, and 1120s. Used on the IRS Form 4506T and 4506-C.
A mortgage which uses present equity in the property to fund monthly payments from the lender to the borrower in lieu of the borrower receiving the proceeds of the loan in a lump sum.
A portion of 100 that represents the financial index, expressed as a percent, used in conjunction with the margin, to set the expected rate used to calculate the principal limit.

terms.term: Reverse Expected Rate Index Source Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type and source of index to be used, in conjunction with the margin, to set the expected rate used to calculate the principal limit.

terms.term: Reverse Expected Rate Index Source Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for the ReverseExpectedRateIndexSourceType.
The date the expected rate and margin are locked for principal limit calculations.

terms.term: Reverse Expected Rate Lock Expiration Date
terms.definition: The date that the original expected rate lock expires.

terms.term: Reverse Expected Rate Lock Extension Date
terms.definition: The date that the expected rate lock was extended.

terms.term: Reverse Expected Rate Lock Extension Expiration Date
terms.definition: The date that the extended expected rate lock expires.
A portion of 100 that represents the expected value rate, expressed as a percent, used to calculate the principal limit.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Cash Flow Total Expenses Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of all recurring expenses incurred by the borrower(s), as evaluated during the financial assessment for a reverse mortgage.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Cash Flow Total Income Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of income evaluated for the borrower(s) as part of the financial assessment in a reverse mortgage loan. This amount is an aggregate of all income streams used to determine borrower eligibility.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Compensating Factor Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information that may mitigate financial risk in a reverse mortgage transaction.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Extenuating Circumstance Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form alphanumeric string which contains additional information about the extenuating circumstances associated with a reverse mortgage financial assessment.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Extenuating Circumstance Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of extenuating financial circumstances impacting qualification for a reverse mortgage.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Extenuating Circumstance Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for ReverseFinancialAssessmentCircumstanceType.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of failure encountered during the reverse mortgage financial assessment process.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Fail Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for ReverseFinancialAssessmentFailType.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Final Analysis Commentary Description
terms.definition: A free-form description used to collect the final analytical considerations and judgments made during the financial reconciliation assessment for a reverse mortgage.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Final Analysis Result Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the final assessment result of the financial reconciliation analysis performed for a reverse mortgage loan application. This data point is used to determine the applicant's financial capability to meet the loan obligations.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Final Analysis Result Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for ReverseFinancialAssessmentFinalAnalysisResultType.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Residual Income Results Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the reverse mortgage residual income results completed as part of the financial assessment.

terms.term: Reverse Financial Assessment Residual Income Results Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for ReverseFinancialAssessmentResidualIncomeResultsType.

terms.term: Reverse Gross Line Of Credit Reserve Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the gross line of credit including remaining set asides.
The total dollar amount that can be distributed or drawn from a reverse mortgage during the initial disbursement limit period.

terms.term: Reverse Initial Disbursement Limit Months Count
terms.definition: The total number of months of the initial disbursement limit period.
The dollar amount of the present value of the total loan proceeds that is the maximum amount of principal as determined at closing.
The maximum dollar amount of home value that can be used to calculate the principal limit on the reverse mortgage.

terms.term: Reverse Line Of Credit Initial Growth Percent
terms.definition: A portion of 100 that represents the initial annual growth percentage for the line of credit.

terms.term: Reverse Line Of Credit Initial Growth Term Months Count
terms.definition: The total number of months during which the line of credit will increase.

terms.term: Reverse Line Of Credit Initial Total Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount established as a line of credit at closing.

terms.term: Reverse Line Of Credit Limit Period Available Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount available during the disbursement limit period of the reverse mortgage loan product.

terms.term: Reverse Line Of Credit Term Months Count
terms.definition: The total number of months the line of credit is available.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains the name of the reverse loan product.

The dollar amount of fees and/or charges incurred in connection with the origination of the reverse mortgage that are requirements for loan approval and which will be paid at closing or during a pre-defined period.
The dollar amount of home value used to calculate the principal limit on the reverse mortgage.
The dollar amount of mortgage insurance premium paid at closing for the reverse mortgage loan being refinanced.
The dollar amount of the monthly payment the borrower will receive after the initial disbursement limit period.

terms.term: Reverse Monthly Payment Initial Disbursement Limit Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the monthly payment the borrower will receive during the initial disbursement limit period.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the duration of the monthly payments for the loan.
The dollar amount of the principal limit reserved for the monthly payments.

terms.term: Reverse Monthly Payment Term Months Count
terms.definition: The total number of months the lender is obligated to send payments to the borrower.
The dollar amount of the service fee that will be charged monthly to the borrower during the life of the loan.

terms.term: Reverse Mortgage Disclosed Monthly Servicing Fee Amount
terms.definition: The disclosed amount of monthly servicing fees on the reverse mortgage.
When true, indicates the loan program uses present equity in the property to fund scheduled payments, a line of credit, and/or a lump sum from the lender to the borrower.
The total amount of the initial payment paid to the borrower upon close of a reverse mortgage, including the initial lump sum advance and any lien payoffs.

terms.term: Reverse Mortgage Obtained After Housing Counseling Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that a household obtained a reverse mortgage after receiving housing counseling services.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the type of reverse mortgage loan being refinanced.

terms.term: Reverse Mortgage Refinance Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for ReverseMortgageRefinanceType.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information in conjunction with Reverse Mortgage Reporting Action Types.
The reporting system status of the reverse mortgage as reported to the investor.

terms.term: Reverse Mortgage Reporting Action Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Reverse Mortgage Reporting Action Type.

terms.term: Reverse Net Line Of Credit Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the remaining line of credit as of the current reporting period for a reverse mortgage.
The dollar amount of the net principal limit as of the current reporting period for a reverse mortgage.
Specifies the manner in which loan proceeds are paid out to the borrower.

terms.term: Reverse Payment Plan Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the Reverse Payment Plan Type.
The term expressed in months over which the borrower is to receive payments in a reverse mortgage.
The date of closing for the reverse mortgage loan being refinanced.

terms.term: Reverse Previous Current Principal Limit Amount
terms.definition: The dollar value of the current principal limit amount of the reverse mortgage loan being refinanced.
The dollar value of the maximum claim amount of the reverse mortgage loan being refinanced.

terms.term: Reverse Property Charge Set Aside Additional Description
terms.definition: A free-form alphanumeric string which contains an additional description for the property set aside coverage.

terms.term: Reverse Property Charge Set Aside First Year Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the total property charge set aside available for disbursement in the first year.

terms.term: Reverse Property Charge Set Aside Required Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates the property set aside charge is required.

terms.term: Reverse Property Charge Set Aside Total Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount calculated for all property charge set asides, including the first year amount, based on applicable policies (e.g. HUD, private industry, etc.).

terms.term: Reverse Property Charge Set Aside Type
terms.definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the funding type for the reverse mortgage property charge set aside amounts.

terms.term: Reverse Property Charge Set Aside Type Other Description
terms.definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when 'Other' is selected for ReversePropertyChargeSetAsideType.

terms.term: Reverse Repair Set Aside Total Amount
terms.definition: The total dollar amount of the principal limit set aside to fund the required repairs on the reverse mortgage.
An agreement to purchase mortgage-backed securities from a party with a simultaneous agreement to resell them at a specified future date and price.
The scheduled payment amount that was determined by the borrower at origination or after a change of the payment plan.

terms.term: Reverse Service Fee Set Aside Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount of the principal limit set aside to fund the monthly service fee on the reverse mortgage.

terms.term: Reverse Set Aside First Year Property Charges Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount that is set aside to cover property expenses during the first year of the loan.

terms.term: Reverse Set Aside Taxes And Insurance Withholding Amount
terms.definition: The dollar amount to be subtracted from the scheduled payment and placed in a tax and insurance set aside.

terms.term: Reverse Set Aside Taxes And Insurance Withholding End Date
terms.definition: The date selected by the borrower to end withholding the tax and insurance set aside.

terms.term: Reverse Set Aside Taxes And Insurance Withholding Rate Percent
terms.definition: The percentage of the scheduled payment amount to be subtracted and placed in the tax and insurance set aside.

terms.term: Reverse Set Aside Taxes And Insurance Withholding Start Date
terms.definition: The date selected by the borrower to begin withholding the tax and insurance set aside.
The total amount available to the borrower under a specific reverse mortgage plan.
A right to future possession retained by an owner at the time of a transfer of an owner's interest in real property.
The estimated value of a property at a specified future date.
A clause providing that any violations of restrictions will cause title to the property to revert to the party who imposed the restrictions.
Name of the company the Review Appraiser is associated with.
Process of ensuring the Closing Protection Letter is on record and covers the loan transaction.
The process in which conventional mortgage options are reviewed for applicability.

Process of auditing and reconciling the document package data and the loan origination system (LOS) data to ensure the data integrity of the LOS. Provides additional validation that the loan was closed and underwritten correctly.

Process of reviewing the subject property characteristics, loan underwriting requirements, and preliminary title report to determine if proper endorsements have been requested and fees disclosed as required for the loan closing.

Process of confirming receipt of the executed closing documents package and performing a review to confirm that all documents are accurately signed and completed, and that all necessary closing conditions were met by the Settlement Agent.
The process in which Farmer Mac Farm and Ranch loan options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which FHA mortgage options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) product options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which Home Equity Loan (HELOAN) product options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which home equity product options, which include a Home Equity Loan (HELOAN) or Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC), are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which loan product options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which other mortgage options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which reverse mortgage options, which could include an FHA HECM or a proprietary loan program, are reviewed for applicability.

terms.term: Review Seller CD Form and Data
terms.definition: Process of receiving, reviewing, and reconciling the Seller Closing Disclosure (CD) to confirm the seller data aligns with the Borrower CD data. This process is applicable to purchase transactions.

Process of reviewing the details of the upcoming loan closing to determine if additional steps are required, such as obtaining a Power of Attorney, Quit Claim Deed, LLC approvals, Trust, Non-Borrower Spouse, Removing Vesting, or additional Attorney reviews.
Process of reviewing the real estate tax certification, as provided by the Settlement Agent and/or Title Agent, to confirm taxes required to be collected during the loan closing.
Process of reviewing detailed information from external resources to verify loan data during the loan origination process.
Process of analyzing the Title Commitment, also known as the Preliminary Title Report

terms.term: Review Title Errors and Omissions Insurance
terms.definition: Process of analyzing the Errors and Omissions insurance associated with individuals or organizations responsible for Title and Settlement.
The process in which USDA mortgage options are reviewed for applicability.
The process in which VA mortgage options are reviewed for applicability.
Process of reviewing and verifying the wire instructions are accurate and to ensure that the wired funds will be sent to the correct financial institution and bank account for settlement.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that categorizes the appraisal report section in which a revision is being made.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Revision Category Type.
The date when the revision was made to the appraisal report.
A free-form alphanumeric string which contains information about the revision made to the appraisal report.
Borrowed money on an open line of credit. Open lines of credit are subject to variable payments in accordance with the balance. Credit cards are examples of revolving debt.
A pool of money set up to make loans. The pool is replenished through borrower paybacks.
In secondary marketing, a situation in which one securities contract is priced relatively higher than another.
An addendum or amendment to a contract.
A right given a lessee by an owner stating that if the owner decides to sell the leased property, the lessee has the first opportunity to purchase the subject property before it is offered to others.

In some states, a right permitting the mortgagor to reclaim foreclosed property by making full payment of the foreclosure sales price. The right of redemption exists for a specified period of time, called the redemption period.
Period of three full days after closing in which the consumer is allowed to negate an owner occupied refinance transaction.

terms.term: Right Of Rescission Waiting Period Waived Indicator
terms.definition: When true, indicates that due to a bona fide personal financial emergency, the consumer modified or waived the right to rescind waiting period requirement that must be met prior to consummation of the mortgage loan transaction.
The survivor's right to the property of a deceased person. In the case of joint tenancy or tenancy by entirety (husband and wife), the undivided property passes to the survivor.
The right to pass over land owned by another. Also, a strip of land used for a street or railway.

The number of contacts made by the Servicer or the agent of the Servicer in the reporting period with the Borrower, co-Borrower, a representative of the estate or anyone that is legally responsible for representing any of these entities.

When true, indicates that a contact was made with the borrower, co-borrower, trusted advisor, such as a housing counselor, or other authorized party that results in a conversation about resolving the loan delinquency.
Places restrictions upon governmental authorities having access to copies of the financial records of any mortgage applicant.
The right of owners to the water and land within the normal flow of a river or stream, or below a high water mark. These rights vary with state laws.

Informs the borrower that a consumer report is used in connection with providing credit with materially less favorable terms than the most favorable terms available to a substantial proportion of customers.
Generally, the rate of return required to attract capital to a particular investment.
Designates that there was an improvement to the credit grade due to compensating factors.
Rules established by the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS) which dictate how much of certain types of capital a savings and loan may hold.
The relationship between risks of investment and the anticipated rewards for undertaking that risk.
Establishes the parties and their respective responsibilities to jointly maintain a road. AKA: Private Road Maintenance Agreement, Street Road Maintenance Agreement.
A digital platform that leverages artificial intelligence to advise users with very minimal human intervention.

To include the closing costs of a refinance transaction in the balance of the new mortgage, i.e. to finance the closing costs of the refinance so that they are not paid in cash by the borrower, or out of pocket.
The renewal of a loan at maturity. Also, reinvestment of proceeds of a sale of an investment into another, which defers payment of taxes on the gain from the sale.
Remote Online Notarization
An unstructured name that identifies the Remote Online Notarization (RON) platform provider used in a RON transaction.
